A1.dimension: A1 — Recap & Coverage (every user request across the engagement + the 8 live critiques) mapped against the Tranche M plan, with the M.W1 bump+migration execution verified live
A1.verdict:
COVERAGE SUMMARY. The M plan (M.md + design/M-*.md, ordering ξ′) is an exhaustive recap-and-fold of the whole fourier engagement: it honours the recurring meta-directive (deeply-audit / idiomatic-gestalt / fold-ALL-chronics / recap-ALL-prompts / NOT-implementation) at the planning layer and — newly this run — RESOLVES-BY-CONSTRUCTION the §0 deepest chronic (planned-6×-shipped-0×) by declaring M the EXECUTION tranche with a PHYSICAL close-gate. The two twice-planned physical chronics (deploy-of-record 44 behind; inv-15 consumer gap, 7 endpoints/0 callers) are correctly absorbed (W2-W4, W10), J + K-deploy fold into M's close, and the §7 chronic ledger gives every item a terminal verb. So at the RECAP/COVERAGE level M is sound: ~90% of the historical prompt corpus is addressed=yes/partial in a named wave.

THE M.W1 EXECUTION IS REFLECTED but the live critique exposes that it was executed FAITHFULLY-TO-MIGRATION, NOT FAITHFULLY-TO-DESIGN-INTENT, and that is the seam the 8 critiques fall into. The migration doc (M-bump-migration.md) is verified-accurate against the live tree (UnderlineTabs→SegmentedTabs variant="underline" at VisualizationView.vue:182, GalleryView, EquationView; glass-subtle→glass-wash correction pending; MetricBadge/glass-floating/glass-scrubber all booked). But M.W1 was run on the working tree BEFORE M's design waves (W5-W9), so the live instance is "4.0 migrated, design-suffused nowhere" — exactly the half-built-and-quarantined state §1 names. The user critiqued THAT intermediate state.

THE 8-CRITIQUE DISPOSITION (each → covered? / new?):
(1) surfaces-not-glassy → COVERED (M.W5 glass ladder + .cartoon-card DELETE, 15 live sites); β adoption gap; the plan is correct, just unexecuted. Live-confirmed: 01/live-paper/live-workspace are flat opaque paper-stamps.
(2) borders-not-rounded → PARTIAL. M.W5 sweeps raw-radii→--radius-* but does NOT name a single rounding SOURCE (squircle.css ships in glass-ui 4.0, unadopted) — new sub-finding.
(3) no-desktop-tabs / mobile-affordance-leaking → PARTIAL/NEW. Source has lg:hidden (correct) yet live @1440 shows the tabs — a real regression the plan does NOT cover; M.W8 only does asideSide, never asserts desktop-vs-mobile tab gating. NEW finding.
(4) all-controls-LEFT (DEC-2) → COVERED (M.W8 asideSide="left"); β; live-confirmed controls pinned RIGHT over dead dot-grid.
(5) dropdown/glass DARKENED → NEW. Root-caused to glass-ui 4.0's alpha-monotonic ladder (overlay ~0.95α / floating ~0.80α) + adaptive --glass-backdrop tint compositing flat-grey with no bright content behind. α (glass-ui-owned) + β (rung choice). NOT in the M plan. NEW.
(6) buttons-invisible-unhovered → COVERED-BUT-UNDER-SPECIFIED. M books dockiconbutton-active + accent-tone; but 09 shows the preset pills DO have idle paint — the real defect is WASHED contrast (light-on-light), so the fix is the tonal-accent idle FILL contrast floor, not "no idle paint." Refines M.W7/W8.
(7)+(10) tabs-should-be-GLASS → THE HEADLINE GAP. M.W1 treats variant="underline" as the CORRECT migration target; the user REVERSES it to glass. The plan has the design choice BACKWARDS. γ residue + β. NEW/REVERSED.
(8) search-OFFSET+SQUARE → NEW. Live (11) shows a square native blue focus outline offset beyond the rounded field. α (glass-ui input focus-ring) + γ (fourier raw outline). NOT in the M plan. NEW.

NET: 3 critiques fully covered (1,4 + the spirit of 6), 2 partial (2,3), 3 NET-NEW that HARDEN M (5 darkened-menu, 7/10 tab-variant-reversal, 8 search-focus-ring). The single most load-bearing correction: M.W1's underline-tab migration choice must be re-opened as a DESIGN decision (glass variant), not preserved as a faithful 1:1 swap.

findings.title: Tab-variant migration choice is BACKWARDS: M.W1 preserved underline; user wants glass (critiques 7+10)
findings.evidence: user-critique/10-tabs-should-be-glass.png (underline tabs shown), user-critique/01 + live-workspace.jpeg (Controls|Canvas underline); VisualizationView.vue:182 variant="underline"; M-bump-migration.md:31,191 + M.md:77 specify UnderlineTabs→SegmentedTabs variant="underline" as the CORRECT 1:1 migration
findings.current_state: M.W1 faithfully maps the retired UnderlineTabs onto SegmentedTabs variant="underline" to preserve the visual contract — and the plan treats this as DONE-correctly. But the user's critique reverses it: the tabs should be the GLASS (pill / glass-track) variant. The plan nowhere re-opens the variant as a design decision; it is locked as a migration faithful-swap.
findings.proposed: Re-open the tab variant as a M.W8 DESIGN decision rather than a M.W1 migration constant. Adopt SegmentedTabs glass variant (the glass-track/pill register backed by glass-ui 4.0's specular-track) wherever a top-level pane switcher exists (viz mobile bar, gallery filter, equation mode). Source the rung from the glass ladder (BAND-2 chrome → glass-floating track + glass-resting thumb) so the selected tab reads as a lifted glass pill, not a hairline underline. NO !important, NO per-component override — pass the variant prop. Keep underline ONLY where a hairline genuinely suits inline secondary nav (none on the critiqued surfaces). This DELETES the assumption that migration-faithful == design-correct.

findings.title: Darkened/opaque nav dropdown is uncovered: glass-ui 4.0 alpha-monotonic ladder composites flat-grey (critique 5)
findings.evidence: user-critique/08-dropdown-glass-darkened.png (flat opaque grey menu, no translucency); glass-ui dist/styles/glass/ladder.css:11-15 (overlay ~0.95α, floating ~0.80α, adaptive --glass-backdrop tint); the M plan has NO row for a darkened menu/overlay surface
findings.current_state: The nav dropdown renders as flat opaque grey, not translucent glass. Root: glass-ui 4.0's ladder is alpha-monotonic — overlay≈0.95α and floating≈0.80α — and the adaptive-tint color-mix recipe composites to near-flat-grey when there is no bright content behind the menu to refract. The M plan's depth ladder (W5) maps PANELS but never the top-layer overlay/menu surfaces, and books no glass-ui ask for the menu-darkening regression.
findings.proposed: Split into two terminal moves. (β, fourier) M.W5/W8: map the nav dropdown onto the correct rung — a top-layer menu is BAND-2 chrome but should pick glass-floating (~0.80α) with --glass-backdrop tuned to the cream page, NOT overlay (~0.95α), so it stays translucent over the article; and set the menu's tint-source to the route accent so it reads as glass, not grey. (α, glass-ui ASK) book a menu/overlay translucency-floor: a high-α overlay rung over a LIGHT non-refractive backdrop should still resolve to a legible translucent glass via a backdrop-saturation/contrast recipe, not collapse to flat grey — fourier consumes once shipped, NEVER an !important fill. No fourier shim.
findings.wave_hint: M.W5 (rung map) + book glass-ui ask; surfaces on M.W8 menus

findings.title: Search focus ring is square + offset: raw native outline on a rounded glass field (critique 8) — uncovered
findings.evidence: user-critique/11-search-offset-square.png (square blue native outline sitting outside the rounded field corners); M plan W5 sweeps raw-radii but has NO row for the input focus-ring; PaperSearchDropdown.vue (no focus/ring/rounded rules found in grep)
findings.current_state: The paper search input shows the browser-default square blue focus outline, offset beyond the field, on top of a field that is itself rounded — the outline does not follow the corner radius and sits proud of the box. The M plan never names an input focus-ring system; W5's rounding sweep is panel-scoped.
findings.proposed: (α, glass-ui ASK) book a rounded glass focus-ring primitive: glass-ui 4.0 input/search components should emit a radius-matched, inset, accent-tinted focus ring (box-shadow ring honoring the field's --radius, not a square outline:auto) — generalizes to every consumer's text input. (β, fourier) M.W5: adopt the glass input/search component (or compose the field's focus from the glass ladder + --radius-* + the tonal-accent --accent-edge ring) and DELETE the inherited native outline by replacing it with the ring token — never outline:none with no replacement (a11y floor: the ring must remain visible). This folds critique 2's rounding into a single --radius source.
findings.wave_hint: M.W5 (adopt field + ring) + book glass-ui input-focus-ring ask

findings.title: Desktop-vs-mobile tab gating regression not asserted: lg:hidden tabs appear @1440 (critique 3)
findings.evidence: live-workspace.jpeg (Controls|Canvas tabs visible at 1440px) vs VisualizationView.vue:181 class="... lg:hidden" (should hide ≥1024px); M.W8 plans asideSide but never asserts the tab affordance is mobile-only on desktop
findings.current_state: Source correctly gates the mobile tab bar with lg:hidden, yet the live @1440 capture shows it rendered — either the capture viewport fell below lg, or the bump/migration perturbed the breakpoint utility, or the Configurator chassis changed the stage flow so the desktop both-panels layout no longer engages. The M plan covers controls-left (asideSide) but has no row asserting the desktop layout shows both panels with NO tab switcher.
findings.proposed: M.W8: make the desktop/mobile split a single isDesktop-driven structural decision owned by the Configurator chassis, not a Tailwind lg:hidden on a hand-rolled bar. On desktop the asideSide=left rail + stage render together with NO tab affordance; the SegmentedTabs switcher exists ONLY below the container breakpoint (drive via @container, consistent with the density lever in M-design-language.md:229). Add a W11 evidence assertion: @1440 the workspace shows no Controls|Canvas tabs. DELETE the bespoke lg:hidden bar in favor of the chassis's own responsive slotting — no parallel breakpoint logic.

findings.title: Idle-button-paint critique mis-diagnosed by the plan: defect is WASHED contrast, not absent paint (critique 6)
findings.evidence: user-critique/09-buttons-invisible-unhovered.png (preset pills Sawtooth/Triangle/|sin(x)|/Gaussian/Step/x² DO have a faint idle pill, near-invisible on the cream bg); M books glass-ui-dockiconbutton-active + accent-tone (M.md:161, §10)
findings.current_state: The user reads the preset pills as 'not visible when not hovered.' The plan attributes this to no-idle-paint and books dockiconbutton-active. But 09 shows the pills DO render an idle background — it is just so low-contrast (light pill on light cream) that it reads as bare text. The real defect is the idle-fill contrast floor, not a missing fill.
findings.proposed: Sharpen M.W7's accent-tone ask + adoption to a CONTRAST-FLOORED idle fill: the tonal-accent recipe (--accent-fill/--accent-edge/--accent-ink) must clamp the idle pill against the cream substrate via value.js safeAccentColor so the resting state is legibly distinct (≥3:1 against bg) BEFORE hover lifts it. The selected pill (the red x(π−x), the warm Square wave) already proves the system; extend the same floored fill to the unselected idle register. This is the existing accent-tone ask, re-scoped from 'add idle paint' to 'floor idle-fill contrast' — no new ask, a corrected one.

findings.title: No single rounding SOURCE named; squircle.css ships in glass-ui 4.0 unadopted (critique 2)
findings.evidence: user-critique/01 (near-square card corners) + 11 (square ring); glass-ui dist/styles/glass/squircle.css present; M-design-language.md sweeps 'raw radii→--radius-*' (line ~ C2 sweep) but names no canonical radius source
findings.current_state: Cards and fields read as near-square. M.W5 says sweep raw radii to --radius-* but never declares ONE rounding source, and glass-ui 4.0 ships a squircle.css (superellipse corners) that fourier does not consume — so even --radius-* yields a circular-arc corner, not the iOS-26 squircle the glass language implies.
findings.proposed: M.W5: declare ONE rounding axis under inv-33 — the --radius-* token ladder for arc radii, and ADOPT glass-ui 4.0 squircle.css on the glass surfaces that want the continuous-curvature corner (cards, panels, the search field, menu). Map each band to a radius rung (BAND-1 panels → --radius-lg squircle; pills → --radius-full). DELETE every literal rounded-* / border-radius:Npx in the 15 cartoon-card sites as the .cartoon-card shim retires. No per-site magic radii.

findings.title: The cartoon-stamp error/empty cards (the most visible 'not glassy' surface) span error+empty states the W5 plan counts but the critique elevates
findings.evidence: user-critique/01-not-glassy-not-rounded (Computation-failed/Bad-Gateway card — opaque fill, hard offset drop-shadow, square border); VisualizationView.vue:163 'cartoon-card p-6 text-center' error card; grep: 15 web/src cartoon-card sites

glassui_asks.name: glass-ui-menu-translucency-floor
glassui_asks.what: A menu/overlay translucency-floor recipe: a high-α overlay/floating rung rendered over a LIGHT, non-refractive backdrop (no bright content behind to refract) must still resolve to a legible TRANSLUCENT glass via a backdrop-saturation/contrast recipe, instead of collapsing the alpha-monotonic ladder (overlay ~0.95α / floating ~0.80α + adaptive --glass-backdrop tint) to flat opaque grey. Source-grounded in ladder.css:11-15.
glassui_asks.why: fourier's nav dropdown renders flat grey over the cream paper (user-critique/08). Every glass-ui consumer with menus over light/document backgrounds (value.js palette menus, speedtest, words/Floridify) hits the same flat-grey-over-light regression. Belongs in the ladder, not a per-consumer !important fill (inv-16).

glassui_asks.name: glass-ui-input-focus-ring
glassui_asks.what: A rounded, inset, accent-tinted focus-ring primitive for glass-ui input/search/textarea components: a box-shadow ring that honors the field's own --radius (squircle-aware), replacing the browser-default square outline:auto that sits offset beyond a rounded field.
glassui_asks.why: fourier's paper search shows a square native blue outline proud of the rounded field (user-critique/11). Every glass form field across the constellation wants a radius-matched glass focus ring; born in glass-ui, the consumer override is just adopting the field — no fourier-local outline hack, a11y ring stays visible.

glassui_asks.name: glass-ui-dockiconbutton-active
glassui_asks.what: (RE-AFFIRM, already booked §10) an active?:boolean prop on DockIconButton stamping aria-pressed + data-active + a selected visual register — re-scoped per A1-05 to ensure the active/idle registers are CONTRAST-FLOORED against light substrates, not just present.
glassui_asks.why: fourier hand-rolls :class={is-active} at 7 dock sites with no backing paint, and the preset-pill idle state reads as bare text on cream (user-critique/09). The toggle's selected AND idle states must both clear a contrast floor.

glassui_asks.name: glass-ui-accent-tone
glassui_asks.what: (RE-AFFIRM, already booked §10) the contrast-floored 3-channel tonal accent (--accent-fill/--accent-edge/--accent-ink from one --tone, reusing value.js mixing+flooring) — re-scoped per A1-05 so the IDLE fill (not just hover/active) is floored ≥3:1 against the page substrate.
glassui_asks.why: the colour-pop idle register is washed-out on cream (user-critique/09); fourier re-derives this color-mix recipe ~57×. The floor must apply to the resting state, which the current booking implies for active/hover only.

open_questions: Critique 3 (desktop tabs @1440): is the live-workspace.jpeg an artifact of a sub-lg capture viewport, or did the M.W1 migration / Configurator chassis genuinely break the lg:hidden gating? Needs a backend-up @1440 capture to disambiguate (A1-04 / A1-08).

Tab variant (critiques 7+10): the user says 'tabs should be glass' — does this mean the SegmentedTabs glass/pill variant on the TOP-LEVEL pane switchers ONLY, or also the equation-mode and gallery-filter tabs? The M.W1 underline choice should be re-opened across all 3 SegmentedTabs sites, but the scope of 'glass' (pill vs glass-track vs specular) is a user design call for M.W8.

Darkened menu (critique 5): confirm whether the nav dropdown currently picks the overlay (~0.95α) or floating (~0.80α) rung — the source did not surface the component; the rung choice is the β lever and determines how much the glass-ui-menu-translucency-floor ask must carry vs fourier re-mapping the rung.

Should M re-sequence so a thin GLASS-LADDER + MENU/FIELD slice of W5 lands BEFORE the next live capture, so the user is not re-critiquing the bare-migrated intermediate state? The plan runs W1 then the full W5-W9 fan-out; the critique implies the user wants to see the glass suffused sooner.

The 8-critique-regression checklist (A1-07/A1-10): should it be a literal Playwright/axe visual-assertion suite in M.W11, or a manual captured-screenshot gate? The §0 physical-gate discipline argues for the former.

A2.dimension: A2 — root-cause of the 8 live critiques (alpha/beta/gamma classification + idiomatic no-legacy owner+fix)
A2.verdict: All 8 critiques root-cause cleanly to file:line, and the split is 1 alpha (glass-ui 4.0 overlay default over-darkens) + 1 mixed-alpha (input focus ring), 5 beta (fourier adoption gaps), 2 gamma (M.W1 bump residue) — the existing M plan ANTICIPATES 6 of the 8 in W5/W7/W8 but UNDER-SPECIFIES four root mechanisms the live state now exposes: (a) critique-08's darkened dropdown is NOT a fourier surface choice but the glass-ui 4.0 `:where(.glass-floating,.glass-overlay)` UNCONDITIONAL AA warm-ink darken (ladder.css ~L196-205) firing over fourier's KNOWN-light cream backdrop — a glass-ui default that must be tuned at SOURCE (book to BB W-ON-GLASS-FG), never papered over locally; (b) critique-11's offset+square focus ring is a raw `<input>` (PaperSearchInput.vue:37) with no rounded glass focus-within ring — fourier must ADOPT the glass-ui `search`/`Input` primitive, not a CSS patch; (c) critique-03 desktop-tabs-leak is a real `lg:hidden` failure under the vite-8/Tailwind-v4 bump that the plan treats only as layout, not as a bump regression needing vue-tsc-3 + a live breakpoint probe; (d) critique-06 idle-invisible pills root-cause to glass-ui-4.0 `outline` variant painting `bg-background` which COLLIDES with the surrounding cartoon-card `--card` fill — the fix is the tonal-accent idle ladder (W7/W8), not merely "tonal fill" in the abstract. The 8 critiques are the physical, live confirmation that M.W5 (delete .cartoon-card → glass ladder), M.W7 (OKLCH idle pops), and M.W8 (asideSide=left + SegmentedTabs variant + Configurator hierarchy) are the highest-leverage waves. NO !important, NO shim survives any proposed fix; every fix DELETES the offending hand-rolled surface.

findings.title: Not-glassy cartoon-stamp cards: the .cartoon-card @utility shim (25 sites) is the offset-shadow opaque-fill surface the user sees, not the glass ladder
findings.evidence: user-critique/01-not-glassy-not-rounded-tabs-controls.png (the 'Computation failed / Bad Gateway' card: 2px border + offset stamp shadow + opaque fill, square-ish corners); live/live-workspace.jpeg (the right Image panel is a flat opaque stamped card); web/src/style.css:107-111 (@utility cartoon-card { @apply cartoon-surface; border-color: var(--border); background: var(--card); }); web/src/components/visualization/ImageUpload.vue:38 (class='cartoon-card …')
findings.current_state: `.cartoon-card` is a resurrected dead class (glass-ui removed the recipe at C.W5; carried since D.W4). It composes `cartoon-surface` (2px border + offset-stamp box-shadow + hover-lift) over an OPAQUE `--card` fill at 25 application sites across 14 files. There is ZERO adoption of the glass-ui 4.0 five-tier ladder (`grep glass-wash|glass-quiet|glass-resting|glass-floating src/` = 0 hits in app code). Every primary content surface — error cards, the Image panel, equation panels, morph cards — renders as a paper sticker, the exact opposite of the GLASS pillar.
findings.proposed: DELETE the `.cartoon-card` @utility shim outright and map every one of the 25 sites onto the frozen 3-band glass depth ladder: in-flow instrument panels → `.glass-wash` (ambient, ~0.30α) or `.glass-resting` (focused); lifted/anchored chrome → `.glass-floating`; the bare math substrate stays band-0. The error/status card adopts `.glass-resting` with the brand rim; ImageUpload's panel adopts `.glass-wash`. Strip all hand-rolled box-shadow/blur/color-mix glass recipes in the same pass. This is the no-shims directive finally honoured — the deletion and the adoption are one act (inv-3 net-decrease).

findings.title: Borders not rounded: cartoon-surface near-square radius + raw outlines bypass the --radius-* token system
findings.evidence: user-critique/01 (card corners are barely rounded); user-critique/11-search-offset-square.png (the focus ring is fully SQUARE on a rounded field); web/src/style.css:107-111 (.cartoon-card inherits cartoon-surface radius, no --radius-* binding); web/src/components/paper/PaperSearch.vue:52 (border-radius: calc(var(--radius) - 2px)) and :113 (results panel raw radius)
findings.current_state: Rounding is applied ad-hoc: cartoon-surface carries its own small radius; several surfaces hand-roll `calc(var(--radius) - Npx)` or raw `0` (PaperSearch.vue:206-220 floating variant zeroes radius). There is no single `--radius-*` ladder consumed across cards/panels/inputs, so corners read inconsistent and near-square next to glass-ui's `rounded-panel`/`rounded-card` primitives.
findings.proposed: Fold rounding into the M.W5 ladder adoption: every surface inherits its radius from the glass-ui `rounded-panel`/`rounded-card`/`rounded-button` tokens (the same ones DropdownMenuContent already uses). Delete the `calc(var(--radius) - Npx)` hand-rolls and the floating-variant `border-radius: 0`. Sweep raw radii → `--radius-*` as the C2 incongruence sweep already names. No new token invention — consume glass-ui's radius scale.
findings.wave_hint: M.W5 (rounding swept with the ladder; C2 incongruence sweep)

The token re-point rides the SAME oklab inheriting axis glass-ui composes — zero new compositing seam.

The idle paint comes from the route-accent token, never a per-pill hand-rolled color. glassui_asks.name: W-ON-GLASS-FG — overlay-band darken opt-out for a KNOWN-light substrate
glassui_asks.what: The glass-ui 4.0 :where(.glass-floating,.glass-overlay) rule (ladder.css ~L196-205) applies the FULL unconditional AA warm-ink darken (--glass-tint-strength: --glass-tint-strength-aa, ~24%) on the entire overlay band because it 'floats over an unknown surface'. Expose a per-app signal — e.g. honoring an ancestor `--glass-backdrop-known: light` (or an app-root --glass-tint-strength the band reads) — that lets a consumer whose backdrop luminance is KNOWN-light dial the overlay tint to the sub-perceptual FLOOR instead of the full AA darken, preserving true translucency without losing legibility. The token escape exists ('set --glass-tint-strength: 0%') but it is documented as a per-surface override, not a clean app-level known-light declaration co-located with the legibility logic.
glassui_asks.why: fourier's nav DropdownMenu/HoverCard band renders as an opaque warm-grey plate over its known-light cream shell (user critique 08). fourier consumes glass-floating correctly; the over-darken is a glass-ui SOURCE default for the unknown-substrate case. inv-16 forbids fourier writing glass-ui, and the no-!important directive forbids a local workaround — so the durable fix is a source-level known-light opt-out that other light-substrate consumers (slides, words) will also want.

glassui_asks.name: W-ON-GLASS-FG — --input-on-glass focus-ring rung for inputs composed over translucent glass
glassui_asks.what: Provide the sibling `--input-on-glass` focus-ring rung named in BB W-ON-GLASS-FG so a search/Input primitive placed over a glass-floating/glass-wash surface paints a rounded, radius-following focus ring whose contrast target is the COMPOSITED glass fill (not --background). Today the Input focus ring is tuned to --background; over the darkened-translucent overlay band it can read low-contrast or mis-anchored.
glassui_asks.why: fourier's paper search (after it adopts the glass-ui search primitive per A2-08) sits inside a glass surface; without the on-glass focus-ring rung the rounded ring may under-contrast over the composited plate. Booking this to BB closes the focus-ring story at source for every consumer instead of a fourier-local outline patch (forbidden).

A4.dimension: A4 — glass-ui 4.0 rendering regressions (alpha class): critique #5 dropdown darkened + critique #8 search focus-ring square/offset + glass-not-translucent on dark page
A4.verdict: Three distinct alpha-class mechanisms explain critiques #5 and #8. None is a glass-ui regression in the defect sense; two are fourier adoption gaps that interact with glass-ui 4.0's NEW self-engage tint system; one is a genuine fourier-owned bespoke surface that never wired the glass-ui Input/focus-ring primitives. The "darkened dropdown" (critique #5) is glass-ui 4.0's UNCONDITIONAL overlay-band tint self-engage (`.glass-floating { --glass-tint-strength: var(--glass-tint-strength-aa) }`) operating CORRECTLY over fourier's dark-page substrate — the plate darkens toward the warm-ink tint at 12% in dark mode. This is design-intended behaviour; what makes it read as "wrong" is that fourier's AppHeader applies its own opaque dark `bg-background/90` header surface WITHOUT `--glass-backdrop: dark` opt-out, and the nav-dropdown items use hand-rolled `.nav-dropdown-item` CSS with flat grey background instead of glass-ui's `.glass-menu-row` + `glass-floating popover-content` combo that would render translucently glassy. The "square offset focus ring" (critique #8) is a pure fourier-bespoke adoption gap: `PaperSearch.vue`'s `.paper-search-input-wrap` uses a raw `border: 1.5px solid var(--border)` + `:focus-within { border-color: … }` with `calc(var(--radius) - 2px)` rounding that (a) does not compose the glass-ui `.input-pill` or `.focus-ring` classes and (b) leaves the native browser `:focus` outline on the inner `<input>` active (the `outline: none` is on the `<input>` element itself, NOT on the wrapper — so the blue `outline` on the `<input>` is offset relative to the wrapper). The glass-not-translucent reading over the bright math canvas is glass-ui 4.0's `W-ON-GLASS-FG` gap — a known named primitive already booked in BB W-CROSSREPO-ASKS that fourier cannot workaround without `!important`.

findings.title: Nav dropdown: hand-rolled opaque surface bypasses glass-floating self-engage tint — reads as flat grey in dark mode (critique #5)
findings.evidence: user-critique/08-dropdown-glass-darkened.png: the DropdownMenuContent renders as a flat medium-grey panel, no translucency. AppHeader.vue:122 — `DropdownMenuContent` carries class `nav-dropdown` (global style AppHeader.vue:315); nav-dropdown has NO background or surface override, so the glass-ui-4.0 `.glass-floating` default applies. Glass-floating in dark mode: `--glass-bg-floating = color-mix(in srgb, var(--card) 88%, transparent)` where dark `--card = hsl(24 8% 16%)` → opaque near-dark plate. Then the unconditional overlay-band self-engage (glass/ladder.css:200-204, `:where(.glass-floating, .glass-overlay) { --glass-tint-strength: var(--glass-tint-strength-aa) }`) applies 12% warm-ink tint (dark-arm.css:236: `--glass-tint-strength-aa: 12%`), pushing the already-opaque dark plate toward the warm-ink `--foreground` — net result: a slightly warm dark-grey opaque slab. The backdrop-filter blur exists (13px floating) but because the plate alpha is 88% in dark and the tint warms it, the translucency is perceptually lost. The hand-rolled `.nav-dropdown-item` rows (AppHeader.vue:317-342) add their own `background: none` + hover `background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--foreground) 6%, transparent)` instead of `.glass-menu-row` — so no glass hover-lift register.
findings.current_state: DropdownMenuContent gets `.glass-floating` from glass-ui CVA (dropdown-menu-BJ7E9js_.js:89). Dark `--card` at L16 + 88% opacity + 12% dark-arm self-engage tint = opaque dark-warm slab. `.nav-dropdown-item` rows are hand-rolled with flat grey hover, not `.glass-menu-row`. The panel reads as an opaque grey card, not translucent glass. The `bg-background/90 backdrop-blur-md` header beneath (AppHeader.vue:54) also blocks the backdrop sample behind the dropdown.
findings.proposed: Fourier adoption fix (beta/gamma mix — no glass-ui source touch): (1) In AppHeader.vue, let the DropdownMenuContent render with its native `.glass-floating` surface without any local `background` override. To ensure translucency reads correctly on the dark page, add `data-over-content="solid"` to the DropdownMenuContent to engage glass-ui 4.0's content-aware under-shadow modifier (glass/ladder.css:327-330). (2) Replace the hand-rolled `.nav-dropdown-item` global CSS block (AppHeader.vue:317-342) with the glass-ui `menuItemVariants` CVA's `surface='glass'` arm — this composes `.glass-menu-row` which paints the glass quiet hover plate in lockstep with the ladder. (3) The header's own `bg-background/90 backdrop-blur-md supports-[backdrop-filter]:bg-background/60` (AppHeader.vue:54) is a Tailwind utility stack bypassing the glass ladder — migrate to `glass-wash` so the header is ONE surface in the ladder and the dropdown's `backdrop-filter` samples the page behind the header, not an opaque header plate. No `!important`, no local override.

findings.title: Dark-mode dropdown: glass-floating 88% opacity + 12% warm-ink self-engage tint is architecturally correct but reads as 'darkened/wrong' because fourier's dark page offers no light backdrop for contrast — W-ON-GLASS-FG gap (critique #5 co-cause)
findings.evidence: glass/ladder.css:200-204 (`:where(.glass-floating, .glass-overlay)` unconditional tint self-engage); tokens/glass.css:137-141 (`--glass-bg-floating` at 80% light / 88% dark opacity); tokens/dark-arm.css:199 (`--glass-opacity-floating: 0.88`), dark-arm.css:236 (`--glass-tint-strength-aa: 12%`). In dark mode the floating tier is `color-mix(in srgb, hsl(24 8% 16%) 88%, transparent)` tinted 12% toward `--foreground` (cream `hsl(48 10% 90%)`) = a warm near-dark plate. The backdrop-filter blur (13px floating) samples the near-black `--background` (hsl 24 9% 4%): the blur blends a near-black backdrop with an 88% dark plate → the composite is dark and reads as opaque. The adaptive-legibility self-engage exists to handle LIGHT backdrops (over a cream page the 12% tint darkens the plate for legibility), but over fourier's dark background it instead lifts the tint toward a warmer-dark, which is correct dark-arm behaviour (the luminous-dark lift) but imperceptible over a very dark substrate.
findings.current_state: Glass-ui 4.0 self-engage is working as designed. The reading problem is that fourier's application-level chrome (the very dark page + dark header) provides no transmissive substrate for the floating glass to be legible against. The muted-foreground on the dropdown items resolves to `var(--foreground)` (unconditional lift per glass/ladder.css:203) in dark mode, which is correct, but the PLATE itself reads dark because 88% of the sample is the dark card color.
findings.proposed: This is the W-ON-GLASS-FG gap already named in BB W-CROSSREPO-ASKS (§A1 P0). The fourier-side adoption: on routes with a dark substrate, set `--glass-backdrop: dark` explicitly on the page root (not needed — that is already the default; the issue is the plate opacity, not the tint direction). The real fix is glass-ui BB W-ON-GLASS-FG shipping a `--muted-foreground-on-glass` token whose contrast target is the COMPOSITED plate fill, not `--background`. Book to BB W-CROSSREPO-ASKS. Fourier consumption: replace all dark-mode muted-foreground reads inside floating surfaces with `var(--muted-foreground-on-glass, var(--muted-foreground))` — a forward-compatible consume-and-upgrade. No fourier `!important`.
findings.wave_hint: M.W5 (glass depth ladder) — consume BB W-ON-GLASS-FG when it ships at 4.1.0

findings.title: Paper sidebar search: bespoke .paper-search-input-wrap bypasses glass-ui Input/.input-pill entirely — raw browser :focus outline leaks as offset square ring (critique #8)
findings.evidence: PaperSearch.vue:47-78 (the `.paper-search-input-wrap` scoped block): the wrapper is a hand-rolled `<div>` with `border: 1.5px solid var(--border); border-radius: calc(var(--radius) - 2px); background: var(--background)`. The inner `<input>` (PaperSearchInput.vue:37-44) carries `class="paper-search-input"` with `outline: none` scoped to `.paper-search-input` — this correctly suppresses the outline on the inner `<input>`. However the WRAPPER div has no `outline: none` and no `border-radius: var(--radius-pill)` — it uses `calc(var(--radius) - 2px)` which at the default `--radius` (0.5rem) resolves to 6px, i.e. near-square corners. user-critique/11-search-offset-square.png: the blue focus ring is clearly OFFSET below and to the right of the field boundary AND is square-cornered. The offset indicates the ring is the browser-native `:focus` outline on the wrapper div itself (triggered by a `:focus-within` rule or a descendant focus in some browsers) OR the `:focus-within` border-color transition leaves the old outline briefly visible. Glass-ui's `--focus-ring-shadow` token (tokens/scale-paper.css:66-67) is `0 0 0 2px color-mix(in srgb, var(--ring) 30%, transparent), 0 0 8px color-mix(in srgb, var(--ring) 15%, transparent)` — a `box-shadow` ring that naturally follows `border-radius`. The `.input-pill:focus-visible` rule (glass/surfaces.css:257-261) composes this with `border-color` on the same element: no offset possible. PaperSearch.vue's wrapper approach has the ring on the `<input>` child while the visible border is on the parent `<div>` — structural offset by construction.
findings.current_state: PaperSearch.vue's sidebar search is a fully bespoke hand-rolled widget: raw `<div>` wrapper + `<input>` child with no glass-ui Input/`.input-pill` composition. The `:focus-within` on the wrapper only changes `border-color` (not a `box-shadow` focus ring), and `calc(var(--radius) - 2px)` gives ~6px near-square corners. The browser paints its own default `:focus` outline on the focused `<input>` child, which is visually offset from the parent wrapper's border boundary by the 0.3rem padding (PaperSearch.vue:54). Result: offset square blue outline.
findings.proposed: Transpose PaperSearchInput.vue's `<div class="paper-search-input-wrap">` to compose glass-ui's `.input-pill` class on a real `<input>` element, or wrap the search affordance in a glass-ui `<Input>` component with `icon` slot for the Search glyph. The `.input-pill` class (glass/surfaces.css:187-227) provides: `border-radius: var(--radius-pill)` (fully rounded), `border: 1.5px solid var(--control-surface-border)`, `backdrop-filter: var(--control-surface-blur)`, and `:focus-visible { outline: none; border-color: var(--color-accent-opaque, var(--ring)); box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px color-mix(in srgb, var(--ring) 30%, transparent) }` — the glass rounded focus ring at ZERO offset. The Search icon and action buttons slot inside via absolute/flex composition on the same element. Migrate the placeholder/icon/clear-btn composition into the glass-ui Input icon-slot pattern. Delete the `.paper-search-input-wrap` / `.paper-search-input` hand-rolled CSS block entirely (no-legacy, net deletion). For the sidebar variant the radius is `var(--radius-pill)` (fully pill) not the current near-square.

findings.title: glass-floating unconditional self-engage tint (overlay band) — glass-ui 4.0 design intent is correct but the calibration over fourier's dark page is imperceptible; the --glass-tint-strength-aa dark value (12%) is a glass-ui knob, not a fourier override target
findings.evidence: glass/ladder.css:200-204: `:where(.glass-floating, .glass-overlay) { --glass-tint-source: var(--glass-tint-ink); --glass-tint-strength: var(--glass-tint-strength-aa); --muted-foreground: var(--foreground) }`. dark-arm.css:236: `--glass-tint-strength-aa: 12%`. findings.title: AppHeader surface: Tailwind utility stack (bg-background/90 + backdrop-blur-md) is a hand-rolled header glass surface bypassing the glass ladder — blocks dropdown backdrop sample
findings.evidence: AppHeader.vue:54: `class="app-header sticky top-0 z-[var(--z-overlay)] bg-background/90 backdrop-blur-md supports-[backdrop-filter]:bg-background/60"`. This is NOT a glass ladder rung — it is a Tailwind arbitrary-opacity utility (`/90`) compositing directly against `--background`. The supports-backdrop-filter arm uses `bg-background/60` which gives a 60% opaque near-black plate (dark mode) with `backdrop-blur-md` (12px). Any DropdownMenuContent floating above this header samples the 60% near-black header plate as its backdrop — not the page content. The `backdrop-filter` on the dropdown (glass-floating at 13px blur) thus sees a dark surface, so its own 13px blur samples near-black → the plate reads dark regardless of opacity. This is the structural root of critique #5: the dropdown is translucent, but the surface it samples is opaque dark.
findings.current_state: AppHeader uses a hand-rolled Tailwind opacity utility stack for its glass surface. The DropdownMenu portal renders above the header in DOM order and samples the header's own near-opaque dark backdrop-filter as its background. The compounded backdrop samples read dark, producing the 'darkened dropdown' appearance.
findings.proposed: Migrate AppHeader's surface to `.glass-wash` (the lowest glass ladder rung, ~30% opacity + 1px blur) so the header's own backdrop is translucent and the dropdown floating above it samples the PAGE content, not an opaque header. Delete the Tailwind `bg-background/90 backdrop-blur-md supports-[backdrop-filter]:bg-background/60` utility stack and replace with the `glass-wash` class. Add `border-bottom: 1px solid var(--glass-border-wash)` as a warm hairline separator. The header's `z-[var(--z-overlay)]` stays. This is the adoption step that makes the entire header chrome participate in the glass ladder and makes the dropdown's backdrop sample meaningful.

glassui_asks.name: W-ON-GLASS-FG (already in BB W-CROSSREPO-ASKS §A1 P0)
glassui_asks.what: Ship a `--muted-foreground-on-glass` token (and a `--foreground-on-glass` sibling) whose contrast target is the COMPOSITED glass fill — not `--background`. The token must be set on the floating/overlay band glass surfaces unconditionally so that muted text inside a dropdown, dialog, or popover clears AA against the translucent plate, not the distant page background. The dark arm value is calibrated against the ~`oklab(0.20)` dark floating plate (approximately `hsl(48 10% 90%)` — the warm cream foreground — since the plate is dark and the legible foreground is the light cream). Forward-compatible: consumers adopt `var(--muted-foreground-on-glass, var(--muted-foreground))`.
glassui_asks.why: Glass-ui 4.0's unconditional overlay-band self-engage tint (`:where(.glass-floating, .glass-overlay) { --muted-foreground: var(--foreground) }`) already does a global lift in dark mode. But over very-dark substrate pages (like fourier's `hsl(24 9% 4%)` background) where the floating plate composes to a dark warm-grey, downstream consumers need a scoped legibility token anchored on the PLATE luminance, not the canvas. The existing unconditional `--muted-foreground: var(--foreground)` lift is the correct direction but the contrast anchor is still `--background` semantically, not the composited plate. The named `W-ON-GLASS-FG` ask (BB §A1 P0) already recognises this; this filing confirms it from fourier's consumption side.

A7.dimension: invariants-audit (A7) — invariant adds/edits + recent-deferred fold, grounded in the live M.W1-migrated critique
A7.verdict: The 8 live critiques expose a structural GAP in the invariant ledger: inv-33 (design-system-single-source) and inv-34 (motion-proportion floor) govern SOURCE-of-truth and proportion, but NOTHING in inv-1..34 binds a RENDERED-FIDELITY floor. Every M design invariant is asserted (one source, one rung, proportion) but none is VERIFIED-IN-A-RENDER — which is precisely how a tree can pass inv-33 (a surface "declares glass" by class) while compositing as opaque grey (critique 01/05/08), pass "rounding tokens applied" while painting a square focus ring offset past the field (critique 02/11), and choose underline tabs over glass (critique 07) with no invariant contradicted. The fix is FOUR fresh-integer invariants (inv-35 glass-fidelity-floor, inv-36 geometry-continuity-floor [rounding + no-raw-focus-ring, unified], inv-37 control-affordance-floor [idle-paint + DEC-2 controls-left + glass-tab-default], inv-38 render-verified-design-gate [the meta-floor that makes 33/34/35/36/37 satisfiable only against a captured render, not a class-grep]) PLUS three EDITS: (a) an inv-33 scope clarification that "picks its rung by depth BAND" is necessary-but-NOT-sufficient — the rung must also COMPOSITE as glass against the live page background (the dark-scheme darkening of critique 08 is an inv-33-conformant class on a non-conformant render); (b) an inv-3/inv-29 clarification that the M.W1 underline-tab choice and the surviving 25-site .cartoon-card shim are RETIRED-class residue, not a floor; (c) a §2 namespace note for 35-38 (clean integers, NO precept collision — the precept band stops at 33). Root-class spread: the fidelity/focus-ring/darkened-menu defects root in glass-ui 4.0 SOURCE (alpha, book to glass-ui BB W-CROSSREPO-ASKS, NEVER a fourier !important) but the INVARIANT that makes them detectable is fourier-owned (the verify-in-render gate); the tab/idle-paint/controls-left defects are fourier adoption+residue (beta/gamma). No new invariant licenses a workaround; each binds an EVIDENCE form (a captured render, a computed alpha, an asideSide assertion), consistent with inv-6 gates-close-on-evidence and inv-9 surface-appropriate-evidence.

A8.verdict: 22 legacy items confirmed across 5 categories. The `.cartoon-card` @utility shim (17 call-sites across 13 files + the definition in style.css) is the single largest item and the root of critique #1 (not-glassy surfaces). Three `SegmentedTabs variant="underline"` residues directly violate the user's critique #7 (glass tabs reversed). Seven `!important` declarations span four files. Five separate `spectrumColor` implementations duplicate what value.js 0.13.0 `sampleColorRamp` should own. Six rAF animation loops (excluding the animation-store playhead and layout-sync exemptions) are M.W9's excise targets. The `glass-scrubber` identifier survives in eight comment blocks — inert today but a maintenance hazard. The `tab-slide-in` global keyframe in style.css is keyed on a retired primitive's data-attribute and belongs upstream. Hand-rolled rgba() box-shadow recipes in at least five components bypass the `--shadow-*` token ladder. Every item below has an idiomatic no-legacy replacement; none require a workaround or !important.

findings.title: `.cartoon-card` @utility shim — 17 call-sites across 13 files
findings.evidence: web/src/style.css:107 defines `@utility cartoon-card { @apply cartoon-surface; border-color: var(--border); background: var(--card); }`. 17 template-level usages: BasisCanvas.vue:521, ImageUpload.vue:38, ContourPreview.vue:33, GalleryView.vue:312, VisualizationView.vue:163, AdminUserList.vue:308+362, GalleryCardModal.vue (border comment at 247), EquationView.vue:230+239+243+251+308, EqCoefficientsPanel.vue:12, InfoCard.vue:18, FunctionInput.vue:93+175, MorphShapePreview.vue:4, HarmonicLevelGrid.vue:2, MorphPhaseConfig.vue:2. Comment at style.css:98 explicitly calls it the 'dead-class resurrection'. Screenshot user-critique/01 shows the Bad-Gateway card as a flat opaque 'paper stamp', not glass. live-workspace shows controls panel with identical cartoon-stamp appearance.
findings.current_state: A @utility shim in style.css resurrects a class glass-ui removed at C.W5 (cards.css:2), mapping it onto `cartoon-surface` + hard `var(--card)` background. Result: 17 surfaces rendered as opaque paper cards, zero glass depth, no translucency — critique #1 root.
findings.proposed: M.W5: DELETE `@utility cartoon-card` from style.css entirely. At each call-site replace with the correct glass-depth-ladder band: BAND 0 bare math substrate (canvas container) → remove surface class entirely, let the Configurator stage own it; BAND 1 in-flow instrument panels (FunctionInput, EqCoefficientsPanel, ContourPreview, MorphPhaseConfig, HarmonicLevelGrid) → `glass-wash` (ambient) or `glass-resting` (focused/active); BAND 2 lifted chrome (sticky toolbars, GalleryView batch bar, AdminUserList top bar) → `glass-floating`; error/status banners → `glass-wash` with `--destructive`/`--muted-foreground` tint via `color-mix`. BasisCanvas.vue canvas-container: drop the surface class — the Configurator `#stage` slot owns the material. The 3-band ladder is frozen at M.W5 and applied in a single pass.

Additionally, audit whether the VisualizationView and EquationView mobile tab bars are redundant once `asideSide="left"` + the Configurator two-column layout is in place — on desktop the tabs should not exist at all (`lg:hidden` is already on both but verify it holds under Configurator's grid). findings.title: `!important` on `.is-auto-active` tonal state — FunctionInput.vue
findings.evidence: web/src/components/equation/FunctionInput.vue:251-253: `.is-auto-active { color: var(--viz-amber) !important; border-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--viz-amber) 40%, transparent) !important; background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--viz-amber) 8%, transparent) !important; }` — three `!important` overrides to force the tonal-accent idle fill on the auto-harmonics button.
findings.current_state: Three `!important` declarations override what appears to be a glass-ui Button's default ghost/outline surface. They mask a specificity race instead of using the platform-provided tonal/accent fill idiom.
findings.proposed: M.W7 (colour pops wave): adopt the glass-ui tonal button pattern — `<Button variant="tonal" :data-accent="vizAmber">` or the equivalent prop that the glass-ui 4.0 Button exports for per-instance accent. The per-instance `--pill-c`/`--accent` CSS custom property override on the component root (without !important) resolves at lower specificity than any descendant rule, eliminating the specificity fight. Remove all three `!important` lines. If glass-ui 4.0 Button does not yet expose a tonal accent slot, book as a BB ask (see glassui_asks).

findings.title: `!important` on `.eq-coeff:hover` — EquationView.vue
findings.evidence: web/src/components/equation/EquationView.vue:421: `.eq-card :deep(.eq-coeff:hover) { color: var(--viz-amber) !important; }` — a deep-selector !important override on a KaTeX-generated span hover to apply the amber accent.
findings.current_state: The deep + !important combination is a specificity escape hatch on content injected via `v-html` (the rendered KaTeX equation). The KaTeX output already has high-specificity inline styles in some cases, so !important may be load-bearing — but the approach is fragile and forbidden by the standing directive.
findings.proposed: M.W5/W7: The `.eq-coeff` class is injected server-side via the LaTeX→KaTeX pipeline. Instead of `!important`, wrap the KaTeX display in a CSS custom property isolation context: `.eq-scroll-region { --eq-coeff-hover: var(--viz-amber); }` and reference `var(--eq-coeff-hover)` in the deep rule without `!important`. If KaTeX inline styles still win, use the `color` property on the containing `.katex` wrapper (which inherits into spans without `!important`) via a data attribute set on hover with a JS handler. This is idiomatic; the !important line is excised.

findings.title: `!important` on `overflow: visible` — EquationResult.vue + EquationView.vue
findings.evidence: web/src/components/equation/EquationResult.vue:74: `.eq-scroll-region :deep(.katex-display) { overflow: visible !important; }`. web/src/components/equation/EquationView.vue:406: `.coeff-popover-inner :deep(.katex-display) { overflow: visible !important; }`. Both override the global `.katex-display { overflow-x: auto; overflow-y: visible; }` rule in style.css.
findings.current_state: Two !important overrides fight the global KaTeX display rule. The global rule in style.css sets `overflow-x: auto; overflow-y: visible` for scrollable display equations; the component rules try to make fractions visible in constrained containers.
findings.proposed: M.W5: Resolve the cascade properly. The global `style.css` rule already sets `overflow-y: visible`; the only conflict is `overflow-x: auto`. In the specific container contexts (popover, coefficient panel) where fractions must not clip, add a scoped CSS custom property `--katex-display-overflow: visible` at the container root and reference it in style.css as `overflow-x: var(--katex-display-overflow, auto)`. No `!important` needed. Excise both override rules.

findings.title: `!important` on `animation-play-state: paused` — GalleryMarquee.vue
findings.evidence: web/src/components/visualization/gallery/GalleryMarquee.vue:99: `.marquee-track:hover .marquee-inner { animation-play-state: paused !important; }` — prevents an override from higher specificity from resuming the marquee on hover.
findings.current_state: The !important is defensive, added to prevent a specificity conflict that may not exist. The selector `.marquee-track:hover .marquee-inner` has sufficient specificity without it.
findings.proposed: M.W9 (motion architecture): When the marquee is transposed to use `@starting-style` and `animation-timeline` (scroll-driven, M.W9), `animation-play-state` manipulation is replaced by native scroll-linked progress. Until then, excise the `!important` — the selector specificity (parent:hover + child) already wins over the base rule. If the motion collapses to the `prefers-reduced-motion` path, the animation is removed entirely, making the paused override moot.

findings.title: Five duplicated `spectrumColor` implementations

glassui_asks.name: BB-TONAL-BUTTON-ACCENT
glassui_asks.what: Expose a per-instance tonal accent on `Button` — a CSS custom property `--button-accent` (or a `tonal` variant with `:color` prop) that sets the idle fill, hover fill, and text colour from a single OKLCH stop without requiring `!important` overrides. The EquationModeToggle's active state, preset pills' active state (`.preset-pill.is-active`), and the BasisSelector's `.basis-toggle[aria-pressed=true]` all hand-roll the same pattern. A first-class tonal accent prop eliminates the entire !important surface and consolidates idle-affordance paint (critique #6 — button options not visible when not hovered) across all panes in one adoption.

glassui_asks.name: BB-INPUT-PILL-VARIANT
glassui_asks.what: Add a `variant="pill"` (or `shape="pill"`) to the `Input` component that applies `border-radius: 9999px`, the glass `--ring`-based focus ring, and suppresses the default square outline. Focus ring must be visually rounded (matching the pill boundary) and must not offset beyond the field boundary.
glassui_asks.why: GallerySearchBar.vue hand-rolls a bare `<input>` with `outline-none` to achieve a pill shape (A8-20). The resulting focus ring is square and offset — exactly critique #8. The fix is a first-class glass Input pill variant so every search field in the product is idiomatic and accessible without custom CSS.

glassui_asks.name: BB-TAB-PANEL-ENTRY-ANIMATION

Moving it into the Tabs primitive removes a global selector from fourier that may conflict with glass-ui's own tab transitions.

glassui_asks.name: BB-CONFIGURATOR-STAGE-MOBILE-HEIGHT
glassui_asks.what: The Configurator's `.configurator-stage` cell should resolve to a nonzero flex height in the mobile flex-column layout (when `display: flex; flex-direction: column` replaces the desktop grid). Currently fourier patches this via `:deep(.configurator-stage) { flex: 1 1 0% }` — an inv-30 violation.
glassui_asks.why: Without the fix the canvas stage collapses to 0px on mobile (the canvas is `position: absolute` inside a flex cell with no intrinsic height). The `:deep` override in VisualizationView.vue (A8-19) exists solely to paper this over. Moving the fix into the Configurator removes the only inv-30 violation in the VisualizationView layout.

glassui_asks.name: BB-CONFIGURATOR-ASIDE-WIDTH-PROP

This is an inv-30 violation (reaches inside the component). A prop-driven aside width removes all three overrides and makes the VisualizationView layout fully declarative.

B1.dimension: B1 — Paper pane (the landing "/"→/paper; PaperView + sidebar + search + article hero)
B1.verdict:
The paper IS the front door (§4.1 resolved) and it fails the user's two foundational critiques at its two largest surfaces. The article sheet (PaperView.vue:516-529) and the sidebar nav (PaperSidebar.vue:151-166) are byte-identical hand-rolled "cartoon stamps" — `border:2px solid …15%` + `box-shadow:3px 3px 0px` + opaque `background:var(--card)` + raw `border-radius:0.75rem` — exactly the offset-shadow opaque card the user flags in crop 01 (#1 not-glassy, #2 not-rounded). The search input shows a square, blue, OFFSET native focus ring beyond the rounded field (crop 11, #8): the wrap carries `:focus-within` border styling but NO managed focus ring, so the engine paints its default outline on the focusable element. The hero is the deepest typography miss: the H1 is raw Tailwind (`text-4xl md:text-[3.25rem]`), the ℱ ornament renders in Plus-Jakarta SANS (`.fourier-f`→`--font-display`) dropped inside a Computer-Modern SERIF headline (reads as a glyph glitch), Fraunces is vendored-fetched-and-DEAD, and there is no scroll-reveal on the body. Root classes split cleanly: the cartoon sheet, raw radii, hardcoded `
` and dead-Fraunces are M.W1-residue/adoption-gap (gamma/beta → M.W5/W6); the darkened glass-floating search dropdown and the absence of a glass input focus-ring are glass-ui-4.0-owned (alpha → BB W-CROSSREPO-ASKS). The proposed gestalt: the article + sidebar stay the deliberate "sheet on a desk" BAND-0 metaphor but re-tokenised onto `--radius-card`/`--shadow-cartoon-*` (no hand-rolled offset), the search adopts a glass focus-ring + veil dropdown, and the hero becomes the in-place Fraunces φ-display mathematical title with a PRM-gated char-stagger — audacious once, at the front door.

findings.title: Raw literal radii on the paper surfaces — not the --radius-* scale (critique #2)

findings.title: Paper search shows a square, offset, blue native focus ring — no managed glass focus ring (critique #8)
findings.evidence: user-critique/11-search-offset-square.png (square blue ring extending BEYOND the rounded field); PaperSearch.vue:47-56 (.paper-search-input-wrap: rounded border + `:focus-within` border-color shift ONLY, no ring); PaperSearchInput.vue:37-46 (the inner <input>); PaperSearch.vue:69-78 (.paper-search-input has `outline:none` but the wrap/Button focus is unmanaged)
findings.current_state: The search wrap rounds via `border-radius: calc(var(--radius) - 2px)` and on focus only shifts `border-color`. The inner input zeros its own outline, but the focused element (input or its wrapping control) still receives the engine's DEFAULT focus outline — a square, non-radius-following, offset ring (crop 11). There is no `:focus-visible` glass ring composed at the field. The square ring sits OUTSIDE the rounded field because the UA outline does not inherit the wrap's `border-radius`.
findings.proposed: TWO halves. (alpha) Book the glass-ui input focus-ring primitive: a `--glass-focus-ring` recipe (radius-following, `box-shadow`-based inset/outset ring on `:focus-visible`, brand-tinted, never the square UA outline) shipped on the library's Input/field primitives so EVERY consumer inherits a rounded glass ring — fourier today owns no glass Input, so this is glass-ui-owned (BB W-CROSSREPO-ASKS). (beta) Until shipped, fourier composes a tokenised `:focus-visible` ring on `.paper-search-input-wrap` using `box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px color-mix(in oklab, var(--route-accent) 45%, transparent)` + `border-radius:inherit`, driven by `:has(:focus-visible)` — radius-following, NOT a UA outline, no `!important`. The accent reads from the M.W7 per-route `--route-accent` (paper=ramp[0]).

findings.title: The paper search results dropdown (glass-floating) renders darkened/flat over the near-white sidebar (critique #5)

(beta, interim) fourier declares `--glass-tint-strength: var(--glass-tint-strength-floor)` on the paper search dropdown's own surface (the inheriting axis the rung's `color-mix` reads — a documented consumer dial-down glass-ui's own comment sanctions: 'a dark-substrate consumer who wants the pristine plate sets `--glass-tint-strength: 0%`'), restoring the translucent floating plate over the known-light paper substrate. Same applies to the mobile-TOC dropdown (BAND 2).

findings.title: The ℱ ornament renders in Plus-Jakarta SANS inside the Computer-Modern SERIF headline — a glyph clash

glassui_asks.name: glass-input-focus-ring
glassui_asks.what: A radius-following glass focus ring on the library's Input/field primitives: a `:focus-visible` `box-shadow`-based ring (brand-tinted, `border-radius:inherit`) that replaces the square, offset UA default outline. Shipped on the primitive so every consumer inherits a rounded glass ring with zero per-field CSS.
glassui_asks.why: The paper search field (crop 11, critique #8) paints the engine's default SQUARE focus outline OUTSIDE its rounded field because the UA outline does not follow `border-radius`. fourier owns no glass Input today, so the fix belongs in glass-ui (inv-16). Every glass consumer with a focusable field hits the identical square-ring mismatch — it generalizes beyond fourier.

glassui_asks.name: glass-floating-band-calm-light-opt
glassui_asks.what: A consumer-declarable opt for the overlay band (`:where(.glass-floating,.glass-overlay)` in ladder.css:200-204) to drop from the UNCONDITIONAL AA-darken to the sub-perceptual floor when the consumer KNOWS its substrate is a calm light surface (e.g. a `--glass-backdrop: light-calm` register, or honour an ancestor `--glass-tint-strength` cap on the band rather than forcing the AA strength). Coordinates with the existing BB `W-ON-GLASS-FG` register (distinct contrast target).
glassui_asks.why: The paper search dropdown + mobile-TOC dropdown are correctly on `glass-floating`, but 4.0 darkens the whole floating band toward warm-ink unconditionally ('floats over WHATEVER the consumer painted'). Over fourier's cream paper substrate this reads as the flat opaque grey the user flags (crop 08, critique #5). The library's own comment already sanctions a per-surface `--glass-tint-strength: 0%` escape — this ask formalizes a declarable calm-light register so the floating plate stays translucent over a KNOWN light surface without each consumer hand-zeroing the tint.

open_questions: Fraunces as `--font-display` is an app-wide override (it also re-points the `.fourier-f` ornament and any other `--font-display` consumer). Confirm at M.W6 that overriding `--font-stack-display` for a SERIF brand does not regress glass-ui surfaces that assume a geometric-sans display face — or whether the booked `--font-display-serif` distinct-slot intent is the cleaner contract (M.md §10).

The interim consumer dial-down for the darkened floating dropdown (B1-PAPER-04 beta half: `--glass-tint-strength: var(--glass-tint-strength-floor)` on the paper dropdown surface) restores translucency over the light paper — but does it hold over the DARK theme, where the band's dark-arm re-tunes the strength to a luminous-dark LIFT? Verify the dial-down does not collapse the dark-theme plate before shipping; the BB ask is the durable fix.

The square offset focus ring in crop 11: is the offending outline on the inner `<input>` (which carries `outline:none`) or on a wrapping glass-ui Button/control whose focus is unmanaged? Confirm the exact focused element at M.W5 so the interim `:has(:focus-visible)` ring is composed on the correct boundary (the wrap) and the UA outline is actually suppressed there.

B2.dimension: B2 — Workspace pane ("/w"): VisualizationView + Configurator + dock/controls composition, grounded in the live critique of the bumped+migrated m/w1 instance.
B2.verdict: The workspace pane is the critique epicentre and every one of the user's eight findings lands here in concentrated form. The diagnosis is decisive and largely VINDICATES the existing M plan rather than overturning it: the inverted controls-RIGHT layout (#4), the not-glassy opaque cards (#1/#2), the underline tabs (#7), the idle-invisible dock (#6), and the desktop tab-bar leak (#3) all trace to fourier ADOPTION GAPS and M.W1 BUMP RESIDUE, NOT to glass-ui-4.0 regressions — glass-ui 4.0 already ships every primitive needed (asideSide="left", asideWidth, the 5-tier glass ladder, squircle.css, SegmentedTabs default variant="pill"). The single hardening the audit demands: M.W1's migration made TWO active wrong choices that directly produced the critique — it pinned SegmentedTabs to variant="underline" (the user wants the default glass pill) and it left the `.cartoon-card` dead-class SHIM resurrected in style.css (the literal cartoon-stamp the user circled). These are no-legacy violations sitting in the migrated tree right now and must be deleted at root, not re-skinned. The Configurator is already mounted (B.W2.a) but consumed against its grain: fourier hand-rolls four `grid-template-columns` overrides + a `:deep(.configurator-stage)` mobile patch to FIGHT the substrate's stage-first arrangement, when passing `asideSide="left"` + `asideWidth` deletes all of that AND satisfies DEC-2. Net: the workspace findings are predominantly beta (adopt the shipped chassis/ladder) + gamma (delete the two bad migration choices); only the dock idle/active register and the on-glass muted-foreground are genuine glass-ui asks, both already booked in BB (W-DOCK-MORPH-FAMILY sibling / W-ON-GLASS-FG / the DockIconButton-active ask). No new waves required; the existing M.W5/W7/W8/W10 mapping holds, hardened with the two delete-at-root corrections.

findings.title: Configurator consumed against its grain: controls pinned RIGHT (DEC-2 inversion) via four hand-rolled grid overrides that fight the shipped asideSide="left"
findings.evidence: live/live-workspace.jpeg (the 'Image — source input' aside pinned top-RIGHT, canvas LEFT over a vast dead dot-grid) + CRITIQUE.md#4; VisualizationView.vue:194 `<Configurator scroll-mode="auto" class="viz-configurator">` (no asideSide passed → defaults to "right"); the four overrides VisualizationView.vue:322,326,329 `grid-template-columns: minmax(0,1fr) minmax(...)` + the mobile `:deep(.configurator-stage)` patch:344; Configurator.vue.d.ts:25,70 ships `asideSide?: 'left'|'right'` ("grid-column placement + border-side only, no source reorder — no a11y regression") + asideWidth:79
findings.current_state: The Configurator's intrinsic arrangement is stage-first (canvas LEFT) + controls-aside (RIGHT). fourier mounts it (B.W2.a) but never passes `asideSide`, so it renders right — the exact DEC-2 inversion. Worse, fourier then HAND-ROLLS four responsive `grid-template-columns` overrides (1024/1280/1536) plus a `:deep(.configurator-stage){flex:1}` mobile patch to force the canvas to fill — re-implementing the chassis's own track logic against it. The aside floats top-right over an enormous empty dot-grid: the controls do not read as an authoring rail.
findings.proposed: Pass `aside-side="left"` + `:aside-width="['360px','440px']"` to the Configurator and DELETE all four `grid-template-columns` overrides AND the `:deep(.configurator-stage)` mobile flex patch (the substrate owns the track band via `--configurator-aside-min/max` and the mobile single-column collapse). The flip is grid-column-placement + border-side only — DOM/tab order stays stage→aside, no a11y regression (per the prop doc). This is the literal DEC-2 authoring-rail: controls LEFT, canvas as the composed-void stage RIGHT. No new CSS, strictly fewer lines.
findings.wave_hint: M.W8 (asideSide=left + delete the 3-4 grid-template-columns overrides + the mobile :deep stage patch — already named in §4 W8)

findings.title: The `.cartoon-card` dead-class SHIM is the literal cartoon-stamp the user circled — a resurrected glass-ui-removed recipe, a standing no-legacy violation
findings.evidence: user-critique/01 (the 'Computation failed / Bad Gateway' card: 2px border + offset hard shadow + opaque cream fill) + live/live-workspace.jpeg (the right aside card) + CRITIQUE.md#1; style.css:98-111 `@utility cartoon-card { @apply cartoon-surface; border-color: var(--border); background: var(--card); }` with the comment admitting 'glass-ui removed the .cartoon-card recipe at C.W5 ... the dead-class resurrection ... the fourier-local KISS stop-gap'; consumed at 25 sites incl. findings.title: Workspace dock icon-buttons render no idle paint and the hand-rolled `is-active` toggle has NO backing paint (toggled-on reads as idle)
findings.evidence: user-critique/09 (bare-text option chips, captioned 'buttons invisible unhovered' — the same idle-ghost pattern) + CRITIQUE.md#6; CanvasControlsDock.vue:54,59,71,77,87 `:class="{ 'is-active': ... }"` (7 sites) with no `.is-active` rule in the scoped style block; glass-ui dock-controls/icon-button.css:35 `background: transparent` at idle BY DESIGN; DockIconButton.vue.d.ts has NO `active`/`pressed`/`tone` prop at 4.0

B3.verdict: The Gallery pane is the clearest in-the-wild demonstration of the user's 8 critiques: the Gallery|Drafts tabs render as an ink-hairline UNDERLINE (critiques #7/#10) because the M.W1 migration pinned `variant="underline"` on a SegmentedTabs whose 4.0 DEFAULT is already `pill` (the glass-track slider the user wants) — a pure gamma residue that reverses with a one-token edit, no new code. The confirm/card dialogs ride `surface="opaque"` rather than the `glass-overlay` rung. The search pill is a hand-rolled `<input outline-none>` (no glass rung, no rounded focus ring — the gallery sibling of critique #8/#11). The empty-state CTA is `variant="outline"` with weak idle paint (the #6 family). None of these need a workaround: every fix is "adopt the rung / flip the variant / delete the shim" — M's "bump + consume + delete" gestalt. The ONE alpha root-cause is glass-ui 4.0's overlay/floating rungs defaulting `--glass-backdrop: light`, which over fourier's dark substrate engages the W55 bright-bucket and DARKENS the glass (the menu/dropdown darkening, critique #5) — fourier must set `--glass-backdrop: dark` on its app root, and book the dark-default register as a glass-ui ask. Beyond the critiques, the card lacks the 3-tier depth hierarchy the M plan freezes, and J's inv-15 publish/provenance affordances remain unsurfaced in this pane.

glassui_asks.name: glass-overlay/floating dark-substrate default (the darkened dropdown root-cause, critique #5)
glassui_asks.what: glass-ui 4.0's `.glass-floating` and `.glass-overlay` rungs (and the menu rows that compose the surface-axis seam) hard-set `--glass-backdrop: light` at their own root (ladder.css:~90,~108; menu.css:24-26 W55 bright-bucket). Over fourier's DARK app substrate this engages the W55 'locally darken the glass over light content' tint-lift — so dropdowns/menus/overlays composite to a flat darkened grey instead of translucent glass (exactly critique #5 / user-critique/08). The library assumes the overlay band floats over light; fourier floats it over dark. ASK: let the dark-substrate consumer opt the overlay band back to the `dark` tint arm via a documented single ancestor token (`--glass-backdrop: dark`) that the floating/overlay rungs RESPECT (today they re-point their OWN tint through a self-rule that overrides the ancestor), OR ship a `data-theme=dark` aware default. fourier's interim: set `--glass-backdrop: dark` on the app root — but only if the rung honours it.

B4.dimension: B4 — per-pane EQUATION (/equation): FunctionInput preset pills, the Compute/error cards, MetricBadge, the mobile tabs, .eq-grid→Configurator, convergence/legend, audacious math typography
B4.verdict:
The Equation pane is the epicentre of critique #6 (idle-invisible controls) and a clean specimen of #1/#2 (cartoon-stamp cards, near-square corners). Root-causing live source confirms the M plan's diagnoses and lets me HARDEN three waves rather than re-derive them. The "buttons invisible unhovered" finding (crop 09) traces precisely to FunctionInput's preset pills using glass-ui 4.0's `outline` variant (`border-input bg-background` = matches the cream page, faint border → reads as bare text), while `is-active`/`x(π−x)` pills DO paint — proving the contrast is the defect, not the markup. The idiomatic fix is the M plan's already-booked `accent-tone` glass-ui recipe (the contrast-floored 3-channel tonal idle fill, re-derived ~57× across fourier) plus adopting an idle-painting variant (`accent`/`glass-wash`) — NOT a fourier `!important` patch. I found a concrete no-legacy violation the audit must fold: FunctionInput's `.is-auto-active` uses THREE `!important`s to fight the glass button variant (lines 250-254) — the exact workaround the standing directive forbids; it must dissolve into the `accent-tone` recipe at W8/W7. The Compute/error/equation/convergence cards all wear the `.cartoon-card` shim (style.css:107 — re-binds the C.W5-removed class to `cartoon-surface`: 2px border + offset-stamp shadow + opaque `--card`), which IS the cartoon-stamp/near-square look of crops 01/09; M.W5 deletes it to the glass ladder. The mobile tab bar in EquationView is correctly `lg:hidden` (critique #3/#7 about desktop glass tabs is a WORKSPACE concern, not equation) — but the M.W1 `variant="underline"` choice still applies here and should flip to the glass `pill` default for consistency. Math-as-subject gaps: the equation pane has NO h1/display-typography hero (only a muted `

` empty-state), the ℱ-glyph/KaTeX hero is not on the φ-ladder (M.W6), the convergence legend is corner-pinned and occludes the curve (M.W8), and there is no convergence-reveal motion at first paint (M.W9). All findings carry idiomatic no-legacy transpositions. No new glass-ui asks beyond the ones M already books (accent-tone, input focus-ring, dropdown surface) — I confirm and sharpen them with equation-pane evidence.
