Net: harden M.W5 (glass+rounding+focus-ring adoption) and book two glass-ui asks; the motion gaps (hero entrance, scroll reveal, ℱ signature) are already correctly planned in M.W10 and need only the once-discipline + reading-primacy guardrails re-affirmed.

findings.title: Paper search focus ring is SQUARE + OFFSET — the raw <input>+wrap opts out of glass-ui's shipped .focus-ring recipe and the Input primitive
findings.evidence: user-critique/11-search-offset-square.png (a blue rectangular ring sitting OUTSIDE the rounded field, square corners on a rounded wrap); PaperSearch.vue:47-60 (.paper-search-input-wrap uses border-color on :focus-within only, no ring); PaperSearch.vue:73 (.paper-search-input { outline: none }); PaperSearchInput.vue:37-46 (bare raw <input class=paper-search-input>, not glass-ui <Input>); glass-ui ships .focus-ring (components.css — a --focus-ring-shadow/--focus-ring-width box-shadow ring that inherits border-radius) and an Input primitive (dist/components/ui/input/Input.vue) that fourier does NOT consume
findings.current_state: The paper search is a hand-rolled <input> with outline:none inside a div wrap whose only focus affordance is a :focus-within border-color shift. Because the input kills its own outline and the wrap supplies no ring, the focused state on the live bumped build paints the UA default :focus-visible outline — a rectangular ring that ignores the wrap's calc(var(--radius)-2px) and renders square + offset. glass-ui 4.0 ships both a rounded .focus-ring box-shadow recipe (radius-inheriting, the correct primitive) and an <Input> component that carries it; the paper search consumes neither.
findings.proposed: Adopt the platform: replace the bespoke raw <input> with glass-ui's <Input> primitive (or, if the inline-icon+expand+clear affordances require a custom field, compose the shipped .focus-ring utility class on .paper-search-input-wrap and keep input{outline:none}). The .focus-ring box-shadow inherits border-radius → the ring becomes a rounded glass ring flush to the field, no offset, no square corners. This deletes the bespoke :focus-within border-color hack and routes the field through inv-33's single material source. No !important, no UA-outline carve.
findings.wave_hint: M.W5 (glass-depth + focus-ring adoption; the search field is paper chrome)

findings.title: glass-ui 4.0 overlay-band UNCONDITIONAL darken reaches the paper search dropdown (glass-floating) — the critique-#5 darkened-glass mechanism, an upstream ask
findings.evidence: user-critique/08 (dropdown renders darkened/flat-grey, 'glass elements darkened and not right'); PaperSearchDropdown.vue:39 (.paper-search-results glass-floating); glass-ui ladder.css:200-204 — `:where(.glass-floating,.glass-overlay){ --glass-tint-source: var(--glass-tint-ink); --glass-tint-strength: var(--glass-tint-strength-aa); --muted-foreground: var(--foreground) }` (UNCONDITIONAL, no @container gate); tokens/dark-arm.css:236,243 (in dark --glass-tint-strength-aa:12%, --glass-tint-strength-floor:12%, --glass-tint-ink resolves to --foreground)
findings.current_state: glass-ui 4.0's ladder self-engages the overlay band (floating/overlay) to darken-toward-ink UNCONDITIONALLY because style queries can't self-match and the :root default is dark, so it cannot distinguish an explicit dark-substrate consumer from the default. The library comment claims that over a dark page this becomes a 'luminous-dark LIFT', but the live render on fourier's dark substrate reads as a flat/darkened plate (critique #5), and the same band carries the paper search-results dropdown. This is a glass-ui-owned behavior; fourier composing glass-floating correctly inherits the unwanted darken.
findings.proposed: BOOK to glass-ui (inv-16, never write glass-ui): the overlay-band self-darken needs a dark-substrate opt-out that does not require every consumer to set --glass-tint-strength:0% on every floating surface (e.g. honour an ancestor --glass-backdrop:dark on the consumer root, or a --glass-overlay-adaptive:off escape that keeps the pristine translucent plate over a known-dark app). fourier's interim, if the dropdown must read translucent NOW, is the documented escape the library itself names (set --glass-tint-strength:0% on the paper search-results surface) — a token re-point on glass-ui's OWN axis, NOT a !important or a hand-rolled background. Prefer waiting for the ask; the M plan should pin which of the two paths ships.
findings.wave_hint: M.W5 (consume the resolved overlay surface; book the ask at M.W0)

findings.title: Paper rounding is a hand-rolled scatter (0.75rem / 0.375rem / 0.25rem / 3px / 1px / calc(--radius-2px) / calc(--radius-4px)), not a system — critique #2
findings.evidence: critique #2 (borders not properly rounded; near-square corners); grep of src/components/paper shows: PaperView.vue:522,640 (0.75rem, 0.375rem), :590 (50%), :624 (8px), :497 (0 1px 1px 0); PaperSidebar.vue:162,193 (0.75rem, 0.25rem); PaperSearch.vue:52,93,113,128,144 (calc(var(--radius)-2px), 3px, calc(--radius-4px)); PaperArticleWindow.vue:183 (0.75rem); MobileFloatingToc.vue:243,340 (0.25rem, 0.375rem)
findings.current_state: Eleven distinct radius values across the paper pane, mixing raw px, raw rem, percentages, and two different calc(var(--radius)-N) offsets. There is no rounding scale — each surface picks its own corner, so nested surfaces (field inside wrap inside card) do not share a coherent concentric-radius relationship, which reads as the 'not properly rounded' incongruence in the critique.
findings.proposed: Adopt a rounding system anchored on glass-ui's --radius token: define the paper's nested-radius relationship as a small ladder (card = --radius-lg, in-card chrome = --radius, control = --radius-sm) and replace every raw px/rem literal with a token rung. Where glass-ui exposes a radius scale, consume it; where it doesn't, derive the rungs once from --radius (concentric inset: child-radius = parent-radius - parent-padding). This is the same single-source discipline as M's glass/colour/type ladders applied to the geometry axis. No magic numbers.
findings.wave_hint: M.W5 (the rounding system rides the glass-depth adoption wave)

findings.title: The .cartoon-card register on the paper article + sidebar is now an EXPLICIT user critique (#1 not-glassy) — resolve B6-08's open question toward the depth ladder for the SIDEBAR (article-sheet may stay)
findings.evidence: critique #1 (surfaces not glassy, cartoon-stamp cards); live/live-paper.jpeg (article + sidebar both render the 2px-border hard-offset-shadow stamp); PaperView.vue:522-529 (.paper-article { border:2px solid; box-shadow:3px 3px 0px 0px; background:var(--card) }); PaperSidebar.vue:163-166 (identical stamp on .sidebar-nav); contrast: MobileFloatingToc.vue:110 glass-resting, PaperView.vue:393 overlay-page glass-wash — the floating chrome IS glass, the structural cards are cartoon (prior B6-08); M-design-language.md:62 currently asserts paper article+sidebar STAY BAND 0 cartoon as deliberate metaphor
findings.current_state: The prior B6-08 left this as an open design question (keep cartoon as 'sheet on a desk' vs migrate to glass) and M-design-language §1.3 chose KEEP for both article and sidebar. The live critique #1 shows the user reads the cartoon-stamp as a defect ('not glassy'), and the pane already mixes two surface languages (glass floating chrome + cartoon structural frames). The article-as-document-sheet metaphor is defensible (reading surface = solid sheet), but the SIDEBAR is navigational chrome and reads incongruously stamped next to the glass mobile TOC.
findings.proposed: Split the decision per B6-08 recommendation (b): keep the ARTICLE as the deliberate solid document sheet (the one cartoon accent, M §1.5 proportion — a sheet on a desk is the correct reading-surface metaphor), but migrate the SIDEBAR TOC (.sidebar-nav) onto BAND 1 glass-resting so the left rail reads as floating navigational glass, matching the mobile TOC's glass-resting. Re-word M-design-language.md:62 to encode this asymmetry explicitly (article=solid-sheet accent; sidebar=glass chrome) so the surface story is documented, not ad hoc. Deletes the sidebar's hand-rolled 2px-border/offset-shadow recipe in favour of the rung (the rung owns the material — inv-33).

findings.title: Hero title is a raw text-4xl, not the φ-display/Fraunces tier — re-affirm B6-01 with the bump-landed reality
findings.evidence: live/live-paper.jpeg (title reads as a modest centered heading dwarfed by whitespace, not a poster hero); PaperView.vue:354-356 (h1 cm-serif text-4xl ... md:text-[3.25rem]); the ℱ glyph is the only Fraunces reach; M-design-language.md:88,100 confirms zero consumers of text-display*/text-hero in src/, Fraunces vendored+dead except .fourier-f
findings.current_state: Identical to prior B6-01 but now confirmed against the live bumped build: glass-ui 4.0's φ-ladder (text-display-2..3, --font-display=Fraunces via theme/bridges.css:67) ships and is consumed nowhere; the masthead is a hand-tuned Tailwind rung in Computer Modern, the display voice carries only one glyph.
findings.proposed:
Promote the title into text-display-3/text-display-2 (φ-fluid clamp, text-wrap:balance retires the hardcoded
), driving the Fraunces display voice across the whole title not just the ℱ; bind --font-stack-display through the consumer boundary so the bump can't shadow it; reconcile the two ℱ sizes onto a shared --fourier-f-size. Pure adoption of shipped tokens. Hero ambition bounded to display-3/4 (reading surface, not poster) per M §2.5.

findings.title: No hero entrance + no scroll-driven section reveal — re-affirm B6-02/B6-03 with the once-discipline + reading-primacy guardrails the live virtual window demands
findings.evidence: PaperView.vue:352-358 (header has no entrance transition); grep data-scroll-reveal/useStaggerReveal in src = 0; the virtual window mounts/unmounts sections (PaperView.vue:67-85, overscan 240/720) and useScrollNavigation teleports far jumps — a naive [data-scroll-reveal] view() recipe re-fires on every warm-window re-entry (flicker); M-motion-architecture.md §5.1-§5.2 already plan the char-stagger + header-only reveal
findings.current_state: The prime hero+scroll surface in the app has zero entrance choreography and zero scroll reveal, exactly as M-motion-architecture §5 plans to fix at M.W10. The load-bearing hazard is the virtualized scroller: the shipped glass-ui recipe has no cross-remount latch (the composable's once option doesn't cover the CSS recipe), so the reveal must be header-only and keyed by stable section id.
findings.proposed: Adopt as M.W10 already specifies: PRM-gated ONCE char-stagger on the title only (book useCharStagger/SplitChars; hand-roll scoped to the hero, keyed in a Set<string> so the virtual remount never re-fires; total ≤600ms); scroll reveal on chapter HEADERS only (never body — reading primacy), latched by section id against the remount churn; book the data-scroll-reveal once-discipline ask to glass-ui. The teleport stable-frame loop stays EXEMPT and must never carry a reveal. No new infra — pure adoption of the shipped recipes under the proportion ceiling.
findings.wave_hint: M.W10 (scroll heroes); the SplitChars + once-discipline asks book at M.W0

findings.title: The 13-hue section palette + ℱ signature reach the hero/dividers/refs as zero pops — re-affirm B6-05/B6-06/B6-07/B6-09 against the colourful-pops directive
findings.evidence: live/live-paper.jpeg (the masthead, the section-divider, the cross-refs all read monochrome; the section palette only colours TOC active states); --section-color-0..12 consumed at PaperSidebar.vue:77,96,112 only; .paper-ref is a single --primary dashed pink; the only math signature is .fourier-f (PaperView.vue:356 / PaperArticleWindow.vue:208, two different sizes 1.35em vs 1.1em)
findings.current_state: A rich, accessible, mathematically-indexed colour system used at ~40% of its reach — the title is grey, cross-refs are one global pink, the scroll-progress bar is --primary-only, dividers are one colour, and the ℱ brand glyph is static + size-inconsistent. The colourful-audacious-pops directive is unmet on the prime reading surface.
findings.proposed: Within proportion, reading-respecting (M §3.5 ≤8% mix on chrome, never body prose): tint .paper-ref by the TARGET section's hue (semantic wayfinding pop); tint the scroll-progress bar by the active section hue (the booked --scroll-progress-color knob, 1-line); draw the hero rule + a section-marker epicycle glyph from --section-color-{i}; reconcile the two ℱ sizes onto --fourier-f-size and give it a one-shot PRM-gated epicycle-settle as the signature. All accent-on-chrome, single-sourced from value.js per M.W7. This consumes the latent palette into the coherent wayfinding language the directive asks for.
findings.wave_hint: M.W7 (colour + math/grid chrome); the section-marker glyph consumes the 5 dead per-page Fourier-path assets

findings.title: Three divergent TOC renderings (desktop sidebar / mobile inline / mobile floating) with different type primitives + sizes — consolidate onto shared TOC tokens
findings.evidence: PaperSidebar.vue (cm-serif text-base links, fira-code 0.72rem numbers); PaperView.vue:361-377 (mobile inline TOC uses glass-ui Button variant=link, text-sm); MobileFloatingToc.vue (cm-serif text-base) — three renderings of the same data, three type treatments; the mobile inline list reads lighter/smaller than the floating TOC that replaces it on scroll
findings.current_state: Functional but inconsistent (prior B6-10). The scroll transition from inline TOC to floating TOC is not seamless because the two use different link primitives and sizes; the desktop sidebar is a third register.
findings.proposed: Unify the three onto shared --toc-link-size / --toc-number-size tokens, cm-serif links and fira-code numbers everywhere, so the inline→floating swap is seamless and the desktop rail matches. Pure token consolidation — composes with the rounding system (B6H-03) and the sidebar-glass migration (B6H-04). Net code decrease.

findings.title: Paper vertical rhythm is hand-tuned magic numbers (mb-10/lg:mb-20, mb-14, 1.25rem 1rem, 0.28rem 0.625rem) not on the φ ladder — hero/section spacing only
findings.evidence: PaperView.vue:352 (mb-10 lg:mb-20), :361 (mb-14), :526 (padding 1.25rem 1rem), PaperSidebar.vue:226 (0.28rem 0.625rem), PaperArticleWindow.vue:167 (--deferred-section-size:1200px); glass-ui ships --space-phi-* + --type-leading-* the paper doesn't reference
findings.current_state: Works visually but the rhythm is a collection of tuned values, not systematic (prior B6-12). The body line-height (1.8) is already good for reading and must stay.
findings.proposed: Migrate the HERO BAND + section-demarcation spacing onto the φ/leading ladder (hero gap derived from --type-title, section gap a leading-multiple); leave proven body metrics untouched. Targeted, not a blanket rewrite — the audacious-typography directive wants the hero rhythm systematic, not the body re-tuned.

findings.title: PaperView reading-progress hand-rolls the @supports gate + manual rAF — adopt useScrollProgress as the sole feature-detected fallback
findings.evidence: PaperView.vue:159-185 (writeProgress/onProgressScroll/armProgressFallback behind a hand-rolled CSS.supports('animation-timeline','scroll()') gate); M-motion-architecture.md §2 row 9 + §5.3 already plan this retirement
findings.current_state: The dual-path single-writer is correct in spirit and exemplary engineering, but the @supports gate logic is fourier-local rather than the shipped composable's. M-motion-architecture already schedules retiring the hand-rolled gate for useScrollProgress.
findings.proposed: Adopt glass-ui's useScrollProgress as the sole Layer-2 fallback (the .scroll-progress CSS recipe stays primary), deleting the fourier-local @supports gate + manual rAF so the dual-path decision lives in the platform. Re-affirm the M.W9 plan; no behavior change, just single-source the gate.

glassui_asks.name: overlay-band dark-substrate opt-out (--glass-backdrop:dark honoured by the overlay self-darken)
glassui_asks.what: glass-ui 4.0 ladder.css:200-204 darkens the floating/overlay band UNCONDITIONALLY (it cannot distinguish an explicit dark-substrate consumer from the :root dark default because style queries don't self-match). Provide a non-per-surface opt-out so a known-dark app keeps the pristine translucent plate without setting --glass-tint-strength:0% on every floating surface (e.g. honour an ancestor --glass-backdrop:dark, or a --glass-overlay-adaptive:off escape).
glassui_asks.why: The paper search dropdown (and the nav dropdown, critique #5/#8) compose glass-floating and inherit the unwanted darken on fourier's dark substrate, reading as the 'darkened/wrong glass' the user reports. inv-16: fourier consumes, never writes glass-ui — this is the correct root-cause owner, not a fourier !important workaround. Book to glass-ui BB W-CROSSREPO-ASKS.

glassui_asks.name: rounded .focus-ring as the default field-focus affordance + Input docs
glassui_asks.what: Confirm the shipped .focus-ring recipe (the --focus-ring-shadow/--focus-ring-width radius-inheriting box-shadow ring) is the canonical field-focus primitive and document composing it on a custom inline-icon field, OR confirm the <Input> primitive carries it by default. Ensure no UA :focus-visible rectangular outline leaks when a consumer sets input{outline:none} inside a rounded wrap.
glassui_asks.why: The paper search square+offset ring (critique #8) is fourier opting out of this recipe with a bespoke raw <input>; the fix is fourier adoption, but the platform contract (which recipe, on the field vs the wrap, radius-inheriting) needs to be the documented single source so every consumer's field-focus is a rounded glass ring. Book as the adoption-reference ask alongside B6H-01.

open_questions: B6-08 surface story, now half-resolved by critique #1: the article-as-solid-document-sheet is a defensible deliberate accent, but does the user want the sidebar TOC migrated to glass (B6H-04 recommends yes) or the WHOLE paper pane glassified? The critique says 'surfaces not glassy' broadly — confirm whether the article sheet stays solid as the one cartoon accent (M §1.5 proportion) or also goes glass.

For B6H-02: ship path A (wait for the glass-ui overlay-band opt-out ask) vs path B (interim --glass-tint-strength:0% on the paper search-results surface now)? The interim is a token re-point on glass-ui's own axis (not a workaround), but it must carry a kill-date = the ask landing.

Hero ambition (carried from B6 open-Q): text-display-3 (~68px, restraint on a reading surface) vs text-display-2 — confirm the paper masthead is a distinct above-the-fold band warranting the larger rung, or stay display-3/4.

Is the search field the glass-ui <Input> primitive (cleanest, but the inline Search-icon + Maximize2/X expand-clear affordances may not fit its slot model) or a custom field that composes .focus-ring? This decides whether B6H-01 is a component swap or a class adoption.

B7.dimension: B7 — PER-PANE: /demo/shape-extractor + /morph (FourierShapeExtractor.vue, FourierMorphDemo.vue, MorphPhaseConfig.vue, HarmonicLevelGrid.vue, MorphShapePreview.vue)
B7.verdict: The /demo/shape-extractor pane is a Playwright-harvesting internal tool with zero design application — it carries raw inline styles (padding: 2rem, border: 1px solid #ccc), no glass surfaces, no rounding tokens, and no hierarchy. The /morph pane (FourierMorphDemo + sub-components) carries three .cartoon-card shim instances, zero Configurator chassis, hardcoded #60a5fa blue tokens, variant="outline" preset buttons with no idle fill, and a hand-rolled rAF animation engine that M.W9 is already planned to retire. The user's 8 live critiques map directly onto this pane: surfaces not glassy (cartoon-card shim × 3), no rounding system (hand-rolled border-radius literals throughout), no idle button paint (variant="outline" preset grid cells invisible at rest), underline tabs (M.W1 migration chose underline, user wants pill/glass), and the step/phase motion pipeline is unencapsulated (three separately-timed MorphPhaseConfig cards with no pipeline framing). No alpha-class (glass-ui-owned) regressions are attributable solely to the morph pane. All findings are beta (fourier adoption gaps) or gamma (M.W1 bump residue), with one plan finding for the extractor tool itself.

findings.title: cartoon-card shim × 3 on morph pane — zero glass depth (critique 1)
findings.evidence: live-morph.jpeg: MorphPhaseConfig cards (3 instances), HarmonicLevelGrid, MorphShapePreview morph-button all render as offset-stamp cartoon-surface over --card opaque fill. Source: MorphPhaseConfig.vue:2 `class="cartoon-card config-card"`, HarmonicLevelGrid.vue:2 `class="cartoon-card levels-card"`, MorphShapePreview.vue:4 `class="morph-button cartoon-card"`. web/src/style.css:107 @utility cartoon-card shim maps to cartoon-surface + var(--card) — opaque paper, not glass.
findings.current_state: Three morph sub-components apply .cartoon-card directly. The shim defined at web/src/style.css:107-111 reinstates the D.W4 dead-class recipe (cartoon-surface + opaque --card background). The morph preview button is styled identically — a paper sticker, not a glass surface.
findings.proposed: M.W5: Delete the .cartoon-card @utility shim from style.css. Replace the three sites with the glass depth ladder: MorphPhaseConfig cards → glass-wash (BAND 1 in-flow instrument panels, the ambient unfocused rung); HarmonicLevelGrid → glass-wash (same band, wider card); MorphShapePreview morph-button → glass-resting (BAND 1 focused — the primary interactive surface deserves the canonical rung). Each site uses <Card surface="cartoon"> ONLY if the cartoon register is genuinely intended; for instrument panels it is not. The shim exit is the M.W5 close-gate item.

findings.title: Morph phase cards: hand-rolled rounding literals, no --radius-* tokens (critique 2)
findings.evidence: MorphPhaseConfig.vue (scoped style): .num-input border-radius: 0.375rem, .easing-preview width/height literals. HarmonicLevelGrid.vue: .grid-cell border-radius: 0.5rem, .level-input border-radius: 0.375rem. MorphShapePreview.vue: .morph-button has border-radius inherited only from cartoon-card. FourierMorphDemo.vue: .btn-export border-radius: 0.5rem, .btn-reset border-radius: 0.5rem — all hardcoded, not reading --radius-* tokens. live-morph.jpeg shows near-square number inputs and nearly-square phase cards.
findings.current_state: All radius values are hardcoded rem literals scattered across four scoped style blocks. The glass-ui 4.0 token system ships --radius-sm / --radius-md / --radius-lg / --radius-full; none of these are consumed anywhere in the morph pane.
findings.proposed: M.W5: Replace all hardcoded border-radius literals in the morph pane with the canonical --radius-* tokens: .num-input / .level-input → border-radius: var(--radius-sm); .grid-cell → border-radius: var(--radius-md); .morph-button → border-radius: var(--radius-lg); export/reset buttons → border-radius: var(--radius-md). The glass-resting / glass-wash surface classes already carry position: relative and their own rounding via the ladder — the card wrapper radius comes from the Configurator chassis once M.W8 migrates the pane.

findings.title: Morph pane: no Configurator chassis — hand-rolled .config-grid + .config-card-title hierarchy (critique 4)
findings.evidence: FourierMorphDemo.vue:22-55: .config-grid (3-column grid, hand-rolled), each MorphPhaseConfig titled with .config-card-title (h3 + font-family: var(--font-serif), @apply text-lg). HarmonicLevelGrid.vue:149-155: .card-title (h3 serif). No Configurator / ConfiguratorLayer / ConfiguratorRow anywhere in the morph pane. M.W8 explicitly targets `.config-grid` (morph) for Configurator migration. DEC-2 (emphatic — controls left) is wholly unaddressed.
findings.current_state: The morph pane is a hand-rolled stack of cartoon-card blocks with h3 titles — exactly the flat undifferentiated mimic that inv-33 (design-system-single-source) forbids. Controls are not on an asideSide='left' authoring rail. The three phase-config cards read as siblings without any pipeline framing or section hierarchy.
findings.proposed: M.W8: Replace .config-grid + MorphPhaseConfig h3 + HarmonicLevelGrid .card-title with a single Configurator chassis: the three phase cards become ConfiguratorLayer sections (Settle Out / Morph / Settle In) inside one Configurator with asideSide='left' and :dividers. The slider + easing select per phase become ConfiguratorRow items. HarmonicLevelGrid migrates to its own ConfiguratorLayer section (Harmonic Levels, Low/High rows). Titles come from the .configurator-section-label register — the √φ subheading, not a free-standing h3. The morph-button preview stage anchors the BAND 0 bare-math substrate (no instrument surface on it). The export/reset row pins to the Configurator footer slot.

findings.title: variant='outline' grid-cell buttons: no idle fill — invisible at rest (critique 6)
findings.evidence: HarmonicLevelGrid.vue:54-65: each harmonic-level thumbnail uses `<Button variant="outline">` with class .grid-cell. The .grid-cell style at lines 228-249 sets background: var(--card) and border: 1.5px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--foreground) 12%, transparent) — a near-invisible hairline on the card background. user-critique/09 (preset-pill analogue) + live-morph.jpeg (harmonic grid thumbnails): the level cells are visually bare with no idle affordance, only an accent border on hover/active/is-bound states.
findings.current_state: The 12% foreground hairline border on var(--card) background renders as near-invisible at rest on both light and dark themes. The user's critique 6 (buttons not visible when not hovered) applies directly to these cells. The .is-bound state uses hardcoded #60a5fa (HarmonicLevelGrid.vue:257) rather than a token — the semantic is 'low/high bound marker' but it reads as an arbitrary blue.
findings.proposed: M.W8: Migrate the harmonic grid cells to a glass-wash idle surface with a 1px --glass-border-wash edge — they are BAND 1 in-flow instruments (selectable harmonic preview thumbnails), not ghost buttons. The active cell uses glass-resting with --accent-red accent border (already set at line 251-254). The is-bound cell uses the route accent (--route-accent / M.W7 OKLCH ramp, the chebyshev section color) — not hardcoded blue. Adopt a subtle scale(1.04) + glass-resting entry on hover via the glass-ui transition tokens, not hand-rolled transform 0.1s ease.

findings.title: M.W1 migration chose variant='underline' for SegmentedTabs — user reversal: tabs must be pill/glass (critique 7)
findings.evidence: VisualizationView.vue:182 `<SegmentedTabs variant="underline"`, GalleryView.vue:223 `<SegmentedTabs variant="underline"`, EquationView.vue:188 `<SegmentedTabs variant="underline"`. user-critique/10-tabs-should-be-glass.png shows the underline hairline rendering. CRITIQUE.md §7: 'The M.W1 migration chose variant="underline" to match the retired UnderlineTabs; the user reverses this → glass.' Glass-ui 4.0 segmented-tabs.css: PILL is the DEFAULT and is explicitly labeled 'THE GLASS MATERIAL' — the quiet-tier track + floating-tier active indicator, glide+squish animation. UNDERLINE is labeled 'THE PAPER MATERIAL' (no plate, no blur, a 2px hairline).
findings.current_state: The M.W1 migration correctly replaced UnderlineTabs with SegmentedTabs but chose variant='underline' as a conservative 1:1 mapping. The user's explicit critique reverses this: the tabs should be the glass pill variant. The underline variant is the paper material — structurally wrong for a glass-first UI.
findings.proposed: M.W8 (or a W1 correction pass): Remove variant='underline' from all three SegmentedTabs call sites (VisualizationView.vue, GalleryView.vue, EquationView.vue) — omitting the prop defaults to 'pill', the glass material. The glass-ui 4.0 pill track uses --glass-bg-quiet + backdrop-filter + a floating-tier active indicator that glides+squishes on --spring-snappy. No additional styling needed; the component owns the material. The style.css tab-panel animation override (lines 82-96) may need review to confirm it does not conflict with the pill variant's indicator engine.

findings.title: FourierMorphDemo export/reset buttons: hand-rolled bespoke button styles duplicate glass-ui Button (critique 6)
findings.evidence: FourierMorphDemo.vue:72-79: `<Button variant='default' class='btn-export'>` and `<Button variant='outline' class='btn-reset'>` both override ALL button styling via scoped .btn-export / .btn-reset rules (background: var(--foreground); color: var(--background); transition: transform opacity; border: 2px solid color-mix…). These scoped overrides nullify the glass-ui Button's own variant styles entirely. The export button has zero idle glass surface — it is a filled-foreground block. The reset button has a near-invisible border at rest (15% foreground opacity). CRITIQUE.md §6: buttons not visible when not hovered.
findings.current_state: The btn-export and btn-reset scoped styles are parallel re-implementations of Button semantics that inv-30 (platform-over-library) forbids. The export button should use a high-intent variant (solid or default) without override; the reset button should use variant='glass' or variant='ghost' with the glass-wash idle surface.

findings.title: Morph phase pipeline has no visual step-sequence framing — three equal cards with no pipeline motion
findings.evidence: FourierMorphDemo.vue:22-55: .config-grid renders three MorphPhaseConfig cards as grid siblings — Settle Out, Morph, Settle In — with no visual connector, no step indicator, and no pipeline framing. The morph animation itself fires these in a defined sequence (useFourierMorph.ts:morph phase logic), but the UI reads as three independent control panels. live-morph.jpeg confirms: three uniform brown cards in a row.
findings.current_state: The three-phase morph pipeline (settle-out → morph → settle-in) is a temporally ordered sequence — a pipeline — but the UI presents it as an unordered peer grid. findings.proposed: M.W8 + M.W9: In the Configurator chassis migration (B7-03), arrange the three phase sections as a VERTICAL pipeline list rather than a 3-column grid: numbered step labels (1 / 2 / 3) via the configurator-section-label register, with a thin --configurator-divider groove between steps (the :dividers prop). During animation, the active phase section lifts to glass-resting (the BAND 1 focused rung) while idle phases remain glass-wash — a purely CSS class swap driven by morph.phase.value. M.W9's useFourierPlayhead motion: when a phase becomes active, a spring-native highlight travels down the pipeline (keyframes.js SmoothProgress on the section border-left accent, --spring-snappy). This makes the three-stage sequence legible as a pipeline without any extra component — the Configurator chassis + the glass depth ladder do the work.

findings.title: useFourierMorph: hand-rolled rAF-based animation (keyframes.js Animation used but not the M.W9 unified architecture)

C2.dimension: C2 — Rounding system (unified --radius-* adoption + the rounded glass focus ring; critiques #2 not-rounded + #8 square/offset search focus)
C2.verdict: The rounding defect is TWO separable root classes, and the live #8 search ring is misdiagnosed if read as one thing. (1) ALPHA — glass-ui 4.0 ships NO `Input`/field primitive and NO rounded glass focus-ring recipe: it ships only the Tailwind `focus-visible:outline-2 / outline-offset-2 / outline-ring` utilities, which paint a SQUARE, OFFSET rectangular outline by construction (outline does not follow border-radius without an explicit `border-radius: inherit`, and `outline-offset:2px` pushes it OUTSIDE the field). That square offset ring IS critique #8 — it is the UA/utility outline, not a glass ring. The fourier-owned half is that `PaperSearch.vue` hand-rolls a raw `<input>` with NO focus-visible ring at all on the wrap, so the browser default focus outline leaks. (2) GAMMA/BETA — fourier's radius vocabulary is fragmented: across the search, sidebar, article, equation and gallery panes corners are authored as raw literals (`0.75rem`, `0.25rem`, `3px`, `1px`) and `calc(var(--radius) − 2px/−4px)` arithmetic (8px → reads near-square at the small search field = critique #2), NONE reading glass-ui 4.0's shipped semantic `--radius-{card,panel,input,control,field,pill}` alias family (`theme/radius.css`). The fix is a unified adoption sweep onto those aliases (NO new fourier token axis — glass-ui already owns the scale) PLUS a glass-ui ASK for a rounded glass focus-ring + a real `Input`/SearchField primitive. The container-owns-rounding principle (P5 KILLED-AS-PHANTOM) is CORRECT and my proposals honour it: outer containers round via `--radius-{card,panel}` + `overflow-hidden`; inner sections stay square by design. NO `!important`, NO shim, NO new primitive on the fourier side.

findings.title: The search field's focus ring is a SQUARE, OFFSET UA/utility outline — there is no rounded glass focus ring (critique #8)
findings.evidence: user-critique/11-search-offset-square.png (blue rectangular ring offset beyond the field's right edge, square corners on the rounded field); web/src/components/paper/search/PaperSearchInput.vue:37-46 (raw <input class="paper-search-input">, NOT a glass-ui primitive); web/src/components/paper/PaperSearch.vue:69-78 (.paper-search-input has outline:none + border:none) and :47-60 (the .paper-search-input-wrap carries ONLY a border-color shift on :focus-within — no ring); glass-ui ships no input focus-ring recipe, only utilities (node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/components.css: focus-visible:outline-2 / outline-offset-2 / outline-ring) which paint a square outline offset OUTSIDE the box.
findings.current_state: The wrap has no :focus-visible ring (only border-color), and the inner input suppresses its own outline; the blue square offset ring the user sees is the browser/utility default outline leaking on the focusable element. glass-ui 4.0 ships NO Input/field primitive (confirmed: no input/field/search component in dist/components or glass-ui/src/components) and NO rounded glass focus-ring — only the square outline-* utilities.
findings.proposed: Two arms. (β fourier-local, ship now) Retire the raw <input> + hand-rolled wrap onto a SINGLE focus-ring idiom: the focus ring lives on .paper-search-input-wrap (the rounded element), as a :focus-within ring that FOLLOWS the corner — `outline: 2px solid var(--ring); outline-offset: 2px; border-radius: inherit` on the wrap, mirroring the canonical fourier pattern already at style.css:136-143 (.sidebar-link:focus-visible et al.) — so the ring is rounded and clipped to the field, no offset rectangle. Resolve the wrap radius onto `--radius-input` (see C2-R2). (α glass-ui ASK) glass-ui ships a real `Input`/`SearchField` primitive carrying a rounded GLASS focus ring as a recipe (ring-follows-radius via box-shadow ring or outline+border-radius:inherit, glass-tinted not raw blue), so fourier consumes it instead of hand-rolling; until then the β arm is the no-legacy stop-gap (a ring recipe, not an !important override).
findings.wave_hint: M.W5 (fourier focus-ring adoption in the incongruence sweep) + glass-ui ASK booked at W0/W5

findings.title: Fourier authors radii as raw literals + calc() arithmetic, never the shipped --radius-* semantic aliases — corners read near-square (critique #2)
findings.evidence: user-critique/01-not-glassy-not-rounded.png + live/live-paper.jpeg (sidebar/search corners read square); PaperSearch.vue:52,113,128 (`calc(var(--radius) − 2px)`=8px, `calc(var(--radius) − 4px)`=6px, and :93,144 raw `3px`); PaperSidebar.vue:162 (`0.75rem`), :192 (`0.25rem`), :227 (`calc(var(--radius) − 2px)`); PaperArticleWindow.vue:183 (`0.75rem`), :197 (`9999px`); glass-ui ships the canonical scale at node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/theme/radius.css:15-51 (--radius-input/-card/-panel/-control/-field/-pill).
findings.current_state: No fourier surface reads the semantic --radius-* family. The search wrap subtracts 2px from --radius (10px→8px) producing the near-square small-field corner the user flagged; sidebar/article use bare `0.75rem`/`0.25rem`; action buttons/results use magic `3px`. The radius language is divergent per file with no single override point — a no-legacy violation (raw literals where a token exists).
findings.proposed: Unified adoption sweep (no new token axis — consume glass-ui's): the search field/wrap → `rounded-input` / `var(--radius-input)`; the inline results dropdown + sidebar/article panel shells → `rounded-panel` / `var(--radius-panel)`; data cards → `rounded-card`; result rows + small action buttons → `rounded-control` (retiring the magic `3px`/`calc(−4px)`); pills/avatars keep `rounded-pill`. DELETE every `calc(var(--radius) − Npx)` arithmetic and raw rem/px literal. This makes the radius scale a single source (glass-ui theme) with per-surface semantic intent, and the small-field corner reads correctly rounded because --radius-input resolves the full 10px, not 8px.
findings.wave_hint: M.W5 (the C2 incongruence sweep already books "raw radii→--radius-*" — this hardens it with the per-surface alias mapping)

findings.title: The floating search variant hard-zeros border-radius — a square field by literal, not by container clip
findings.evidence: web/src/components/paper/PaperSearch.vue:204-216 (`.paper-search--floating .paper-search-input-wrap { border:none; border-radius:0 }` and `.paper-search--floating .paper-search-input { border-radius:0 }`).
findings.current_state: In the floating (mobile-overlay) presentation the field is authored fully square via `border-radius:0`. This is a second, independent square-corner source distinct from the calc() arithmetic, and if the #11 crop is the floating variant the ring offset compounds with a flat 0-radius field. It is a hand-authored literal that bypasses the container-owns-rounding principle.
findings.proposed: Let the OUTER floating container own the radius (`--radius-panel` + `overflow-hidden`, the P5-affirmed container-owns idiom) and let the inner field inherit/round to `--radius-input` rather than forcing `0`. The square inner edge — if intended for a full-bleed overlay — should come from the container's clip, NOT a per-field `border-radius:0` literal. Removes the divergent zero-radius branch and unifies both variants onto the token family.

findings.title: Affirm container-owns-rounding as the fourier radius DOCTRINE (P5 is correctly KILLED-AS-PHANTOM — do not re-book inner-section rounding)
findings.evidence: docs/constellation/ADOPTION-ASKS.md:124,148,174 (glass-ui-P5-inner-rounding KILLED-AS-PHANTOM); docs/tranches/M/M.md §13:206 (M does not re-book P5); glass-ui Configurator.vue owns the radius at the container clip (`rounded-panel … overflow-hidden`); fourier's own canonical clip idiom is the model.
findings.current_state: The radius doctrine is implied but not stated as the governing principle for the W5 sweep. Without it codified, a future sweep risks re-introducing per-inner-section radii (the exact P5 phantom) or hand-rolling inner rounding.
findings.proposed: State the doctrine once in M.W5 design notes and enforce it in the sweep: the OUTER container rounds (semantic --radius-{card,panel,field} + `overflow-hidden` to clip children); inner sections / dividers / rows stay SQUARE by design and inherit the container's clip. No surface carries its own radius arithmetic. This is the no-legacy unification AND the standing guard against re-booking P5. It also resolves critique #2 systemically: cards read rounded because the container clips, not because each child guesses a radius.

glassui_asks.name: glass-ui-rounded-glass-focus-ring + Input/SearchField primitive
glassui_asks.what: glass-ui 4.0 ships NO Input/field/search component (confirmed absent in dist/components and src/components) and NO rounded glass focus-ring recipe — only the Tailwind utilities `focus-visible:outline-2 / outline-offset-2 / outline-ring`, which paint a SQUARE outline pushed OUTSIDE the box (outline does not follow border-radius, and offset:2px sits beyond the field). Ask: (a) ship a real `Input`/`SearchField` primitive consuming `--radius-input`, and (b) ship a rounded GLASS focus-ring recipe (ring follows the corner radius — either an inset/outset box-shadow ring or outline+`border-radius: inherit` — glass-tinted via --ring, not a raw blue UA rectangle) as the canonical focus affordance for fields and glass controls. fourier currently hand-rolls a raw <input> in PaperSearch.vue because no primitive exists.
glassui_asks.why: Critique #8 (search screen offset + square) roots in glass-ui's absence of a field primitive and rounded focus ring — it is glass-ui-owned (inv-16; fourier consumes, never an !important workaround). A single glass-ui focus-ring recipe fixes the square/offset ring across EVERY fourier field at the source, and the Input primitive lets fourier delete the hand-rolled search wrap entirely (the no-legacy win). Book to glass-ui BB W-CROSSREPO-ASKS with a kill-date = the glass-ui release that ships it; fourier rides the β :focus-within ring-follows-radius stop-gap (style.css:136 pattern) meanwhile, which is a recipe not an override.

open_questions: Is the #11 crop the SIDEBAR search variant (calc(--radius−2px)=8px outer, the square UA focus ring offset around it) or the FLOATING variant (border-radius:0, fully square)? The wrap shows a visible border so it reads as the sidebar variant — but PaperSearch.vue:204-216 zeros the floating radius, so both produce a square defect by different mechanisms. The W5 sweep must fix BOTH branches (C2-R1 ring + C2-R2 token + C2-R3 floating-zero).

Does the glass-ui BB tranche (ships 4.1.0) intend to ship a field primitive at all? The W-CROSSREPO-ASKS band (BB-AMENDMENT-crossrepo.md) currently books value.js/keyframes/speedtest asks but NO input/focus-ring ask — fourier must ADD the glass-ui-rounded-glass-focus-ring ask to its own ADOPTION-ASKS ledger and surface it to the maintainer (fourier writes only fourier-analysis/** + deploy/**, inv-16).

Should fourier's β focus-ring stop-gap use `outline + border-radius: inherit` (cheap, the existing style.css:136 pattern) or a box-shadow ring (truer glass, composites with the backdrop-filter)? Recommend outline+inherit now for parity with the codebase's one conformant pattern, switching to the glass-ui box-shadow recipe on adoption — kill-date = the primitive ships.

C3.dimension: C3 — Controls-LEFT authoring rail + DELETE desktop tabs (critique #3 + #4, DEC-2 emphatic): VisualizationView / EquationView / MorphView layout + the Configurator asideSide API + the mobile-tab affordance
C3.verdict: The controls-RIGHT regression (critique #4) and the leaking desktop tab affordance (critique #3) are BOTH live-confirmed and BOTH fourier-owned adoption/residue — zero glass-ui asks fall out of this charge. glass-ui 4.0's Configurator already ships `asideSide="left"` as a first-class, a11y-safe prop (grid col-start placement + border-side swap; DOM/tab order stays stage→aside — verified in useConfiguratorState-kiIlun8I.js and Configurator.vue.d.ts:25,70). The live failure has a precise mechanism: VisualizationView.vue:194 passes the chassis NO `aside-side` prop (defaults to `right` → controls pin RIGHT over a vast dead dot-grid, exactly the live-workspace.jpeg), and worse, the fourier-local `.viz-configurator` CSS at VisualizationView.vue:317-330 hand-redefines `grid-template-columns: minmax(0,1fr) minmax(...)` which DEFEATS the substrate's `asideSide` machinery at the root — the substrate flips columns via `lg:col-start-1/2` placement, not a redefined template, so even adding the prop would be overridden. The existing M.W8 plan (B2-01/B2-04) already names the asideSide flip + the 3 grid-override deletes, BUT under-specifies critique #3: the mobile `SegmentedTabs` bar (VisualizationView.vue:181-186, EquationView.vue:187-192) is wrapped in `lg:hidden` yet renders on desktop in the live capture — a parallel mobile-only state machine (`mobileView` ref + `panel-inactive` toggle) bolted onto a chassis that ALREADY collapses to single-column below lg and goes two-column at lg+, making the tab bar redundant scaffolding that must be DELETED, not merely desktop-hidden. The idiomatic transposition is subtractive: pass `aside-side="left"`, delete the grid overrides + the `:deep(.configurator-stage)` mobile patch + the entire mobileView/SegmentedTabs/panel-inactive apparatus, and let the chassis own the geometry on both axes. This HARDENS W8 from "flip + adopt glass tabs" to "flip + DELETE the mobile-tab state machine + let the void compose."

findings.title: Workspace controls pin RIGHT — Configurator gets no aside-side prop (DEC-2 violated at the call site)
findings.evidence: live/live-workspace.jpeg (controls panel pinned top-RIGHT over a vast dead dot-grid stage); user-critique #4 (emphatic); VisualizationView.vue:194 `<Configurator scroll-mode="auto" class="viz-configurator">` — NO aside-side prop; Configurator.vue.d.ts:70 default `asideSide="right"`
findings.current_state: The visualization workspace mounts the glass-ui Configurator with only `scroll-mode` + `class`. The chassis defaults `asideSide` to `right` (the inspector idiom), so the controls aside renders RIGHT and the canvas stage claims the LEFT — the exact inverse of DEC-2 (controls on the LEFT authoring rail). The CSS comment at VisualizationView.vue:293-295 even admits the migration flipped the prior bespoke controls-left+canvas-right grid.
findings.proposed: Pass `aside-side="left"` to the Configurator at VisualizationView.vue:194. glass-ui 4.0 implements this as pure grid-column placement (stage→`lg:col-start-2`, aside→`lg:col-start-1 lg:row-start-1`) plus a border-side swap (`lg:border-r lg:border-l-0`), with DOM/tab order unchanged (stage→aside) — no a11y regression (confirmed in useConfiguratorState-kiIlun8I.js). One prop, no shim, no !important. The aside becomes the LEFT authoring rail; the canvas stage claims the right/center void.

findings.title: Hand-rolled grid-template-columns override DEFEATS the asideSide machinery at the root
findings.evidence: VisualizationView.vue:322 `grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr) minmax(320px, 360px)` (+ :326 1280px, :329 1536px variants); useConfiguratorState-kiIlun8I.js — the substrate flips via `lg:col-start-1/2` placement, NOT a redefined template; M-design-language.md:231 (B2-01) names the 3 overrides for deletion
findings.current_state: `.viz-configurator` re-defines `grid-template-columns` at three breakpoints (1024/1280/1536px) with the stage as the 1fr first track and the aside as the fixed second track. Because the substrate's asideSide flip works by reassigning `col-start` (not by redefining the template), these host overrides silently override-and-pin the columns in inspector order — so even if C3-01's `aside-side="left"` prop were added, this CSS would keep the controls RIGHT. It is the deeper root of the regression: fourier is fighting the chassis it adopted.
findings.proposed: DELETE the three `grid-template-columns` override blocks (VisualizationView.vue:322,326,329) entirely. Express the aside width band through the chassis's own `aside-width` prop / `--configurator-aside-min`/`--configurator-aside-max` custom properties (Configurator.vue.d.ts:79) — e.g. `:aside-width="['360px','440px']"` or set the two CSS vars in the cascade for the responsive band. The chassis then owns BOTH the column geometry and the side. Net CSS decreases; the substrate is the single source of layout truth (inv-30/inv-33).

findings.title: Desktop tabs leak — the mobile-only Controls|Canvas SegmentedTabs renders on desktop (critique #3)
findings.evidence: live/live-workspace.jpeg (the `Controls | Canvas` underline tab bar visible at the top of a @1440 desktop capture); user-critique #3; VisualizationView.vue:181-186 (tab bar wrapped in `lg:hidden`) — the wrapper is `lg:hidden` yet the tabs render; EquationView.vue:187-192 (identical pattern)
findings.current_state: Both viz + equation views render a `Controls | Canvas` SegmentedTabs bar inside a `<div class="... lg:hidden">`. The intent is mobile-only, but the live desktop capture shows the bar present — a mobile affordance leaking onto desktop. The deeper issue is architectural, not a single broken utility: a parallel `mobileView` state machine (`ref<'controls'|'canvas'>`) + `panel-inactive` class toggles drive a tab-switch that DUPLICATES the responsibility the Configurator already discharges (it collapses to a single flex column below lg and is two-column at lg+). The tab bar is redundant scaffolding regardless of whether `lg:hidden` momentarily works.
findings.proposed:
DELETE the mobile-tab apparatus outright rather than merely hardening its desktop suppression: remove the `
` block, the `mobileView` ref, the `:class="{ 'panel-inactive': mobileView !== ... && !isDesktop }"` bindings, and the `.panel-inactive { display:none }` rule, in BOTH VisualizationView.vue and EquationView.vue. On mobile, drive controls↔canvas with the chassis's intrinsic single-column stack (controls aside then stage, scroll-revealed) OR — if a swap is still wanted on phones — let a single source-of-truth media affordance live INSIDE the chassis, not a parallel ref. Desktop shows controls-left rail + canvas claiming the stage with no tab toggle (compose-the-void). Removes a whole state machine; net code decreases (inv-3).

findings.title: The mobile `:deep(.configurator-stage)` flex patch is a symptom of fighting the chassis — retire it with the tab machine
findings.evidence: VisualizationView.vue:333-348 — the `@media (max-width:1023px)` block flips the chassis to `display:flex; flex-direction:column` and patches `:deep(.configurator-stage) { flex:1 1 0%; min-height:0 }` with a 12-line comment explaining the stage collapses to 0px; M-design-language.md:231 (B2-04) names the mobile :deep patch for deletion
findings.current_state: To make the canvas not collapse to ~4px on mobile, the host overrides the chassis to a flex column AND reaches through `:deep` into glass-ui's internal `.configurator-stage` cell to force it to grow. This is fourier re-implementing the chassis's own responsive collapse and then band-aiding the fallout — a classic fighting-the-substrate pattern (the same root as C3-02). It is also load-bearing ONLY because the mobile tab/`panel-inactive` machine hides one pane; once the chassis owns the single-column stack natively the patch loses its reason to exist.
findings.proposed: DELETE the `@media (max-width:1023px)` flex override + the `:deep(.configurator-stage)` patch (VisualizationView.vue:333-348). Let the chassis's native single-column collapse provide the mobile layout. If the canvas's absolutely-positioned `.canvas-container` (inset:0) needs intrinsic height in the chassis's stage cell, give the stage cell an aspect-ratio or a min-height token on the FOURIER stage wrapper (`.viz-panel-right`/`.canvas-stage`) — never by reaching into glass-ui internals with `:deep`. No `:deep` into substrate internals, no !important. Couple this deletion with C3-03 (same wave, same gesture).

findings.title: EquationView already orders controls-LEFT but never consumes the chassis — migrate preserving the rail
findings.evidence: EquationView.vue:194 `.eq-grid`; :338-350 `grid-template-columns: 360px 1fr` (1280→400px, 1536→440px) — the LEFT 360px track IS controls (correct side); EquationView.vue:13+188 the mobile SegmentedTabs; M-design-language.md:227 (C1-02) + M.md:84 (W8) name `.eq-grid` for Configurator migration
findings.current_state: The equation route uses a raw `.eq-grid` CSS grid with controls in the LEFT fixed track and the result pane in the 1fr right track — so critique #4 (controls-left) is ALREADY satisfied here geometrically, but it is hand-rolled, never consuming the Configurator chassis, and it carries the same redundant mobile-tab machine (C3-03) as the workspace. The W8 migration onto the chassis must NOT regress the side: the chassis defaults `asideSide="right"`, so a naive migration would FLIP equation controls to the right.
findings.proposed: When migrating `.eq-grid` onto `<Configurator>` + stacked `ConfiguratorLayer`s (Function/Controls/Coefficients in the aside, the result+convergence in the #stage slot), pass `aside-side="left"` to preserve the existing controls-left order — DEC-2 holds for equation too. Delete the `.eq-grid` grid-template-columns blocks (:339,349,350) and express the width band via `aside-width`. Delete the equation mobile-tab apparatus in lockstep with C3-03. The result: equation + workspace share ONE chassis instrument with the same left rail, the same width band tokens, the same intrinsic mobile collapse — one layout source.

findings.title: MorphView is single-column (no aside, no tabs) — confirm it does NOT grow a spurious left rail in the chassis migration
findings.evidence: FourierMorphDemo.vue:1-82 — single centered `.demo-page` (max-width:960px) with `.controls-section` stacked below the `MorphShapePreview` stage; :258-269 `.config-grid` (3-col phase cards); NO SegmentedTabs, NO left/right split; M.md:84 (W8) names `.config-grid` for the chassis
findings.current_state: The morph route is intentionally a single-column, stage-on-top + controls-below composition — it has no controls-left/right axis and no tab affordance, so critiques #3/#4 do not apply. W8 plans to migrate `.config-grid` (the 3 phase-config cards) onto `ConfiguratorLayer`s. Risk: a naive `<Configurator>` adoption would impose the stage|aside two-column grid and a spurious left rail where the design wants a centered single column.
findings.proposed: In W8, migrate ONLY the morph `.config-grid`'s three phase cards to `ConfiguratorLayer`s (Settle Out / Morph / Settle In) for the section-label + density + groove ladder — but keep the morph page's single-column stage-above-controls composition (do NOT impose the two-column stage|aside chassis here). If a Configurator wrapper is used, it must render single-column (the chassis is single-column below lg by design; pin it there for morph) so the centered demo voice is preserved. This is the per-route discrimination: viz/equation are two-pane stage|aside-left; morph is single-column. Document the distinction in the W8 plan so the migration is not mechanically uniform.

findings.title: `isDesktop` useMediaQuery + the mobileView ref are dead weight once the tab machine is deleted — sweep the script
findings.evidence: VisualizationView.vue:69-70 `const mobileView = ref(...); const isDesktop = useMediaQuery("(min-width: 1024px)")`; EquationView.vue:44-45 (identical); these feed only the `panel-inactive` toggle the C3-03 deletion removes
findings.current_state: Both views keep a `mobileView` ref and an `isDesktop` media-query whose ONLY consumers are the `panel-inactive` class bindings (the mobile tab machine). The `useMediaQuery` import + the refs are scaffolding for an affordance the user wants gone. Leaving them after the markup deletion would be dead code (inv-3 violation: no orphaned state).
findings.proposed: When C3-03 deletes the tab markup + `panel-inactive` bindings, also delete the now-orphaned `mobileView` ref and the `isDesktop` `useMediaQuery` (and the `useMediaQuery` import if no other consumer) from BOTH VisualizationView.vue and EquationView.vue. Verify with a grep that no other binding references them before deletion. Net script decreases; the layout becomes purely declarative over the chassis breakpoints (no imperative media state in the SFC). Couple to C3-03 as one atomic change.

open_questions: Live capture width ambiguity for critique #3: live-workspace.jpeg is labelled @1440 yet the `lg:hidden` mobile tab bar is visible. Either (a) the capture was actually taken at an effective viewport ≤1023px (browser chrome / devtools split), or (b) the Tailwind v4 `lg:hidden` utility is not compiling/applying in the bumped build. On the morph route (C3-06): does the user want the morph controls eventually moved into a left authoring rail for cross-route consistency with viz/equation, or is the centered single-column demo voice intentional and preserved? Mobile controls↔canvas behaviour after the tab machine is deleted (C3-03): is the intrinsic single-column scroll-stack (controls aside, then canvas stage, scrolled) acceptable on phones for the canvas-heavy workspace, or is a pane-swap genuinely needed on small screens? If a swap is still wanted, it should live as ONE chassis-internal affordance, not the parallel `mobileView` ref — confirm the desired mobile UX before deleting unconditionally.

C4.dimension: C4 — Tabs-as-glass (critique #7): the SegmentedTabs material across every fourier tab usage
C4.verdict: The M.W1 migration mechanically preserved the OLD look by choosing `variant="underline"` at all three SegmentedTabs sites (`VisualizationView.vue:182`, `GalleryView.vue:223`, `EquationView.vue:188`) — a verbatim port of the retired UnderlineTabs ink-rule. The user's critique #7 REVERSES that choice: tabs are to be GLASS. This is correct by the design language — `pill` is the glass-ui 4.0 DEFAULT and IS the glass material (the `--glass-bg-quiet` track + `--glass-bg-floating` indicator that glides+squishes on the calibrated snappy spring; `segmented-tabs.css:5-9,36-101`), whereas `underline` is explicitly "THE PAPER MATERIAL — NO plate, NO blur, NO track surface" (`segmented-tabs.css:11-13,234-235`). The user calls the underline result not-glass directly in `10-tabs-should-be-glass.png` (the bare ink rule under "Controls") and it is live on DESKTOP in `live-gallery.jpeg` (the Gallery|Drafts rule) and `live-workspace.jpeg`. ROOT CLASS: gamma — this is M.W1 bump residue: the migration chose underline to match what was being retired rather than to honour the design language; the fix is a one-token reversal to the glass DEFAULT (drop the prop, or `variant="pill"`), not a workaround. NO glass-ui change is required (the pill material ships and is correct) — the only glassui_ask is a thin desktop-strip cap that today only the responsive Select path reads. Two adjacent, higher-leverage transpositions surface: (a) the desktop Controls|Canvas pair (critique #3 / C3) is a mobile-only affordance (`lg:hidden`) — its glass-pill reskin must be scoped to mobile, never leaked to desktop where both panels show; and (b) fourier hand-rolls the glass-pill twice already (NotationPills, EquationModeToggle — bare `<button>` + `color-mix` `--pill-color`, the exact idle-paint gap of critique #6), so the true idiomatic close folds those onto the SAME SegmentedTabs pill engine. The glass pill is the one tab idiom; underline is retired from fourier's surface entirely. No M wave currently owns this reversal — it must be added to M.W8 (control-pane / tab composition).

findings.title: All 3 SegmentedTabs sites pinned to variant="underline" — reverse to the glass pill (the DEFAULT, the glass material)
findings.evidence: user-critique/10-tabs-should-be-glass.png (bare ink rule under "Controls", no glass track); live-gallery.jpeg (Gallery|Drafts underline, desktop); live-workspace.jpeg (Controls|Canvas underline). VisualizationView.vue:182, GalleryView.vue:223, EquationView.vue:188; glass-ui segmented-tabs.css:5-9 (pill=glass material, DEFAULT), :234-235 (underline=paper material, no blur/plate).
findings.current_state: M.W1 migrated UnderlineTabs→<SegmentedTabs variant="underline"> verbatim (M-bump-migration.md:31,62) to preserve the retired component's ink-rule look. All three sites carry the explicit underline prop. The user's critique #7 reverses this: tabs should be glass.
findings.proposed: Drop the `variant` prop entirely at all three sites so they render the glass-ui 4.0 DEFAULT `pill` material (the `--glass-bg-quiet` track + `--glass-bg-floating` gliding indicator on the `--spring-snappy`/`--tab-indicator-duration` clock — segmented-tabs.css:36-101,116). Equivalent to `variant="pill"` but states the idiom by absence (no-legacy: no leftover material flag to drift). Retire the underline material from fourier's surface entirely — there is no remaining fourier consumer of the paper ink-rule tab. This is the canonical no-legacy close: the glass pill IS the tab idiom; the underline was only ever a port of the thing being deleted.

findings.title: Gallery|Drafts tabs render underline on DESKTOP — the exact critique #7 surface (not a mobile affordance)

findings.title: Mobile Controls|Canvas glass-pill reskin must stay mobile-scoped — do not leak the strip to desktop (intersects C3)
findings.evidence: VisualizationView.vue:181 (`<div class="flex px-3 py-1 bg-background lg:hidden">`) + :182 SegmentedTabs; EquationView.vue:187-188 identical. live-workspace.jpeg shows the desktop critique still showing Controls|Canvas at the top-left — the audit must confirm this is the `lg:hidden` strip and that on true desktop both panels show controls-left (DEC-2 / C3), not a leaked tab.

Critique #3 flags that a tabs affordance is reading on desktop — the C4 reversal must not inadvertently surface it.

This keeps C4 (material) orthogonal to C3 (presence): the pill is glass everywhere it renders; it simply does not render on desktop. No new breakpoint logic; the existing `lg:hidden` is the boundary. Cross-reference the C3 finding for the desktop-layout (controls-left, no tabs) decision.

findings.title: NotationPills + EquationModeToggle hand-roll the glass pill (bare buttons + color-mix) — fold onto the SAME SegmentedTabs pill engine
findings.evidence: NotationPills.vue:24,43-45 (bare option buttons, `--pill-color` + `color-mix(in srgb, var(--pill-color) 12%, transparent)` idle-vs-active fill); EquationModeToggle.vue:2,16,26,65 (two `<Button>` + a `color-mix(... --foreground 8% ...)` active fill, no idle track). Prior audit D2-02 (findings-index.txt:355) confirms both re-implement SegmentedTabs and are never imported. Ties to critique #6 (no idle paint) and #7 (should be glass).
findings.current_state: fourier ships TWO hand-rolled segmented toggles that are conceptually the glass pill: a sigma/expanded mode toggle and the notation pill row. They re-derive the track+indicator by hand, miss the glass material entirely, and produce the bare-text/no-idle-paint look the user flags in critique #6.

NotationPills' per-option tint (trig/exp/polar hues) maps onto the pill via the `#option` scoped slot (SegmentedTabs.vue.d.ts:66-69 exposes `{option, active}`) driving the tonal-accent recipe (the M.W7 `accent-tone` `--tone` channel) on the active indicator — keeping the colour-pop while inheriting the glass track + gliding/squishing indicator + the calibrated spring. Single engine, single idiom across tabs + mode toggles + notation pills.

glassui_asks.name: SegmentedTabs responsive desktopOptions cap for the non-collapsing strip (LOW — optional)
glassui_asks.what: The `SegmentedTabsResponsive.desktopOptions` subset (SegmentedTabs.vue.d.ts:26-28) only applies on the responsive Select-collapse path (`responsive` set). The Gallery strip grows from 2 to 5 options in admin mode with no responsive cap; if a future need arises to show a desktop subset while keeping the full pill strip (no Select collapse), a `desktopOptions` honoured on the non-responsive pill path would help. C5.dimension: C5 — Button idle-paint + tonal-accent (critique #6): the preset pills, notation pills, mode toggle, basis-selector buttons, and dock toggle-buttons read as bare text with no idle affordance; the colour-pop accent system is hand-mixed ~57x with no single source.
C5.verdict: Critique #6 ("button options not visible when not hovered") is REAL and root-causes to TWO compounding gaps, neither a glass-ui-4.0 rendering bug. (gamma) The M.W1 migration left the preset/notation/basis pills on `variant="outline"` (glass-ui 4.0 resolves this to `bg-background border-input` — neutral-0 fill + neutral-4 border) painted ON a `.cartoon-card` whose `--card` is itself near-white: white-chip-on-white-panel with a faint grey hairline reads as no-paint at rest (screenshot 09 — every pill but the one active `x(π−x)` is bare text). The mode-toggle + basis-selector use `variant="ghost"` (`bg-transparent text-foreground/70`) which has ZERO idle fill by design. So at rest the pills are invisible; only :hover (neutral-3) and the hand-rolled `.is-active` tint paint anything. (beta+chronic) The ACTIVE/idle paint is hand-mixed: the same `color-mix(in srgb, <tone> 12%, transparent)` fill + `40%` edge + solid `ink` trio is re-derived ~57× (the prior D2-01 count; I confirm 33 fill-sites + 40 edge-sites across 18 components) with no glass-ui home — this IS the colour-pop system the user wants, quarantined into per-component scoped CSS, with A8-13's triple `!important` band-aid where the specificity graph collapsed. The fix is NOT a fourier idle-fill override and NOT `!important` — it is (1) a glass-ui `accent-tone` recipe (the booked ask, HARDEN with the live evidence + a kill-date) that mints `--accent-fill/-edge/-ink` from ONE `--tone` with contrast flooring, replacing all ~57 sites; (2) selecting an idle-paintED variant for the pills (a `tone`-armed pill that always paints a faint tonal chip, so EVERY option reads as a chip at rest, the active one merely deepens) — the pills become a tonal SegmentedTabs/chip-group, not bare `outline` buttons; (3) adopting glass-ui 4.0's already-shipped `--dock-active-{bg,color,scale,border,shadow}` cohort so the 7 hand-rolled `is-active` DockIconButton sites finally have backing paint (today `is-active` toggles a class with NO visual register — a toggled-on dock button looks idle). value.js 0.13 (sampleColorRamp shipped) is the mixing engine the recipe rides; the M.W7 OKLCH ramp feeds the per-route `--tone`. Two glass-ui asks (accent-tone, dockiconbutton-active register) book to BB W-CROSSREPO-ASKS; the dockiconbutton-active ask is now SCOPED-DOWN (the token cohort exists at 4.0 — the ask is the ergonomic `active`-prop sugar + default register, not the whole mechanism).

C6.dimension: C6 — Typography Audacity (Fraunces display voice, the φ-display ladder, KaTeX as a hero ladder member, the ℱ sans-clash fix)
C6.verdict: The single most under-realized axis against the user's "large & audacious" mandate, and it is the one charge with NO direct critique crop yet a damning live screenshot: the app has exactly ONE typographic moment of any scale (the paper hero "An Introduction to ℱourier Analysis"), and even that is broken — the ℱ ornament renders in Plus Jakarta SANS inside a Computer-Modern SERIF headline, a visible glitch in live-paper.jpeg and live-equation.jpeg. The φ-display ladder glass-ui 4.0 ships (text-hero, text-display-audacious through text-display, text-title, .text-pane-title) has ZERO consumers in web/src; Fraunces is vendored, fetched, and dead (zero consumers); gallery + equation + visualize pages carry NO h1 at all (confirmed in live-gallery.jpeg / live-workspace.jpeg — the most audacious type on those screens is a 14px tab label). KaTeX is a hand-tuned 1.1em multiplier divorced from the ladder, so the display math — the one place a math journal should SHOUT — reads at body scale. The §2 M-design-language spec is substantively correct and I HARDEN rather than re-derive it; my additions: (1) the ℱ-clash is app-WIDE (logo, paper hero, paper callout, gallery modal — 4 sites), not paper-only, so the fix is the shared utility not a per-site patch; (2) this charge is overwhelmingly root_class=beta (fourier adoption gap), with the ONE alpha being whether glass-ui exposes a serif-display slot vs the consumer overriding --font-display wholesale (book to BB); (3) the bump (gamma) risk is real — vue-tsc 3 not run, and the 4.0 bridge chain --font-display→--font-stack-display must be asserted post-bump. None of the 8 user crops target type directly, so every finding here is is_deferred=false but severity-capped at high (the user did not flag it this round) EXCEPT the ℱ-clash which IS visible in the live shots the user reviewed.

C7.dimension: C7 — colourful pops from icons (within proportion): one OKLCH icon-ramp via value.js 0.13 sampleColorRamp, per-route accents, contrast-floored, more-but-proportioned pops
C7.verdict: The M.W7 icon-rainbow colour system (M-design-language.md §3) is correctly conceived and survives the critique intact — but the live bump has DISSOLVED its central risk and the user critique ADDS a load-bearing new vector. (1) HARDENING: value.js 0.13.0 is now INSTALLED (node_modules @0.13.0) and ships sampleColorRamp/safeAccentColor/mixColorsN — the plan's `mixColorsN`-equal-weight interim + kill-date booking (§6.3) is STRUCK; M.W7 must author against sampleColorRamp({space:'oklch', hueMethod:'longer'}) from the start. Fourier today imports ONLY easings from value.js (easeInOutSine/timingFunctions) — zero colour functions; the colour authority is a dependency sitting unused. (2) CONFIRMED ROT: 4 duplicate spectrumColor copies (all sRGB-HSL (1-t)*300/85%/55%, none favicon-derived), the 117-line bespoke parser (cssVarToHex/hslToHex/rgbToHex), and the STATIC.rainbow Tailwind-400 twin (drift-guaranteed second 'icon palette') all verified live. (3) NEW from critique: the UI is demonstrably UNDER-POPPED — live-paper shows the entire chrome near-monochrome cream with the ONLY chroma being the magenta 'Introduction' heading + the violet logo mark; the six-colour favicon brand reaches almost no surface; the nav flattens all five distinctly-iconed routes onto ONE --viz-amber (AppHeader.vue:197,341) and amber is force-applied via an !important triple (FunctionInput.vue:251-253). The fix is the per-route --route-accent + contrast-floored tonal pops the plan already specifies, now URGENT and proportion-governed. Root: predominantly beta (fourier adoption gap — adopt the value.js colour authority + wire --route-accent + add proportioned pops); the only glass-ui-owned seam is accents composited OVER glass needing a glass-fill contrast target (W-ON-GLASS-FG, already booked in BB).

D1.dimension: D1 — glass-ui 4.0 idioms to adopt (critique grounding + concrete adoption sites)
D1.verdict: The eight user critiques resolve into three clean root classes. The most critical systemic gap is the unadopted glass depth ladder — fourier's 22-site `.cartoon-card` shim is a fourier-authored @utility (style.css:107) that recreates a paper-stamp surface glass-ui retired at C.W5; every content card reads as a sticker, not glass. The `Configurator asideSide="left"` prop is SHIPPED in glass-ui 4.0 (Configurator.vue.d.ts:70) but NOT passed in VisualizationView.vue (the grid-template-columns overrides in scoped CSS reorder columns manually while leaving the DOM in right-aside order — a layout shim, not adoption). The M.W1 migration chose `variant="underline"` on all three SegmentedTabs sites (VisualizationView:182, GalleryView:223, EquationView:188) reversing the user's glass-pill intent. The preset pill buttons in FunctionInput.vue (variant="outline") carry no idle tonal fill — they are bare outlines that only resolve on hover. The PaperSearch input uses a raw `:focus-within` border-color cross-fade (PaperSearch.vue:58) instead of the `.input-pill` class whose `:focus-visible` ring is the canonical glass-ui pattern. The dropdown darkening (critique 5) has a genuine alpha — glass-ui 4.0 ladder.css:200 makes `.glass-floating` and `.glass-overlay` unconditionally self-darken via `--glass-tint-ink` at `--glass-tint-strength-aa`; this is the correct library default for floating surfaces over unknown (possibly light) backgrounds, NOT a regression. The square/offset focus ring (critique 8) traces to the raw `outline` on the PaperSearch wrapper and raw `outline: 2px solid var(--ring)` in style.css:140 — both miss the `.input-pill:focus-visible` rounded box-shadow ring that glass-ui ships. Every critical finding has a no-legacy, shim-free idiomatic adoption path in M.W5 or M.W8.
