VisualizationView.vue:182, GalleryView.vue:223, EquationView.vue:188 all use variant='underline'. glass-ui 4.0 segmented-tabs.css documents: 'PILL (DEFAULT) — THE GLASS MATERIAL. The track rides --glass-bg-quiet + a hairline edge; the active indicator is the selected-reads-as-glass plate (--glass-bg-floating)'. The M.W1 migration from UnderlineTabs→SegmentedTabs(variant='underline') preserved the outgoing component's visual — a gamma residue. The user's critique 7 ('tabs should be GLASS not underline') explicitly reverses this choice.
findings.current_state: Three SegmentedTabs instances explicitly pass variant='underline', selecting the paper ink-hairline material (no track, no blur, no glass plate). The M.W1 migration chose underline to match the retired UnderlineTabs visual; the user reverses this — the glass pill (the DEFAULT variant) is the intended material.
findings.proposed: Drop variant='underline' on all three sites (or explicitly pass variant='pill'). The pill variant is the default; omitting the prop is the idiomatic form. The glass track (glass-bg-quiet backdrop-filter) and floating-tier indicator (glass-bg-floating) render automatically. The anchor-position glide + volume-preserving squish (--spring-snappy) ship with the component. The VisualizationView and EquationView mobile tab bars additionally carry class='lg:hidden' — the desktop layout fix (D1-04) must ship in the same wave so desktop shows both panels side-by-side (controls left) and the tab strip is truly mobile-only.

findings.title: Mobile tab bar visible on desktop: SegmentedTabs Controls|Canvas strip leaks beyond lg:hidden
findings.evidence: live/live-workspace.jpeg (Controls | Canvas tabs visible at 1440px desktop width, critique 3). VisualizationView.vue:181 wraps the SegmentedTabs in class='flex px-3 py-1 bg-background lg:hidden'. EquationView.vue:187 does the same. On desktop the Configurator asideSide layout (D1-02) renders both panels simultaneously — the mobile tab affordance must not show.
findings.current_state: The lg:hidden Tailwind utility should hide the strip above 1024px. The live screenshot shows it visible at 1440px, which means either the breakpoint is not applied (class merge issue with a scoped flex wrapper), the isDesktop reactive ref driving panel-inactive toggles is inverted, or the strip is showing due to a class precedence issue in the Tailwind v4 build.
findings.proposed: Verify the lg:hidden class reaches the rendered DOM on the 1024px+ breakpoint (check vue-tsc-3 build output and the compiled CSS). If the Configurator grid is restored and asideSide='left' is wired (D1-02), the mobile tab strip is definitionally not needed on desktop — enforce this with a single class='lg:hidden' at the wrapping div. The mobileView reactive ref (controlling panel-inactive) should only engage when !isDesktop. The isDesktop breakpoint logic (useMediaQuery) should match the Configurator's lg (1024px) threshold exactly.

findings.title: Preset pills have no idle tonal fill: ghost/outline buttons are invisible at rest (critique 6)
findings.evidence: user-critique/09-buttons-invisible-unhovered.png (Sawtooth / Triangle / |sin(x)| / Gaussian / Step / x² pills with no idle background). FunctionInput.vue:158 uses variant='outline' size='sm' class='preset-pill'. The active state in FunctionInput.vue:244 adds background + border-color only on .is-active. The is-active book in style.css:136 is scoped to sidebar/toc/gallery elements, not these preset pills.
findings.current_state: Preset buttons use variant='outline', which paints a border at rest but no background fill. The idle state renders as bare text-on-nothing with a thin border that is sub-perceptual on the dark glass background. The affordance is invisible until hover. The glass-ui 4.0 glass-btn idiom (.glass-btn[aria-pressed='true'] background: var(--surface-tint-10)) provides the idle tonal fill for the active/selected state — this pattern is unadopted on preset pills.
findings.proposed: Replace variant='outline' with variant='glass' (or a SegmentedTabs preset row within the Configurator's preset slot — the idiomatic M.W8 path). If kept as individual Button children, adopt the .glass-btn[aria-pressed='true'] idiom: the active pill reads surface-tint-10 background + surface-tint-25 border, the inactive pill reads glass-bg-wash with the glass-blur-wash backdrop-filter. The :aria-pressed binding already exists (FunctionInput.vue:162 class binding checks activePreset). The preset row belongs in the Configurator <template #presets> slot (the configurator-presets CSS partial already wires the chip gap and block-padding rhythm). Book glass-ui-dockiconbutton-active (the tonal idle fill ask) in ADOPTION-ASKS §11.

findings.title: Search input uses raw :focus-within border shift instead of .input-pill focus-visible ring: square + offset focus ring (critique 8)
findings.evidence: user-critique/11-search-offset-square.png (focus ring mis-positioned, square corners). PaperSearch.vue:47-60: .paper-search-input-wrap has border: 1.5px solid var(--border); border-radius: calc(var(--radius) - 2px); background: var(--background); and :focus-within { border-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--primary) 50%, transparent); } — a raw border-color shift, not a rounded box-shadow ring. PaperSearchInput.vue:40 uses a bare <input> with class='paper-search-input' + outline: none. GallerySearchBar.vue:46-53 uses a bare <input> with class='search-input ... outline-none'.
findings.current_state: The search inputs use a hand-rolled .paper-search-input-wrap wrapper with a raw :focus-within border-color cross-fade. No rounded focus ring is present — the browser's native outline (square by default) shows at some cascade positions, and the border-color shift on the wrapper can appear offset from the input itself. The glass-ui .input-pill:focus-visible rule (surfaces.css:257) ships the correct pattern: outline: none on the input itself + border-color: var(--color-accent-opaque) + box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px var(--color-accent, ...) on the same element, which renders as a rounded glass ring that follows the border-radius.
findings.proposed: Both PaperSearchInput and GallerySearchBar should replace the hand-rolled wrapper pattern with a container that composes .input-pill on the actual <input> element (or on the pill wrapper with the input inside via :focus-within mirroring the .input-pill:focus-visible box-shadow). The canonical path: the pill wrapper adds border-radius: var(--radius-pill), backdrop-filter: var(--control-surface-blur), background: var(--control-surface-bg), and the :focus-within { box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px var(--color-accent, ...) } mirrors .input-pill:focus-visible exactly. No raw outline anywhere. This is a beta adoption gap — glass-ui ships the idiom; fourier's hand-rolled wrapper does not use it.

findings.title: Dropdown/overlay darkening is the correct glass-ui 4.0 default, not a regression — BOOK as glass-ui ask only if over-darkened on dark substrate
findings.evidence: user-critique/08-dropdown-glass-darkened.png (nav dropdown flat opaque grey). glass-ui 4.0 ladder.css:200-204: ':where(.glass-floating, .glass-overlay) { --glass-tint-source: var(--glass-tint-ink); --glass-tint-strength: var(--glass-tint-strength-aa); --muted-foreground: var(--foreground); }' — the overlay band self-darkens UNCONDITIONALLY. This is intentional (the library's default-over-unknown-surface behaviour, documented). On a dark page substrate the darken is sub-perceptual (warm-ink over dark plate is a small shift); the AA strength is 18%.
findings.current_state: The DropdownMenu/Select content surfaces use .glass-floating (the overlay band), which now self-darkens unconditionally in glass-ui 4.0. On fourier's dark substrate (#0a0a0b or similar) the tint compounds into a visibly grayer plate than the prior glass-ui 3.x behaviour. The user reads it as 'oddly darkened'. This is NOT a fourier adoption gap — the glass-ui library INTENTIONALLY darkens overlay-band surfaces. A consumer who wants the pristine plate on a dark substrate sets --glass-tint-strength: 0% on the band or uses .glass-opaque.
findings.proposed: Root-cause audit: check whether fourier's page background is dark enough that the unconditional AA darken reads as a grey slab (the luminance floor). If yes, book as a glass-ui ask (W-CROSSREPO-ASKS): 'provide a --glass-tint-strength-dark token arm so dark-substrate consumers tune the overlay tint independently of the bright-substrate AA floor.' Do NOT add a fourier !important or --glass-tint-strength: 0% override — that would mask the library behaviour and create a maintenance seam. If the visual is acceptable on a correctly dark substrate (as documented), close this as a non-finding.

findings.title: Borders not rounded: raw radii and missing --radius-* token adoption on content cards
findings.evidence: user-critique/01-not-glassy-not-rounded-tabs-controls.png (near-square card corners). user-critique/11-search-offset-square.png (square focus ring). PaperSearch.vue:51: border-radius: calc(var(--radius) - 2px) — a one-off calc rather than --radius-card or --radius-pill. FunctionInput.vue:103: class includes 'rounded-lg' (a Tailwind literal, not a token). VisualizationView.vue cartoon-card sites use the shim's box-shadow but no explicit border-radius (relying on cartoon-surface's implicit geometry). GallerySearchBar.vue:148: border-radius: 0.5rem — a literal px/rem, not a token.
findings.current_state: Rounding is applied inconsistently: some sites use Tailwind rounded-* utilities (literal rem values), some use calc(var(--radius) - 2px), none use the canonical glass-ui --radius-card or --radius-pill tokens. The resulting cards appear near-square at the 4–8px literal radii used, failing the rounded-glass aesthetic.
findings.proposed: Adopt the glass-ui radius token family across all fourier surfaces. Content cards: border-radius: var(--radius-card). Search/input pills: border-radius: var(--radius-pill). The glass-card class already applies var(--radius-card) (surfaces.css:23) — sites adopting glass-card get correct rounding automatically. Remaining hand-rolled surfaces (search wrappers, filter panels) replace literal rems and calc() with the matching token. This is a one-pass sweep in M.W5 alongside the cartoon-card deletion.

findings.title: useSpecularTracking unadopted: no catch-light on BAND 1 glass over the bright math canvas
findings.evidence: live/live-workspace.jpeg (instrument panels are flat, no moving catch-light). glass-ui 4.0 ships useSpecularTracking (composables/glass/useSpecularTracking.d.ts): writes --mouse-x/--mouse-y on pointermove (rAF-coalesced, PRM-gated), the .glass-material::before recipe maps it to --specular-x/y and paints the travelling glow. No fourier component calls useSpecularTracking (grep of web/src returns 0 hits). The M-AMENDMENT-latest-and-BB.md §3 notes glass-ui BB's W-LIQUIDHOVER will ship a tier-root specular auto-arm that removes the per-consumer wire — but 4.0.0 (the live branch) still requires the composable.
findings.current_state: Zero fourier components wire useSpecularTracking. All glass surfaces render with a static catch-light at the centred 50% fallback (the CSS default when --mouse-x/y are unset). The instrument panels over the bright math canvas are the highest-priority site (the BAND 1 catch-light the M.W5 plan names).
findings.proposed: Wire useSpecularTracking on the primary BAND 1 instrument panels: VisualizationView's Configurator controls aside, EquationPanel.vue (the eq-panel glass-wash), and ConvergenceLegend.vue (legend-overlay glass-wash). Import from '@mkbabb/glass-ui/composables/glass'; bind specularStyle to :style on the host glass surface element; bind onPointerMove to @pointermove. When glass-ui BB ships W-LIQUIDHOVER (the tier-root auto-arm), delete the per-consumer wiring — the composable call becomes a no-op replaced by the CSS auto-arm. Book this deletion as a named wave-gate against BB's 4.1.0 publish.

findings.title: useTextHighlight unadopted: paper search and diff-viewer do not use the CSS Custom Highlight seam
findings.evidence: PaperSearchDropdown.vue:58 uses v-html='highlightFuzzy(resultLabel(r), search.query.value)' — an innerHTML-based fuzzy highlight (a JS DOM-string mutation). glass-ui 4.0 ships useTextHighlight (composables/motion/useTextHighlight.d.ts): drives a named CSS Custom Highlight reactively (setFromMatches(container, query, matcher)), imports from '@mkbabb/glass-ui/motion-core'. The M.md §4 M.W8 names useTextHighlight adoption; the M.md §4 M.W10 names the AtomDiff consumer. No fourier component imports from /motion-core (grep returns 0 hits).
findings.current_state: Text highlight is implemented via innerHTML/v-html string injection (the fuzzy highlightFuzzy function), coupling the highlight to a string-interpolation DOM update. The CSS Custom Highlight API (CSS.highlights registry) allows the same painting as a pure CSS ::highlight() rule with zero DOM mutation. useTextHighlight wraps this idiomatically with a supported flag PE floor.
findings.proposed: Replace the PaperSearchDropdown v-html highlight with useTextHighlight('paper-fuzzy-search'): call hl.setFromMatches(containerEl, query, fuzzyRangeMatcher) on each [query, results] change (watch), add a ::highlight(paper-fuzzy-search) CSS rule for the accent paint. The supported flag PE floor: when !hl.supported the component falls back to plain text (no innerHTML). The diff-viewer (M.W10 AtomDiff consumer) uses useTextHighlight('atom-diff') for the changed/added/removed range highlight. Import from '@mkbabb/glass-ui/motion-core' (the source-verified path per M-AMENDMENT).

findings.title: Scroll-driven CSS recipe (.scroll-progress + [data-scroll-reveal]) unadopted: paper scroller uses no compositor-safe scroll animation
findings.evidence: live/live-paper.jpeg (paper article, flat entry with no scroll reveals). glass-ui 4.0 ships scroll-driven.css: .scroll-progress (animation-timeline: scroll() — a 0..1 scaleX reading-progress bar) and [data-scroll-reveal] (animation-timeline: view() per-child fade+lift, no setTimeout cascade). No fourier component uses either class (grep returns 0 hits). The M.md M.W9 plans adoption of useScrollProgress/.scroll-progress + [data-scroll-reveal].
findings.current_state: The paper route has no scroll-linked animation. Section reveals, reading-progress, and parallax are absent. The M.W10 'scroll heroes' and M.W6 paper hero are planned but have zero CSS substrate today.
findings.proposed: Import scroll-driven.css via the glass-ui style index (already @imported in glass-ui's index.css — the fourier app imports glass-ui's full style index so scroll-driven.css is already in the cascade). Adopt at two sites in M.W9: (1) add .scroll-progress on a position: fixed reading-progress bar in PaperView.vue (the M.W6 W-BORDER-PROGRESS primitive, once BB ships, supersedes this with a value.js OKLCH fill); (2) add data-scroll-reveal on the paper section container so each section's ::before/.children fade+lift on scroll entry. The dual-path: when @supports (animation-timeline: view()) the CSS owns the animation; useStaggerReveal composable is the feature-detected fallback. Gate the whole block under prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference (already done in scroll-driven.css).

findings.title: View-Transition recipe (view-transition.css + gl-list-item) unadopted on gallery cards
findings.evidence: live/live-gallery.jpeg (gallery grid, static card layout). glass-ui 4.0 ships view-transition.css: ::view-transition-group(.gl-list-item) with spring-bouncy timing + slide-in/out for added/removed members. No fourier component uses view-transition-class: gl-list-item or view-transition-name: row-<id> (grep returns 0 hits). M.md M.W9 plans adoption of useViewTransition/view-transition.css.
findings.current_state: Gallery card additions/removals and sort reranks are instant DOM mutations. The View-Transitions API (document.startViewTransition) wraps the mutation so the browser geometry-morphs tracked elements. The glass-ui useViewTransition helper (importable from /motion-core) wraps the DOM mutation with the instant-update fallback when document.startViewTransition is absent.
findings.proposed: In GalleryView.vue, wrap sort/filter mutations in a glass-ui useViewTransition call. Add view-transition-class: gl-list-item and a unique view-transition-name: gallery-card-<slug> on each GalleryCard root. The view-transition.css is already in the cascade (see D1-11 note). Import useViewTransition from '@mkbabb/glass-ui/motion-core'. The instant-update fallback (synchronous mutate() when document.startViewTransition is absent) is the ≤ 20-LOC PE floor. Gate: prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference via the library's ::view-transition-group { animation: none !important } rule in view-transition.css.

findings.title: inert a11y attribute unadopted: background panels remain keyboard-reachable when visually inactive (mobile tab switch)
findings.evidence: VisualizationView.vue:197+219: panels are hidden via panel-inactive class (CSS visibility/opacity toggle) but not marked with inert. EquationView.vue:196+219: same pattern. The a11y inert attribute (WicG inert, Baseline Widely) removes a subtree from the accessibility tree and prevents focus reaching it. M.md M.W8 lists 'adopt inert a11y' as a named deliverable.
findings.current_state: The mobile tab switch (Controls|Canvas) hides the inactive panel visually via .panel-inactive CSS (likely display:none or opacity:0 + pointer-events:none) but the DOM subtree remains accessible to keyboard navigation and screen-readers unless it is also display:none. If panel-inactive uses only opacity/visibility, the inactive panel is reachable by Tab. The Configurator layout on desktop renders both panels simultaneously — inert is only needed on the explicitly-hidden mobile-inactive panel.
findings.proposed: Bind :inert='mobileView !== panel && !isDesktop' on each panel wrapper div in VisualizationView and EquationView. The inert attribute is a boolean HTML attribute (no value needed); Vue binds it as :inert='condition'. On desktop (isDesktop=true) never set inert (both panels are visible and interactive). On mobile, the inactive panel gets inert. This is a single-line bind per panel, no CSS change needed.

findings.title: ConfiguratorLayer hierarchy unadopted: eq-grid and config-grid are bespoke layout grids bypassing the Configurator chassis
findings.evidence: EquationView.vue:194 uses class='eq-grid' — a bespoke scoped CSS grid. MorphPhaseConfig.vue and MorphShapePreview.vue use .config-card (cartoon-card). The Configurator, ConfiguratorLayer, and ConfiguratorRow components (glass-ui/configurator) are imported in VisualizationView.vue but not in EquationView.vue or any morph component. M.md M.W8: 'Migrate .eq-grid (equation) + .config-grid (morph) onto Configurator + ConfiguratorLayer'.
findings.current_state: The equation pane uses a bespoke eq-grid layout (two-column grid with custom panel classes) and CollapsibleSection headers rather than ConfiguratorLayer/ConfiguratorRow. The morph pane uses cartoon-card config-card containers. Neither adopts the Configurator chassis, so the asideSide='left' layout, the configurator-section-label typography hierarchy, and the :dividers inter-row grooves are absent from these panes.
findings.proposed: Import Configurator, ConfiguratorLayer, ConfiguratorRow from '@mkbabb/glass-ui/configurator' in EquationView.vue, MorphView.vue. Replace eq-grid with <Configurator asideSide='left' :dividers>. Migrate each CollapsibleSection into a <ConfiguratorLayer>. Retire the bespoke eq-grid / config-grid CSS classes. The configurator-section-label CSS (configurator.css, already in the cascade) paints the section header register automatically. The preset row (PRESETS) moves to the <template #presets> slot (the configurator-presets CSS wires the chip gap). density='compact' as the ONE rhythm lever for tight morph rows.

findings.title: glass-menu-row / glass-menu-section unadopted: nav dropdown uses flat accent hover, not the glass-quiet hover-lift row
findings.evidence: user-critique/08-dropdown-glass-darkened.png (flat grey dropdown, no per-row glass lift). glass-ui 4.0 menu.css ships .glass-menu-row: transparent at rest, glass-quiet plate + --foreground color + translate(0, -1px) lift on hover/highlight. The menuItemVariants CVA default surface='glass' arm composes .glass-menu-row. If fourier's nav dropdown uses custom list items (not DropdownMenuItem), the glass-menu-row class is absent.
findings.current_state: The nav dropdown items' hover state appears as a flat opaque accent fill (the .interactive-item:hover fallback in utilities/base.css) rather than the glass-quiet hover-lift plate that .glass-menu-row paints. The glass-menu-section caption register (.glass-menu-section + .glass-menu-section-label) is also unadopted for any section labels in dropdowns.
findings.proposed: Ensure nav dropdown items use DropdownMenuItem (the reka-ui headless primitive wrapped by glass-ui's DropdownMenu) rather than bare <li>/<button> elements. DropdownMenuItem composes menuItemVariants CVA with surface='glass' by default, which emits the .glass-menu-row class. If the nav uses a custom structure, add class='glass-menu-row' to each interactive row. Section captions adopt .glass-menu-section + .glass-menu-section-label for the mono small-caps register.

findings.title: glass-ui BB W-LIQUIDHOVER specular auto-arm: book to ADOPTION-ASKS §11, consume at M.W1b
findings.evidence: M-AMENDMENT-latest-and-BB.md §3: 'W-LIQUIDHOVER: the tier-root specular auto-arm (--mouse-x/y auto-written; useSpecularTracking already ships) — STRIKES the M useSpecular ask — M.W5 consumes the auto-arm for the BAND-1-over-canvas catch-light (zero per-consumer wiring)'. glass-ui 4.0 currently requires the per-consumer useSpecularTracking wire (D1-09); 4.1.0 (BB close) auto-arms it at the tier root.
findings.current_state: At glass-ui 4.0.0 (the live m/w1-bump-migration branch), useSpecularTracking must be called per glass surface. At glass-ui 4.1.0 (BB's fold-all close), W-LIQUIDHOVER ships the auto-arm — every .glass-material surface gets the catch-light automatically. The M.W5 plan names this; the adoption-asks ledger has not recorded it as a concrete ask entry.
findings.proposed: Book to ADOPTION-ASKS.md §11 as 'glass-ui-liquidhover-auto-arm: W-LIQUIDHOVER tier-root specular auto-arm — consume at M.W1b (glass-ui ^4.1.0); removes all per-consumer useSpecularTracking wires added in M.W5 (delete them at M.W1b)'. The M.W5 per-consumer wires (D1-09) are the interim step; W-LIQUIDHOVER is the terminal form. The kill-date is glass-ui BB 4.1.0 publish.

findings.title: glass-ui BB W-ON-GLASS-FG contrast register: book to ADOPTION-ASKS §11 for BAND 1 over bright canvas
findings.evidence: M-AMENDMENT-latest-and-BB.md §3: 'W-ON-GLASS-FG: a muted-foreground register whose contrast target is the composited GLASS FILL (+ --input-on-glass) — M.W5: fourier's BAND-1 glass over the bright math canvas needs exactly this contrast register'. No fourier component uses --input-on-glass today (grep returns 0 hits).
findings.current_state: BAND 1 instrument panels (glass-wash/glass-resting over the bright math canvas) may exhibit muted-foreground legibility issues because --muted-foreground is calibrated against the page background, not against the composited glass fill. The W-ON-GLASS-FG primitive re-calibrates the muted register against the actual composited surface.
findings.proposed: Book to ADOPTION-ASKS.md §11 as 'glass-ui-on-glass-fg: W-ON-GLASS-FG --input-on-glass + muted-foreground-on-glass register — consume at M.W5 (BAND 1 over bright canvas)'. Consume when BB ships 4.1.0 by applying --muted-foreground: var(--muted-foreground-on-glass, --muted-foreground) on BAND 1 glass surfaces over the canvas. The kill-date is glass-ui BB 4.1.0.

glassui_asks.name: glass-ui-dockiconbutton-active
glassui_asks.what: A tonal-accent idle fill for the active/selected state of pill buttons and dock icon buttons — surface-tint-10 background + surface-tint-25 border at rest (not only on hover). The .glass-btn[aria-pressed='true'] rule (surfaces.css:111) ships this for glass-btn but not for the broader Button CVA variants used as preset pills (variant='outline').
glassui_asks.why: Fourier's equation preset pills (Sawtooth / Triangle / |sin(x)| / Gaussian / Step / x²) are invisible at rest — the active selected state must read without hover (critique 6). The tonal-accent idle fill is the missing register.

glassui_asks.name: glass-ui-overlay-tint-dark-arm
glassui_asks.what: A --glass-tint-strength-dark token arm (or a --glass-backdrop: dark context escape) that allows dark-substrate consumers to tune the overlay-band tint strength independently of the bright-substrate AA floor. The unconditional overlay-band self-darken (ladder.css:200) is correct for the unknown-substrate default but can compound on a dark page.
glassui_asks.why: Critique 5 (dropdown darkened): on fourier's near-black substrate the unconditional AA darken reads as a grey slab. A dark-arm token lets fourier set a lower strength on dark pages without a !important override.

glassui_asks.name: glass-ui-splitchars
glassui_asks.what: A <SplitChars> or useSplitChars composable that splits a string into per-character spans with stagger-entrance + PRM-gated char-by-char animation, consuming the keyframes.js Sequence primitive.
glassui_asks.why: M.W6 paper hero needs a single PRM-gated char-stagger entrance on the Fraunces display title. Without this primitive fourier would hand-roll per-character animation (the exact pattern M bans as a rAF-loop legacy).

glassui_asks.name: glass-ui-scroll-reveal-once
glassui_asks.what: A once-discipline flag or data attribute on [data-scroll-reveal] so the entry animation fires exactly once per session (not on every scroll-back into view). The current scroll-driven.css implementation re-fires on every viewport entry.
glassui_asks.why: M.W9/W10 scroll heroes need once-discipline (the paper section reveals should not replay on scroll-back). The once-discipline is a named M deliverable.

glassui_asks.name: glass-ui-canvas-anchored-overlay
glassui_asks.what: A CSS/composable recipe for a glass panel anchored to a canvas element's bounding box via CSS Anchor Positioning, so glass instrument panels track a moving canvas (the equation card popover, the ConvergenceLegend overlay) without bespoke JS position writes.
glassui_asks.why: EquationView.vue:252+261 hand-rolls a glass-floating coeff-popover with JS mousemove position tracking. M.W5 D1-09 notes the specular catch-light adoption; the anchoring pattern would replace the bespoke JS anchor.

open_questions: Is the dropdown darkening (D1-07) actually over-darkened on fourier's dark substrate at the live 18% AA tint strength, or is it sub-perceptual? Measure the composited luminance against WCAG contrast targets on the dark page before booking a glass-ui ask.

Does the .panel-inactive class in VisualizationView and EquationView use display:none (which already removes focus reachability) or opacity/visibility (which does not)? The inert adoption (D1-13) is urgent only if the former is not in use.

When glass-ui BB publishes 4.1.0 with W-LIQUIDHOVER: should fourier's M.W5 per-consumer useSpecularTracking wires be written as deletable stubs (with a TODO comment naming the BB kill-date) or should M.W5 defer ALL specular work until W1b? The answer affects M.W5's implementation sequencing.

The VisualizationView Configurator has three hand-rolled grid-template-columns overrides in scoped CSS that fight the Configurator's own layout. After adding asideSide='left', are those overrides dead or do they still govern the aside width? Clarify whether asideWidth prop or --configurator-aside-{min,max} cascade variables are the right aside-width mechanism at M.W8.

Should the GallerySearchBar search pill adopt .input-pill (a glass control surface with backdrop-filter) or remain a custom pill (the current color-mix muted background is intentionally less prominent)? The user critique targets the focus ring squareness, not necessarily the pill's glass level.

D2.dimension: D2 — glass-ui gaps abstracted into glass-ui (the alpha-class cross-repo asks)
D2.verdict: Three of the eight live critiques root-cause to glass-ui 4.0 (alpha-class) and must be booked as glass-ui:BB W-CROSSREPO-ASKS — NEVER a fourier `!important` mask (inv-16). The cardinal one is REAL and confirmed in source: the overlay band (`.glass-floating`/`.glass-overlay`, i.e. DropdownMenu + Select content) in `glass/ladder.css:200-204` UNCONDITIONALLY darkens toward warm-ink (`--glass-tint-strength-aa`) on the assumption it floats over an UNKNOWN surface — over fourier's near-white paper page this composites as the flat opaque-grey menu the user circled (critique #5, image 08). That self-engage is a calibration regression, not a fourier mis-adoption. The other two are genuine generalisation GAPS surfaced by the critique: glass-ui ships NO canonical glass focus-ring primitive (so fourier hand-rolled a raw `<input>` whose browser-default square ring leaked — critique #8, image 11) and NO selectable-chip/toggle-pill tonal register (so a preset picker must mis-pick the idle-less `outline` button variant — critique #6, image 09). findings.evidence: user-critique/08-dropdown-glass-darkened.png (the nav DropdownMenu renders flat opaque grey, no backdrop showing through); glass-ui ladder.css:200-204 `:where(.glass-floating, .glass-overlay){ --glass-tint-source: var(--glass-tint-ink); --glass-tint-strength: var(--glass-tint-strength-aa); --muted-foreground: var(--foreground); }` (UNCONDITIONAL self-engage); ladder.css:154-199 header comment confirms the intent ('floats over WHATEVER the consumer painted … darkening toward the warm-ink is the correct DEFAULT over an UNKNOWN surface'); tokens/glass.css:285 `--glass-tint-strength-aa` ≤24%; dark-arm.css:236 12% in dark.

(c) Expose `--glass-overlay-tint-strength` as a first-class retint knob so a light-paper consumer dials the overlay band toward the floor on ONE ancestor (today the only escape is `--glass-tint-strength: 0%` per surface, which kills the legibility lift entirely — a binary, not a calibration). fourier then sets ONE host token, no per-surface override. D3.verdict: The single highest-leverage finding of this charge is a genuine glass-ui-4.0 ALPHA regression that explains the user's critique #5 (darkened dropdown, image 08): the glass overlay band (.glass-floating/.glass-overlay — which DropdownMenuContent/SelectContent/PopoverContent/HoverCardContent all compose) self-engages the FULL unconditional 20% warm-ink AA darken (ladder.css:200-204; --glass-tint-strength-aa:20% at tokens/glass.css:304), on the documented rationale that it "floats over an UNKNOWN consumer surface." But fourier's surface is a KNOWN light cream --card, and 20% warm-ink over it composites to a flat oklab(~0.785) grey slab — the EXACT gray-slab failure the content-tier recalibration (BA.W-DARK-MATERIAL scope 7 / R9-1) already fixed for .glass-card/.glass-resting/.glass-quiet/.glass-wash by gating the full darken behind the @container style(--glass-backdrop:light) bright signal — and DELIBERATELY left on the overlay band. D4.dimension: D4 — PLATFORM-OVER-LIBRARY (inv-30): hand-rolled vs. glass-ui/platform/keyframes owned
D4.verdict: Seven concrete platform-over-library violations span the whole codebase. The most urgent are: (1) the `.cartoon-card` shim — a style.css `@utility` resurrecting a class glass-ui intentionally deleted at C.W5, squatting at 21 call-sites and responsible for the "not glassy / cartoon-stamp" live critique; (2) the `.eq-grid` / `.config-grid` hand-rolled control layouts replacing the shipped `Configurator asideSide="left"` prop (DEC-2, emphatic); (3) the hand-rolled glass CSS cluster (`AnimationControls.vue` `.play-btn`, `PaperSearch.vue` `.search-modal-overlay`, `PaperView.vue` `.overlay-btn`) that duplicates the 5-rung ladder fourier already imports; (4) the dual rAF clock (`stores/animation.ts` + `ConvergencePlot.vue` verbatim duplicate), the hover-scale lerp rAF in `useCanvasHover.ts`, and the curve-transition rAF in `useCurveTransition.ts` — all hand-rolling what keyframes.js 4.3 `Animation` owns; (5) the `PaperSearchInput` + `PaperSearchModal` hand-rolling what `glass-ui/search` `SearchBar` + `FuzzySearch` + `useFuzzySearch` ship natively; (6) the dual `spectrumColor` hand-roll (two independent HSL implementations, one per render domain) against `value.js 0.13 sampleColorRamp`; (7) the `tab-slide-in` global keyframe in `style.css` pending glass-ui tabs shipping it. All findings are M.W5/W8/W9 scope — classified beta (fourier adoption gap) or gamma (M.W1 bump residue), except the `.play-btn` hand-rolled glass which borders alpha (token parity gap in glass-ui 4.0).

findings.title: .cartoon-card shim — style.css @utility resurrecting a deleted class at 21 sites
findings.evidence: web/src/style.css:107-111 declares `@utility cartoon-card { @apply cartoon-surface; border-color: var(--border); background: var(--card); }`. The comment at line 98-106 is explicit: glass-ui removed `.cartoon-card` at C.W5; this shim is a 'fourier-local KISS stop-gap.' 21 vue call-sites confirmed (BasisCanvas.vue:521, EquationView.vue:230/239/243/251/308, FunctionInput.vue:93/175, EqCoefficientsPanel.vue:12, InfoCard.vue:18, ContourPreview.vue:33, ImageUpload.vue:38, GalleryView.vue:312, VisualizationView.vue:163, AdminUserList.vue:308/362, MorphShapePreview.vue:4, HarmonicLevelGrid.vue:2, MorphPhaseConfig.vue:2). Live critique user-critique/01 and live/live-workspace confirm these render as paper cartoon-stamp stickers, not glass. M.md §1 names this as 'the deepest chronic' (seven tranches carried since D.W4).
findings.current_state: The shim in style.css creates a fourier-local class that mimics the deleted `cartoon-surface` utility on top of opaque `--card` background. Every primary content panel (equation cards, config cards, canvas container, upload strip, gallery, morph) is an opaque stamp rather than a glass-ladder member. The per-tier backdrop-filter, glass-border-*, and glass-bg-* tokens never fire on these surfaces.
findings.proposed: Delete the `@utility cartoon-card` block from style.css entirely. Reclassify all 21 call-sites onto the correct glass-ladder tier: BAND 1 math substrate (bare canvas frame) receives no surface decoration; BAND 2 instrument panels (FunctionInput, EqCoefficientsPanel, BasisSelector layers, ContourSettings, ConfiguratorLayer bodies) adopt `glass-quiet` or `glass-resting` as appropriate to their depth; BAND 3 lifted/anchored chrome (EquationPanel overlay, GalleryView sticky footer, AdminUserList sticky header, modal error states) adopts `glass-floating`. Morph config cards (`MorphPhaseConfig`, `HarmonicLevelGrid`) adopt `glass-quiet` as in-flow instrument panels. Where a decorative stamp character is explicitly desired (MorphShapePreview toggle button) use `cartoon-surface` directly on top of its resolved glass-ladder rung — `cartoon-surface` is a decoration-only utility, NOT a replacement tier. This is M.W5 work.

findings.title: Dual rAF animation clock — stores/animation.ts + ConvergencePlot.vue verbatim duplicate; useCanvasHover + useCurveTransition additional rAF loops
findings.evidence: web/src/stores/animation.ts:51-75: `function startLoop() { let rafId: number | null = null; function tick(now: number) { ... rafId = requestAnimationFrame(tick); } rafId = requestAnimationFrame(tick); }` — a ping-pong rAF clock with `IntersectionObserver` gating. web/src/components/equation/ConvergencePlot.vue:57-70: `function startLoop() { ... function tick(now: number) { ... rafId = requestAnimationFrame(tick); } rafId = requestAnimationFrame(tick); }` — the same ping-pong clock, structurally verbatim. M.md §1 explicitly names this: 'two ping-pong rAF clocks duplicated verbatim.' Additionally: web/src/components/visualization/composables/useCanvasHover.ts:52-63 has a `updateHoverScale` lerp loop (`currentScale += diff * 0.12; hoverAnimFrame = requestAnimationFrame(updateHoverScale)`) and a `shimmerTick` loop (lines 71-79). web/src/components/equation/composables/useCurveTransition.ts:44-53 has a 500ms eased lerp loop. keyframes.js 4.3.0 is installed (package.json, confirmed in useFourierMorph.ts:14 `import { loadAnimationEngine, type Animation } from '@mkbabb/keyframes.js'`). M.md §3 completion criterion: 'zero requestAnimationFrame animation call-sites remain (layout-sync measure loops exempt + doc-marked).'
findings.current_state: Six distinct hand-rolled rAF constructs animate the application: (1) the ping-pong playhead in `stores/animation.ts`; (2) the verbatim duplicate in `ConvergencePlot.vue`; (3) the hover-scale lerp in `useCanvasHover.ts`; (4) the shimmer loop in `useCanvasHover.ts`; (5) the curve-transition lerp in `useCurveTransition.ts`; (6) the progress-bar fallback rAF in `PaperView.vue:171` (layout-sync measure, acceptable). The M.md motion architecture audit calls the animation store the 'MEMORY-flagged legacy' and names it for collapse into `useFourierPlayhead`.
findings.proposed: M.W9: author `useFourierPlayhead` as the ONE shared playhead clock, driven by a keyframes.js 4.3 `Animation` instance with the `ping-pong: true` cycle mode, replacing both the `stores/animation.ts` rAF loop and the `ConvergencePlot.vue` duplicate. The `stores/animation.ts` becomes a pure reactive STATE atom (t, playing, speed, easing, scrubbing refs) with no rAF of its own — the playhead composable drives it. The hover-scale lerp in `useCanvasHover.ts` migrates to a keyframes.js `Animation` with a short spring easing (the library's light-tier spring); the shimmer loop migrates similarly. The `useCurveTransition.ts` 500ms lerp adopts a keyframes.js one-shot `Animation` with `easeInOutSine`. The `PaperView.vue` progress-bar fallback rAF is layout-sync / scroll-event-driven and is exempt (doc-mark with `// layout-sync rAF — exempt per M.W9`). Net delta: six rAF constructs → zero animation rAFs; one keyframes.js engine instance shared.

findings.title: Dual spectrumColor HSL hand-roll — two independent HSL implementations against value.js sampleColorRamp
findings.evidence: web/src/components/visualization/lib/canvas-drawing/transforms.ts:3-8: `export function spectrumColor(i, total) { const t = i / Math.max(total-1,1); const curved = Math.pow(t, 0.6); const hue = (1 - curved) * 300; return 'hsl(' + hue + ', 85%, 55%)'; }` — sRGB HSL, power-curved. web/src/components/equation/lib/harmonics.ts:81-88: `export function spectrumColor(i, total, alpha=1) { const hue = (1 - i / Math.max(total-1,1)) * 300; return 'hsla(' + hue + ', 85%, 55%, ' + alpha + ')'; }` — sRGB HSL, linear (no power curve), supports alpha. Two independent implementations in two separate import trees (canvas epicycle renderer vs. equation convergence plot + legend). value.js 0.13.0 ships `sampleColorRamp` (confirmed in M-AMENDMENT-latest-and-BB.md: 'value.js 0.13.0 [sampleColorRamp SHIPPED]'). M.md §1: 'the icon-rainbow IS audacious but lives in one chart legend, while four duplicated HSL spectrumColor copies… hand-mix what value.js 0.12 generates perceptually from the favicon's own six stops.'
findings.current_state: Two separate `spectrumColor` functions produce non-identical ramps (one power-curved, one linear) from raw sRGB HSL. Neither is perceptually uniform (sRGB HSL hue ≠ OKLCH hue), and neither is keyed to the app's actual brand palette. The two implementations diverge visually between the epicycle canvas colours and the convergence-plot legend colours for the same harmonic index.
findings.proposed: M.W7: Delete both `spectrumColor` implementations. Define ONE `harmonicColorRamp` in a shared `lib/color.ts` using `value.js sampleColorRamp` over the same OKLCH stops derived from the favicon/icon-rainbow palette (`--route-accent` as the anchor). Export a `harmonicColor(i: number, total: number, alpha?: number): string` function that samples the ramp. Wire it into both the canvas epicycle renderer (`epicycles.ts:162`) and the convergence-plot (`ConvergencePlot.vue:207`, `ConvergenceLegend.vue:36`). The ramp generates perceptually uniform OKLCH colours rather than the sRGB HSL skew. This is the ONE colour source the M.md §1 colour story demands.

E1.dimension: E1 — Mathematical-animation opportunities (the signature motion as brand: epicycle traces, convergence sweeps, harmonic reveals, spectral build-up), grounded in the live M.W1 critique state.
E1.verdict: The M.W9 motion-architecture doc is strong and largely correct: the three-layer rule, the `useFourierPlayhead` collapse, the convergence-reveal signature (§4), and the PRM/INP/proportion floor (§6) are idiomatic and no-legacy. It needs HARDENING, not re-derivation, on ONE axis the live evidence exposes loudly: in every captured pane the signal surface is EMPTY/IDLE/ERROR (dead dot-grid in workspace, "No visualizations yet" in gallery, Bad Gateway in equation/morph) — so fourier's entire mathematical motion is bound to DATA-PRESENT states, and the brand signature is INVISIBLE at the exact moment of first encounter. The convergence-reveal (§4) fires only "the first time data arrives"; the placeholder (`placeholder.ts`) and the gallery/equation empty states are static. That is the single biggest E1 gap: the signature must also live in the ZERO-DATA states (an ambient epicycle/Lissajous breathing in the empty canvas, a converging-curve loading skeleton, a math-motion error/retry), each PRM-collapsing and INP-bounded. Secondary hardening: the §4 reveal lacks an explicit anti-replay latch keyed to the virtual-window remount (same hazard §5.2 names for scroll reveals but does NOT carry into §4's "first-paint" trigger); the morph's 10-thumbnail degradation strip (live-morph) is a static filmstrip that should be the literal harmonic-build-up reveal; the spectrum bars (CoefficientsSpectrum / FrequencyGraph) have no amplitude-rank rise build-up wired despite §4.1 naming it; and the trail's draw-on (§4 gesture 3) is named but the `TrailManager` precompute already holds the exact arc-length slice to make it free. None of this changes the architecture — it extends the SAME `useFourierPlayhead` + `Sequence` + `stagger` primitives to the states the live critique actually shows. The three critique items E1 touches (idle/no-paint surfaces #6, the dead workspace #3/#4, the inert chrome) are adoption gaps (beta), with the wall-clock-oscillator PRM hole partly a glass-ui motion-preset ask (alpha-adjacent: the convergence-reveal preset).

findings.title: The convergence-reveal (§4) has no anti-replay latch keyed to the virtual-window remount — the same flicker hazard §5.2 names for scroll reveals applies to the canvas first-paint trigger

This makes the shimmer a phase read, deletes the two divergent magic periods (200/300ms) by deriving both from one clock, and closes the PRM hole. E3.verdict: keyframes.js 4.3 is pinned and installed (web/package.json `^4.3.0`) but fourier uses ZERO of its light-tier primitives for animation. Every animation loop — the ping-pong epicycle clock (animation.ts), the convergence-plot ping-pong (ConvergencePlot.vue), the curve-transition lerp (useCurveTransition.ts), the hover-scale spring (useCanvasHover.ts), and the shimmer loop (useCanvasHover.ts) — is a hand-rolled rAF pattern that pre-dates keyframes 2.x. The one genuine keyframes usage (useFourierMorph.ts) reaches behind the `loadAnimationEngine()` HEAVY boundary to construct a CSS-keyframes `Animation` as a tween, when `NumericAnimation` (LIGHT, value.js-free, zero dynamic import) is the idiomatic primitive for exactly that use-case. The `loadAnimationEngine` boundary is used correctly in that one site but its architecture is now over-heavy for what fourier actually needs. M.W9 is the designated discharge wave; this audit maps every site, identifies the correct light-tier substitute, and flags two residual risks: (1) the `warmEngine()` call is absent — the HEAVY engine (needed only for useFourierMorph) cold-loads on first morph with no pre-warm; (2) the easing catalog in easings.ts duplicates value.js's `timingFunctions` registry by static import + manual aliasing instead of calling `resolveEasing` at the keyframes/value.js boundary.

findings.title: animation.ts: manual ping-pong rAF clock must become RAFPlayback.loop + SmoothProgress or Oscillator
findings.evidence: web/src/stores/animation.ts:32-80 — a hand-rolled `let rafId: number|null` + `startLoop()/stopLoop()/tick()` ping-pong that manages its own start-time, cycle arithmetic, and visibility gate. The comment at line 47 explicitly says 'Manual rAF loop' and acknowledges the former keyframes.js Animation was excised as dead substrate.
findings.current_state: A bare `requestAnimationFrame(tick)` loop in the Pinia store owns `rafId`, computes `cycle/frac` manually for ping-pong, and re-arms on `speed` watch. The MEMORY.md M.W9 contract names this as 'the MEMORY-flagged legacy DELETED'. The off-screen IntersectionObserver gate (visibleCanvases ref) is correct intent but is wired by hand instead of through a managed driver.
findings.proposed: Replace the entire `startLoop/stopLoop/tick/rafId` block with a single `RAFPlayback` instance (LIGHT, value.js-free, from `@mkbabb/keyframes.js`). The ping-pong `t` update (`cycle % 2 === 0 ? frac : 1 - frac`) moves verbatim into the `RAFPlayback.loop(cb)` callback; `RAFPlayback.stop()` replaces `stopRAF()`; `speed` watch calls `playback.stop(); playback.loop(...)`. The off-screen gate stays as a boolean guard inside the `loop` callback (`if (!playing.value || !anyCanvasVisible.value) return false`). `RAFPlayback` owns no rAF handle except through its public API — the generation guard it carries eliminates the stop+restart race (the `this._gen++` class) that the hand-rolled approach has no protection against. `stores/animation.ts` becomes a pure STATE atom: it holds `t`, `playing`, `speed`, `easing`, `scrubbing`, `visibleCanvases` as refs, and the `RAFPlayback` instance — no raw `requestAnimationFrame` call-site.

findings.title: ConvergencePlot.vue: duplicate ping-pong rAF clock is a verbatim copy of animation.ts — collapse to useFourierPlayhead
findings.evidence: web/src/components/equation/ConvergencePlot.vue:49-75 — `let rafId: number|null = null; let loopStartTime: number|null = null; function startLoop() { ... rafId = requestAnimationFrame(tick); } function stopLoop() { cancelAnimationFrame(rafId); }`. The cycle/frac arithmetic at lines 63-65 is byte-identical to animation.ts:63-69.
findings.current_state: Two independent ping-pong clocks: one in the Pinia store driving the epicycle canvas, one in ConvergencePlot driving the convergence animation. They are structurally identical (same `elapsed % dur / dur`, same `cycle % 2 === 0 ? frac : 1 - frac`). M.W9 describes 'ONE useFourierPlayhead for the epicycle canvas + ConvergencePlot (kills the duplicate clock + the off-screen loop)'. The ConvergencePlot also has no visibility gating — it runs at 60fps regardless of whether the equation pane is visible.
findings.proposed: Extract `useFourierPlayhead(options: { duration, speed, onTick, onFrame? })` — a thin composable that wraps ONE `RAFPlayback` instance with the ping-pong cycle math and the off-screen IntersectionObserver gate (shared implementation with animation.ts replacement). ConvergencePlot consumes `useFourierPlayhead` instead of its own `startLoop/stopLoop`. The epicycle canvas (BasisCanvas.vue) reads `t` from the animation store which itself now delegates to the same composable. One clock path, two consumers.

findings.title: useCurveTransition.ts: hand-rolled lerp rAF tween must retire to NumericAnimation (LIGHT)
findings.evidence: web/src/components/equation/composables/useCurveTransition.ts:36-53 — `let rafId: number|null = null; function tick(now) { elapsed = now - start; state.progress = easeInOutSine(Math.min(1, elapsed/DURATION)); onFrame(); if (state.progress < 1) rafId = requestAnimationFrame(tick); }`. Called from ConvergencePlot.vue:312-314 as `cancelTransition = startTransition(transition, draw)`.
findings.current_state: A standalone `startTransition` factory that creates a new rAF loop per transition, eases progress manually via value.js `easeInOutSine`, and returns a cancel closure. It has no reduced-motion awareness and no generation guard — if `startTransition` is called twice before the first completes, two rAF chains run in parallel (the cancel-before-restart pattern at line 312 catches the common case, but it is a discipline not a guarantee).
findings.proposed: Replace with `NumericAnimation<{ progress: number }>` (LIGHT static import, zero value.js edge, zero dynamic import): `new NumericAnimation([{progress:0},{progress:1}], { duration: 500, timingFunction: easeInOutSine, respectReducedMotion: true })`. Call `.at(t)` from the consumer's own render loop (the `draw()` call that ConvergencePlot already drives per frame) rather than `.play(onFrame)`, since ConvergencePlot already owns a rAF clock. This eliminates the second rAF loop entirely — the transition progress is read stateless from `NumericAnimation.at(t)` where `t` comes from `RAFPlayback`-driven elapsed time already computed in `useFourierPlayhead`. Delete `createTransitionState`, `startTransition`, `snapshotForTransition` — the snapshot data moves to local refs and `lerp` becomes a one-liner the caller computes inline.

findings.title: useCanvasHover.ts: hand-rolled lerp scale animation must become SpringProgress.drive
findings.evidence: web/src/components/visualization/composables/useCanvasHover.ts:52-63 — `function updateHoverScale() { const diff = targetScale - currentScale; if (Math.abs(diff) < 0.002) { currentScale = targetScale; hoverAnimFrame = null; onRedraw(); return; } currentScale += diff * 0.12; onRedraw(); hoverAnimFrame = requestAnimationFrame(updateHoverScale); }`. This is an exponential lerp manually implementing the same physics `SmoothProgress` provides.
findings.current_state: A `diff * 0.12` per-frame multiplier is a fixed-dt damped approach — identical to `SmoothProgress` with `damping: 0.12` but without frame-rate independence, reduced-motion awareness, or the settle detection that `SmoothProgress.settled` provides cleanly. The `hoverAnimFrame` guard re-arms correctly but diverges from `RAFPlayback.drive`'s idempotency contract (the `if (this._rafId !== null) return` guard that prevents double-arming).
findings.proposed: Replace `currentScale`, `targetScale`, `hoverAnimFrame`, and `updateHoverScale` with `new SpringProgress({ response: 0.25, dampingFraction: 0.85, initial: baseScale, respectReducedMotion: true })`. On mouse enter: `spring.setTarget(hoverScale); playback.drive(spring, () => onRedraw())`. On mouse leave: `spring.setTarget(baseScale); playback.drive(spring, () => onRedraw())`. Read `spring.current` where `getScale()` is called. `RAFPlayback.drive` is idempotent — re-arming on every `setTarget` call is safe. The `respectReducedMotion: true` option snaps the scale immediately under reduced-motion, which the hand-rolled version cannot do.

findings.title: useCanvasHover.ts: shimmer rAF loop is a second independent rAF chain — retire to RAFPlayback.loop
findings.evidence: web/src/components/visualization/composables/useCanvasHover.ts:66-80 — `let shimmerRafId: number|null = null; function startShimmer() { if (shimmerRafId) return; function shimmerTick() { if (!hoveredBasis) { shimmerRafId = null; return; } onRedraw(); shimmerRafId = requestAnimationFrame(shimmerTick); } shimmerRafId = requestAnimationFrame(shimmerTick); }`. A second independent rAF chain running alongside the scale-animation chain.
findings.current_state: Two concurrent rAF chains from `useCanvasHover`: one for scale, one for shimmer. Both call `onRedraw()`. When a basis is hovered, both fire on the same frame, causing two `drawFrame()` calls per rAF tick (the shimmer loop and the scale loop are not coalesced). There is no lifecycle guard — the shimmer loop can outlive its creator if `onUnmounted` fires between the `cancelAnimationFrame` call and the next scheduled tick.
findings.proposed: Collapse both chains into ONE `RAFPlayback` instance for the hover composable. Use `RAFPlayback.loop(cb)` where `cb`: (1) steps `spring.tickDt(dt)` for the scale physics, (2) calls `onRedraw()` once, and (3) returns `!spring.settled || !!hoveredBasis` as the continue condition. `startShimmer/stopShimmer` are deleted. The single loop handles both the scale animation and the shimmer redraw in one frame, coalescing the two `drawFrame` calls into one.

findings.title: useFourierMorph.ts: HEAVY Animation as a tween driver must transpose to NumericAnimation + Sequence (LIGHT)
findings.evidence: web/src/composables/useFourierMorph.ts:14 — `import { loadAnimationEngine, type Animation } from '@mkbabb/keyframes.js'`; lines 38-44: `let enginePromise: Promise<AnimationCtor>|null = null; function getAnimationCtor(): Promise<AnimationCtor> { enginePromise = loadAnimationEngine().then(e => e.Animation); }`. Lines 122-143: `createTweenAnimation` adds CSS keyframe strings (`'0%' { v: '0px' }`, `'100%' { v: '1px' }`) — the CSS parser is loaded purely to drive a `0→1` progress tween via a framecallback hack.
findings.current_state: The morph composable crosses the HEAVY dynamic boundary (`await loadAnimationEngine()`) to obtain a `CSSKeyframesAnimation` constructor and then uses it as a glorified `requestAnimationFrame` wrapper. It adds dummy CSS keyframes (`v: '0px' → '1px'`) and reads the engine's internal `time / duration` ratio as a tween driver. This is the heavy engine used as a light primitive — the 4.3 light tier contains the correct answer (`NumericAnimation`) without any dynamic import. The three morph phases (settle-out, morph, settle-in) are three sequential `await new Promise` blocks chaining `Animation.play()` — exactly the pattern `Sequence` is built for.
findings.proposed: Transpose to: `NumericAnimation<{t:number}>([{t:0},{t:1}], {duration, timingFunction: getEasingFn(easing)})` for each phase, called as `anim.play(({t}) => onTick(t))`. The three phases become entries in a `Sequence` (LIGHT): `seq.add(settleOutAnim); seq.add(morphAnim); seq.add(settleInAnim)`. `seq.play()` returns a Promise resolving when all three complete. `loadAnimationEngine()` is deleted from this file entirely — the HEAVY boundary is no longer crossed for morphs. `warmEngine()` (from the barrel, also LIGHT-adjacent) can be called at app boot to pre-warm if other heavy features need it, but morphing itself becomes zero-dynamic-import.

findings.title: easings.ts: manual value.js `timingFunctions` aliasing duplicates what resolveEasing provides — retire the registry copy
findings.evidence: web/src/lib/easings.ts:9-60 — `import { timingFunctions } from '@mkbabb/value.js'`; then `EASING_PRESETS = Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(EASING_LABELS).map(([name, label]) => [name, { label, fn: timingFunctions[name] as EasingFn }]))`. Also lines 10-16: static named imports of `easeInOutSine/Cubic/Quad/Expo/Circ` from value.js used in `ANIMATION_EASINGS` record.
findings.current_state: fourier statically imports the whole `timingFunctions` record from value.js and builds its own local registry (`EASING_PRESETS`) keyed by string name. The `ANIMATION_EASINGS` subset does the same with explicit named imports. `useFourierMorph.ts` then calls `getEasingFn(name)` (a string→function lookup from this registry) to get a `TimingFunction` for `NumericAnimation`. This is the pre-4.x pattern: before `resolveEasing` existed, consumers built their own string registries. The `resolveEasing(name): Promise<TimingFunction>` export on the keyframes barrel is the idiomatic 4.x successor — it resolves through the value.js registry via the dynamic boundary, returning the callable.
findings.proposed: The `EASING_PRESETS` registry and the static named easing imports from value.js are retired. The async `resolveEasing(name)` is called once at morph-phase construction (each phase already awaits before its `NumericAnimation` runs). The `ANIMATION_EASINGS` subset (the in-UI preset labels for the EasingPicker) retains its label/description metadata but loses the `.fn` field — the picker stores an easing NAME string in the store; the runtime resolves it lazily via `resolveEasing` at play-time. The `getEasingFn` function is deleted. The `generateCurveSVGPath` and `easingCurvePath` utilities that sample easing functions for SVG previews call `resolveEasing` once per name (cached in the existing `_svgCache`) at preview-render time.

findings.title: No warmEngine() call at app boot — morph HEAVY engine cold-loads on first user gesture
findings.evidence: web/src/main.ts (no warmEngine call present); web/src/composables/useFourierMorph.ts:38-44 — the `enginePromise` is lazily constructed on the first `morphTo()` call. The CHANGELOG 4.3.0 Band I notes 'the cold hero rainbow-play now STARTS the engine on the first gesture' as a P0 fix in the keyframes demo — the same latency class affects fourier's morph pane.
findings.current_state: The first morph the user triggers incurs the full `loadAnimationEngine()` dynamic import latency (parsing + evaluating the heavy engine chunk + value.js). On a slow connection or cold cache this is a visible delay between gesture and animation start. `warmEngine()` is exported from the keyframes barrel as a LIGHT-callable fire-and-forget — it initiates the dynamic import during idle time without blocking anything.
findings.proposed: Add `import { warmEngine } from '@mkbabb/keyframes.js'` to `web/src/main.ts` and call `warmEngine()` after `app.mount()`. This fires the dynamic import during browser idle after the first paint, so the morph pane's first animation finds the engine already cached. No API changes to useFourierMorph. Per the 4.3 changelog, `warmEngine()` is the ONE correct pre-warm surface — it is a no-op if the engine is already loaded.

findings.title: loadAnimationEngine boundary: useFourierMorph comment cites 'keyframes 2.2.0' — stale doc-drift post 4.3 bump
findings.evidence: web/src/composables/useFourierMorph.ts:33-35 — the comment reads 'keyframes 2.2.0 moves the value.js-bearing `Animation` engine behind the `loadAnimationEngine()` dynamic boundary'. The file is pinned at `^4.3.0` (package.json); the comment's version reference is two majors stale and the architecture comment is now moot because the E3-06 transposition to NumericAnimation eliminates the `loadAnimationEngine` call entirely.
findings.current_state: A version-reference comment that was correct at 2.x, mechanically outdated at 4.3, and will be vacated by the E3-06 NumericAnimation transposition. The `enginePromise` machinery it explains will not exist post-M.W9. Per inv-32 (version-currency doc-rot), stale version references in code comments are tracked as chronic.
findings.proposed: After the E3-06 NumericAnimation transposition lands, delete the entire `enginePromise`/`getAnimationCtor` block and the comment that documents it. If any heavy engine usage remains (e.g. for future compile-to-CSS work), the comment should cite '4.3.0' and reference `docs/tranches/M/M.md §W9` rather than the 2.x changelog.

findings.title: ConvergencePlot per-frame resize (canvas width/height reassigned every draw tick) is a chronic not yet addressed in M.W9 plan
findings.evidence: web/src/components/equation/ConvergencePlot.vue:87-96 — inside `draw()`, on every rAF tick: `canvas.width = Math.round(rect.width * dpr); canvas.height = Math.round(rect.height * dpr); canvas.style.width = ...; canvas.style.height = ...`. This forces a layout read (`getBoundingClientRect`) and a canvas resize (which clears the canvas and forces a compositor flush) on EVERY FRAME, even when the container has not changed size.
findings.current_state: The ConvergencePlot canvas reads its container's bounding rect and resets canvas dimensions on every `draw()` call regardless of whether the size changed. This is the exact anti-pattern the M.W9 plan names: 'fix the ConvergencePlot per-frame resize'. A `ResizeObserver` is already mounted (line 325) but its callback only calls `draw()` — the resize detection logic is not used to GATE the canvas resize inside `draw()`.
findings.proposed: Cache the last-set `{width, height}` as module-scope variables. Inside `draw()`, only reassign `canvas.width/height` when `Math.round(rect.width*dpr) !== cachedWidth || Math.round(rect.height*dpr) !== cachedHeight`. The `ResizeObserver` callback updates the cache and triggers a redraw. On each rAF tick, `getBoundingClientRect()` is replaced with reading the cached dimensions — zero layout thrash per frame. This is a one-function fix that eliminates the forced layout read from the 60fps hot path.

findings.title: PaperView.vue: scroll progress rAF is a layout-sync measure loop — exempt from retirement per M.W9, but needs doc-mark
findings.evidence: web/src/components/paper/PaperView.vue:160-187 — `let progressRaf = 0; function writeProgress() { ... bar.style.transform = 'scaleX('+p+')'; } function onProgressScroll() { if (progressRaf) return; progressRaf = requestAnimationFrame(writeProgress); }`.
findings.current_state: This is a scroll-throttled layout measurement loop, NOT an animation loop — it batches scroll events behind a single rAF to avoid layout thrash. It is already gated by the CSS-native `NATIVE_SCROLL_TIMELINE` flag (the native path is preferred; this is the JS fallback). The M.W9 plan correctly notes 'layout-sync measure loops exempt + doc-marked'. The comment `// I.γ` style doc-mark is present elsewhere but missing on this rAF usage.
findings.proposed: Add a comment `// layout-sync measure: exempt from the M.W9 rAF retirement (PRM-gated JS fallback for scroll-timeline progress)` at the `progressRaf = requestAnimationFrame(writeProgress)` line. No code change. This prevents a future auditor from flagging it as a missing M.W9 retirement and documents the exemption criterion: it is a measure-then-write single-shot throttle, not an animation loop.

findings.title: useScrollNavigation.ts: multiple raw rAF calls for layout-correction are measure loops — need doc-marks, not retirement
findings.evidence: web/src/components/paper/useScrollNavigation.ts:89, 106, 125, 138, 159, 163, 187 — seven `requestAnimationFrame` calls, all in layout-correction contexts (measuring element positions after scroll/hash navigation, correcting for sticky headers, waiting for DOM mutations). None drive animation values.
findings.current_state: Seven rAF calls serving as DOM-measurement synchronization (the double-rAF pattern for layout settle at line 174 in router/index.ts is the same class). These are all layout-sync measure loops, not animation loops — they schedule a layout read after the browser has painted, not to animate a value. The M.W9 'zero requestAnimationFrame animation call-sites' mandate explicitly exempts 'layout-sync measure loops' — but none of these are doc-marked as exempt.
findings.proposed: Add `// layout-sync measure: exempt from M.W9 rAF retirement` comments at each of the seven call sites. No code changes required. This is the same doc-mark discipline as E3-11 — making the exemption class explicit so the M.W12 cohort-hygiene sweep can verify the mandate is met without false positives.

findings.title: Oscillator primitive unadopted: the convergence-plot animation is a natural Oscillator consumer for its phase clock
findings.evidence: web/src/components/equation/ConvergencePlot.vue:34-41 — `const animDuration = computed(() => { const n = trigHarmonics.value.length; return Math.max(2_000, Math.min(12_000, 3_000 + Math.max(0, n-3)*200)); })`. The ping-pong `t` drives a periodic phase that maps harmonics along a timeline. The keyframes.js 4.3 `Oscillator` (LIGHT, value.js-free) is a 'frequency-driven phase ramp ∈ [0,1) with a pure waveform shaper' — exactly the mathematical primitive for a Fourier-plot clock.
findings.current_state: The convergence animation uses a manual ping-pong `t` rather than an `Oscillator` phase. The `Oscillator` with `waveform: 'triangle'` produces exactly the ping-pong `0→1→0` ramp that the `cycle % 2 === 0 ? frac : 1-frac` arithmetic computes. The `frequency` would be `1 / animDuration.value` (cycles per ms). The Oscillator's `tick(dt)` + `waveformValue(phase, 'triangle')` replaces the entire cycle/frac arithmetic.
findings.proposed: In `useFourierPlayhead`, the ping-pong `t` becomes `Oscillator({ frequency: 1/duration, waveform: 'triangle' })`. Each frame: `osc.tick(dt/1000)` (dt in ms from `RAFPlayback`), then `t = (waveformValue(osc.phase, 'triangle') + 1) / 2` to remap the `[-1,1]` triangle output to `[0,1]`. This is the on-brand choice: the Fourier demo's convergence clock IS an oscillator — a periodic phase over harmonics. The `animDuration` computation stays as `1/frequency`. The Oscillator is a named LIGHT primitive; its name makes the domain relationship explicit in code.

findings.title: reducedMotionScale / ReducedMotionPolicy unadopted: fourier's three PRM checks are three separate matchMedia reads
findings.evidence: web/src/components/paper/PaperView.vue:174 — `const prm = typeof window !== 'undefined' && window.matchMedia?.('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches;`. useFourierMorph has no PRM check. ConvergencePlot.vue has no PRM check. useCanvasHover has no PRM check. M.W9 plan states 'close the 3 PRM gaps'.
findings.current_state: PaperView constructs a new `matchMedia` call per mount (not the engine's shared singleton). The animation store, ConvergencePlot, and canvas hover have no PRM awareness — under reduced motion they all run at full amplitude. `reducedMotionScale` and `withReducedMotion` (exported from keyframes LIGHT barrel) are the canonical engine-wide gate that `SpringProgress`/`SmoothProgress`/`NumericAnimation` all consult when `respectReducedMotion` is set. None of fourier's consumers set this flag.
findings.proposed: Each adopted primitive gets `respectReducedMotion: true`: `NumericAnimation` for useCurveTransition (E3-03), `SpringProgress` for useCanvasHover (E3-04), `NumericAnimation` for useFourierMorph phases (E3-06). `RAFPlayback.play()` in useFourierPlayhead gets `{ respectReducedMotion: true }`. PaperView replaces `window.matchMedia(...)` with `import { prefersReducedMotion } from '@mkbabb/keyframes.js'` — the engine's shared singleton, not a per-call construction. This closes all 3 PRM gaps through the one engine-wide gate, satisfying M.W9.

findings.title: useKfAnimation (keyframes-vue) unadopted: ConvergencePlot and BasisCanvas bridge animation state to Vue reactivity by hand
findings.evidence: web/src/components/equation/ConvergencePlot.vue:28-30 — `const t = ref(0); const playing = ref(false);` manually updated inside the rAF tick. BasisCanvas.vue reads `anim.t` directly from the Pinia store (the store IS Vue-reactive, so this is acceptable). The keyframes-vue package (`@mkbabb/keyframes-vue`) ships `useKfAnimation` — the 'settle-and-pause kernel' that bridges a kf Animation's rAF-mutated state to reactive refs.
findings.current_state: ConvergencePlot manually maintains `t` and `playing` as reactive refs updated from the rAF tick — the exact problem `useKfAnimation` solves ('the engine objects are deliberately un-proxied — Vue cannot track an rAF-driven mutation'). However, after the E3-02 useFourierPlayhead extraction, the `t` reactive ref in ConvergencePlot is replaced by a prop/emit from the shared playhead — so `useKfAnimation` is not the right fit for the ping-pong clock (it bridges Animation objects, not RAFPlayback). `useKfAnimation` IS the right fit if useFourierMorph's `Animation` usage is retained, but E3-06 retires it.
findings.proposed: After E3-02 and E3-06 land, `useKfAnimation` has no natural consumer in fourier (the one `Animation` usage is retired to `NumericAnimation`; the ping-pong clock is a `RAFPlayback.loop` not a kf `Animation`). Book this as a FUTURE candidate if the HEAVY engine is ever adopted for scroll-scene or compile-to-CSS work. Do NOT add `@mkbabb/keyframes-vue` as a dep now — it has no concrete consumer post-M.W9.

open_questions: After the E3-06 NumericAnimation transposition, does useFourierMorph ever need the HEAVY engine for any remaining feature? If scroll-scene or compile-to-CSS is adopted in a future tranche, warmEngine() at boot (E3-08) and the dynamic boundary are still correct architecture — the question is whether the morph pane itself has any unresolved heavy requirement.

The E3-13 Oscillator proposal replaces the manual ping-pong arithmetic. However, the Oscillator's `tick(dt)` takes dt in SECONDS while RAFPlayback provides `now` timestamps (ms). The useFourierPlayhead implementation must convert: `dt_seconds = (now - lastNow) / 1000`. Is the sub-millisecond precision of `RAFPlayback`'s dt clock (which uses `now - this._lastFrameT` in ms) sufficient for an Oscillator running at frequencies as low as 1/12000 Hz (12-second period)?

The Sequence primitive (E3-06 proposal) drives child Animation objects via `advanceTo`. After the NumericAnimation transposition, `Sequence` would orchestrate three `NumericAnimation` instances. The Sequence API takes `Animation` (the heavy engine type) as its entry type — does Sequence accept `NumericAnimation` directly, or does it require the heavy `CSSKeyframesAnimation`? This needs source verification before the M.W9 implementation; if Sequence requires heavy Animation, the three-phase morph uses three sequential `NumericAnimation.play()` Promises instead (chained directly, no Sequence).

E4.dimension: E4 — value.js 0.13 leverage: colour + motion (sampleColorRamp, safeAccentColor, mixColorsN, OKLCH ramp, harmonic colour sweeps, palette transitions)
E4.verdict: value.js 0.13.0 ships `sampleColorRamp` (`mix.ts:83`, exported `index.ts:158`), dissolving the M.md §11 risk-6 interim. The M.W7 plan is now fully unblocked — it may adopt `sampleColorRamp` directly, retiring the `mixColorsN`-equal-weight interim and its kill-date. Five concrete colour + motion leverage opportunities harden the plan: (C7) the four `spectrumColor` HSL copies collapse to one `sampleColorRamp`-backed `harmonicColor`; the `STATIC.rainbow` twin and the 118-line bespoke parser are deleted; per-route `--route-accent` is contrast-floored by `safeAccentColor` systematically rather than the ad-hoc D.W4 amber patch; harmonic colour sweeps on the canvas become a gamut-mapped OKLCH animation rather than sRGB drift; and palette transitions (morph stroke, convergence legend) receive a proper perceptual arc. No alpha glassui asks are introduced here — all five findings are fourier-local beta/gamma adoption work that M.W7 owns. The `mixColorsN` kill-date entry in M.md §11 must be struck and replaced with the confirmed `sampleColorRamp` adoption.

findings.title: sampleColorRamp ships at 0.13 — retire the mixColorsN interim and its kill-date
findings.evidence: M.md §11 risk-6 books `sampleColorRamp` with 'kill-date = the 0.13.0 publish'; value.js/src/units/color/mix.ts:83–184 confirms `sampleColorRamp` shipped and is exported at index.ts:158. The amendment (M-AMENDMENT-latest-and-BB.md §4) correctly dissolves the risk but does NOT update the M.W7 design-language prose or the PROGRESS.md wave ledger to confirm the direct adoption.
findings.current_state: M.W7 is described as using `mixColorsN` equal-weight as an interim ramp-generator. The real API — `sampleColorRamp(from, to, n, { space: 'oklch', hueMethod: 'longer' })` — is now live in the installed 0.13.0 dep and is the semantically correct primitive (it bakes the hue-arc sampling that bare two-stop @keyframes cannot encode, per mix.ts:97). The `mixColorsN` path overpays: it pairwise-folds N pre-supplied colors rather than interpolating from→to with the cylindrical hue path.
